### Closeout review — 2026-10-26

**Status: Implementation recorded; qualification pending.**

Work needed before closure:

- [ ] Keep the MCP adapter thin: trust the core build's SQLite result for a normal build. If restored artifacts require a separate SQLite rebuild, handle only that branch through the shared core operation with explicit requested mode and the restored artifact generation/root. Preserve cancellation and progress forwarding. Do not solve this by disabling core SQLite, because core owns validation/promotion and selected-build identity.
- [ ] Normal MCP build_index invokes one SQLite pipeline through core, not a second adapter-owned pass.
- [ ] code/prose/extracted-prose/records selections never expand to all in the adapter.
- [ ] Artifact-restore branch rebuilds only its intended modes/root when needed.
- [ ] Include follow-up acceptance: tools/setup/bootstrap.js:303-316 runs the normal index build, then invokes --stage4 again when --with-sqlite is selected.
- [ ] Include follow-up acceptance: core normal flow runs stage2 with allowSqlite:true; pipeline SQLite policy already builds selected modes when sqlite.use is not false. The CLI delegates to this core owner.
- [ ] Pass the related existing checks and the complete original/follow-up acceptance on the resulting candidate; preserve positive and negative controls.

Current source owners: [`tools/mcp/tools/handlers/indexing.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/accf98f64a560a5df9b1bdb175f7ca22331672af/tools/mcp/tools/handlers/indexing.js), [`src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/accf98f64a560a5df9b1bdb175f7ca22331672af/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js), [`src/storage/sqlite/build/runner/options.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/accf98f64a560a5df9b1bdb175f7ca22331672af/src/storage/sqlite/build/runner/options.js).

Related checks (starting points; not execution evidence): `services/mcp/index-build-cancellation`, `services/mcp/search-build-identity-observability`, `services/mcp/tool-build-index-progress`.

Keep this issue open until its original requirements and follow-up acceptance are demonstrated on the resulting candidate.

[Issue assessment and evidence](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f8532f1d2e54597feecf017e3a60d9ae3258762c/docs/archived/github-issue-closeout-2026-10-26.json#L451) · [Audit overview](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f8532f1d2e54597feecf017e3a60d9ae3258762c/docs/archived/github-issue-closeout-2026-10-26.md).
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Finding
The MCP build_index handler passes sqlite:true into coreBuildIndex and then unconditionally calls coreBuildSqliteIndex again. The core build already performs stage4 SQLite work. The second adapter-owned call omits mode and indexRoot, so a requested code-only build is followed by an all-mode SQLite pass against newly resolved active roots rather than the generation selected by the core operation. Default incremental:false makes this redundant storage work a full rebuild; failures in the redundant pass can turn a successfully completed core build into a failed MCP call.

Verified at PR #572 head 9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d. This is a concrete duplicated-orchestration and argument-drift seam, not a request to add another parallel build abstraction.

## Pinned source
- [MCP core build followed by extra SQLite invocation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/mcp/tools/handlers/indexing.js#L60-L84).
- [Core resolves requested SQLite modes and configured enablement](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js#L170-L177), then [runs stage4 with the stage2 build root](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js#L308-L327).
- [Missing SQLite mode normalizes to all](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/storage/sqlite/build/runner/options.js#L16-L27).

## Bounded evidence
An extracted exact handler fixture with stubbed core boundaries calls buildIndex({repoPath:'/fixture',mode:'code'}), with SQLite enabled and the stub core reporting successful stage4. Captured calls:
1. coreBuildIndex with mode:'code', sqlite:true, incremental:false.
2. coreBuildSqliteIndex with incremental:false, no mode, and no indexRoot.

This demonstrates adapter orchestration and option forwarding only; source tracing establishes the real core stage4 call. Node24.19.0 mechanism check, not native SQLite or supported Node26 integration qualification. No actual index/storage work ran.

## Repair direction
Keep the MCP adapter thin: trust the core build's SQLite result for a normal build. If restored artifacts require a separate SQLite rebuild, handle only that branch through the shared core operation with explicit requested mode and the restored artifact generation/root. Preserve cancellation and progress forwarding. Do not solve this by disabling core SQLite, because core owns validation/promotion and selected-build identity.

## Acceptance criteria
- Normal MCP build_index invokes one SQLite pipeline through core, not a second adapter-owned pass.
- code/prose/extracted-prose/records selections never expand to all in the adapter.
- Artifact-restore branch rebuilds only its intended modes/root when needed.
- Core stage4 errors propagate, but no post-success duplicate pass can cause a false failure.
- Test with injected core calls and one small SQLite integration fixture; preserve sqlite:false behavior.

followupRequirements.body:
## Independent remediation review: retain two-stage result semantics

The normal synchronous duplicate-build finding is supported. One acceptance qualification is important before implementing the thin adapter repair: a resolved `coreBuildIndex` call does not always mean SQLite has completed.

At the pinned `9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d` head, [core index.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js#L337-L420) returns `{stage2:{queued:true,...}}` or `{stage2:{background:true}}` for configured two-stage background work. Synchronous two-stage work instead delegates to `runStage('stage2', ..., {allowSqlite:true})`, whose [selected-root SQLite owner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/stages.js#L897-L941) performs SQLite within that stage rather than the separate `stage4` return shape.

Keep core as the owner in all these branches; do not replace the duplicate call with a test that assumes only `result.stage4` can establish ownership, and do not start an adapter-side rebuild against active roots while core has only queued enrichment. Preserve/distinguish completed versus queued/background outcomes in progress and result reporting rather than unconditionally claiming storage completion. Add two-stage synchronous and queued/background cases to the injected-core acceptance matrix, alongside ordinary, restored-artifact, and `sqlite:false` cases.

This is a source/control-flow clarification, not an executed queue/native SQLite test or a separate broad orchestration redesign.

Performance-audit follow-through: the same duplicate adapter-owned SQLite stage occurs in two additional orchestration callers at the audited head; please include them in this owner rather than repeat the fix only in MCP.

- [tools/ci/build-artifacts.js:73-106](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/ci/build-artifacts.js#L73-L106) runs a normal build_index.js, then invokes --stage4 again whenever --skip-sqlite is absent.
- [tools/setup/bootstrap.js:303-316](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/setup/bootstrap.js#L303-L316) runs the normal index build, then invokes --stage4 again when --with-sqlite is selected.
- [core normal flow](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js#L412) runs stage2 with allowSqlite:true; [pipeline SQLite policy](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/integrations/core/build-index/stages.js#L897-L944) already builds selected modes when sqlite.use is not false. The CLI delegates to this core owner.

Thus, when the first normal build already performed SQLite, these wrappers add a redundant storage rebuild and associated startup. This is a source-traced conditional duplicate, not a measured universal speedup; no SQLite build ran in the audit. Preserve the separate SQLite step when the normal build was skipped/restored or actually did not produce the requested SQLite state. Do not just remove all stage4 branches, disable core validation/promotion, or treat an existing DB path as current-generation proof.

Extend acceptance to recording subprocess/core fixtures for normal, skip-build/skip-index, restored-artifact, SQLite-config-disabled and explicit SQLite-request cases. A normal build should have one authoritative selected-generation SQLite pipeline; separate-stage cases must use an explicit qualified generation/root and retain failure propagation. Verify --skip-sqlite semantics against the intended command contract since the current wrapper does not forward a disabling flag into its initial full build. Coordinate artifacts packaging/readiness with the same core result rather than a second independently resolved build.

### Qualification audit — PR #572 at `74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295`

**Source credit:** Normal MCP builds no longer run the adapter-owned second SQLite pass; the remaining explicit call is guarded by restoredArtifacts and forwards requested mode.

**Still needed before closure:** The accepted bootstrap follow-through is still concrete: tools/setup/bootstrap.js runs a normal build and then a separate stage4 when with-sqlite is true. Reconcile ownership so normal setup does not duplicate core work, and qualify normal/restore code/prose/extracted-prose/records roots, sqlite:false, cancellation/progress and core error propagation with injected calls plus the requested tiny SQLite integration.

Reviewed owners: [`tools/mcp/tools/handlers/indexing.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295/tools/mcp/tools/handlers/indexing.js), [`tools/setup/bootstrap.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295/tools/setup/bootstrap.js), [`src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js).

Next focused qualification: `node tests/run.js --lane all --match 'services/mcp/tool-build-index-progress' --jobs 1 --timeout-ms 30000 --retries 0`; retain `services/mcp/index-build-cancellation` controls. Run only after the repository's supported Node26 bootstrap is verified. This pass inspected the issue, follow-ups, source and retained evidence; it did not execute that command. The shared cloud attempt obtained official Node26.12.1, but locked `npm run bootstrap:ci` was killed during installation (exit137, including a memory-bounded retry), before patches/native/readiness. That setup block is not a product-test failure or permission to bypass readiness.

**Follow-up acceptance retained:** include `tools/ci/build-artifacts.js` as well as bootstrap: it still runs a normal build and separate Stage4 unless skipped. Recording fixtures must cover normal/skip-build/skip-index/restore/config-disabled/explicit-SQLite and `--skip-sqlite` forwarding, with one selected-generation authority. Also distinguish synchronous two-stage completion from queued/background core results; a resolved `coreBuildIndex` or missing `result.stage4` is not proof SQLite finished or permission for an adapter rebuild.

---

## Defect
At PR #572 head `9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d`, throughput reporting advertises --latest and --repo filters but does not apply them to the aggregation input:
- latestCount is referenced only in option destructuring, output filter metadata and baseline-child argv. No run selection uses it, so --latest 1 still aggregates every historical JSON.
- repoFilter is applied only inside buildRepoRows, after every run has already contributed to global/folder totals, distributions, outcomes, provenance and regressions. Overview, family, comparison and JSON exports therefore retain unrelated repositories despite reporting the requested filter in metadata.
- --mode is described as restricting focused views, but only buildRepoRows selects the mode; family/comparison use hard-coded code metrics. pickModeDistribution exists but has no caller.

These are actual option-wiring/selection omissions, not a request for a new filtering feature. A report labeled filters.latest=1 or filters.repo="target" can describe a different population than the caller requested.

## Pinned evidence
- [Option meanings](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/reports/show-throughput/options.js#L63-L83)
- [Every folder JSON is admitted and summarized](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L597-L741)
- [Chronological sort happens only after aggregation, with no latest slice](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L759-L780)
- [Metadata claims filters](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1521-L1534)
- [Family hardcodes code; repo filtering occurs only in final rows](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1594-L1637)

A complete identifier-use audit of latestCount, repoFilter and modeFilter establishes the missing selection step. This is source/control-flow proof, not a full CLI reproduction.

## Narrow repair
Create a shared admitted-run selection step before aggregate mutation: resolve identity/timestamp, apply repository restriction and documented chronological latest-N-per-folder policy, then aggregate selected runs. Preserve stable timestamp ties and explicitly handle missing timestamps. Apply selected mode consistently to focused family/repo/comparison data, or reject/document unsupported combinations rather than silently ignoring the option. Keep any historical runs intentionally used solely for regression baselines distinct from the displayed/aggregated population.

Delay avoidable feature-metric/deep-analysis loading until after cheap admission where possible; no performance multiplier is claimed.

## Acceptance
Use two repos, multiple out-of-filename-order timestamps and deliberately different metrics. Verify --latest 1, --repo, --mode and combinations against expected run count, totals, distributions, outcomes/provenance and focused rows across text/JSON/CSV. Verify missing/equal dates deterministically, no implicit file mutation, and selected filters match metadata. No full benchmark needed.

## Deduplication / limits
All-state throughput/filter/latest searches and historical #278/#279 reviewed. Distinct from #764, which makes comparison export actually compute a baseline; this issue owns the run population and mode before aggregation, including non-comparison profiles. Live head verified. No project CLI/bootstrap/native execution, source edits or supported Node26 suite acceptance claim.

followupRequirements.body:
## Current-head credit and narrow mode-projection residual

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the original late/missing run admission is repaired in inspected source: [show-throughput.js:599–608](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L599-L608) selects before aggregation and expensive per-run reconstruction, using [selection.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/selection.js#L1-L16) for repo filtering, chronological latest-N, missing-date order and filename ties. [The small selection test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/reports/throughput-selection-and-order.test.js#L1-L13) now covers those cases. Focused family/compare chunk and file metrics also call the selected-mode picker. Preserve these repairs.

One current selected-mode projection remains contradictory: [folder JSON:1554–1568](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1554-L1568) emits `selectedMode` and selected-mode `chunksMedian` but still takes `variability` from **code**. [buildFamilyRows:1576–1592](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1576-L1592) similarly takes chunk/file rates from the requested mode, then code variability; [getSortValue:538–541](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L538-L541) sorts on that field. A prose-focused family table can therefore show prose throughput with code CV and rank --sort variability by the wrong population. For two folders with stable code/noisy prose versus noisy code/stable prose, the source selects the opposite variability ordering from the requested prose metric. No run was executed for this counterexample.

The focused line-rate field is also `aggregateLinesPerSec`, summed across all modes at [782–794](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L782-L794). Either explicitly label it all-modes or select the requested mode's numerator/denominator; do not imply all focused cells share a mode scope when they do not. Global/raw overview aggregates can intentionally remain all-mode, and build duration may intentionally cover the whole build: express metric scope rather than forcing unrelated metrics into a mode.

Finish one shared focused-metric projection carrying mode/scope for rates, CV and sorting, then feed text/JSON/CSV. Extend the existing tiny profiles fixture with opposing code/prose variability, extracted-prose key normalization, per-mode line counts and stable ties. Assert the same selected values/order across formats, while preserving the repaired run-admission counts. #279 owns the JSON-safe/profile-result export envelope; this owner retains which population/mode each selected metric describes. Source-only audit, no implementation or suite execution.

### Same focused-projection owner: compare sort keys are not projected
[buildComparison:1677–1696](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1677-L1696) creates rows with currentChunks/currentBuild, then sends them to the generic sortRows. [getSortValue:523–546](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L523-L546) instead looks for chunksMedian/chunkMedian/codeDistribution and buildIndexMedian. Thus --profile compare --sort chunks or --sort build compares default zeros and falls back to names, not the requested numeric column; unsupported query/files/lines/variability fields likewise silently fall through to empty values. Define each profile's supported sort columns and explicit getter over that profile's DTO. Reject unavailable columns or provide documented scope rather than silently sorting labels. Add two alphabetically opposed comparison rows with different current numeric values and --top 1, asserting the intended row in text/JSON/CSV. This is separate from #776's repaired regression comparator.

### Qualification audit — 2026-10-29

Reviewed the original issue and complete live follow-ups against PR #572 `74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295`, with main `3a4945decc4adc2975f477e96463b42ea5b7a9ea` as the separate baseline.

**Implemented / current evidence:** Repository/latest admission is performed before reconstruction/aggregation, and selected-mode projection has dedicated source paths. The small selection fixture proves chronological ordering and missing-date placement.

It therefore always sees 0 and can misclassify proc-queue waiting as slow file processing. The existing `file-watchdog-hard-timeout.test.js` also asserts both omitted fields ([lines 114-121](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/tests/indexing/stage1/file-watchdog-hard-timeout.test.js#L114-L121)).

Actual JSON is `{"queueDelayMs":1000,"activeDurationMs":1300,"writeDurationMs":0,"totalDurationMs":2300}`; both expected SCM/effective fields are absent. Consequently the Stage1 caller substitutes 0, treating 1300 ms as effective work instead of 650 ms.

## Finding
`appendChargramsToSet` adds a hash *before* checking whether the shared set has already reached `maxPerChunk` ([postings-helpers.js lines 266-281](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/index/build/state/postings-helpers.js#L266-L281)). Consequently each later nonempty field can add an extra unique chargram past the configured per-chunk limit.

## Direct reproduction
```js
const s = new Set();
appendChargramsToSet('abc', 2, 2, s, 2); // size 2
appendChargramsToSet('xyz', 2, 2, s, 2); // size 3, expected <=2
```
The first call produced two hashes; the second added a third before returning false from its rolling-hash callback.

## Finding
`assembleIndexPieces` compares input `compatibilityKey`s but never checks each input index state's `mode` against the requested output `mode`. The compatibility key is generated from the *set* of build modes, so a code and prose index from one multimode build can share it (`src/contracts/compatibility.js`). `tools/index/assemble-pieces.js` accepts arbitrary `--input` directories and defaults output `--mode code`. Passing a prose piece (or mixing code/prose pieces) can thus merge the wrong chunk/postings corpus and publish it labeled `code`, even with `strict: true`.

## Expected
Validate every input's persisted mode (and cohort identity as appropriate) against the requested output mode before merging or writing. Add a multimode fixture proving same-compatibility-key code/prose pieces cannot be assembled together or under the wrong mode.

## Audit provenance
Current source HEAD `9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d`; CLI/compatibility/assembly source proof. No full native assembly run because local Node is below supported floor. Existing issue search found no mode-mismatch issue.

## Verified current-head close ordering

At PR #572 head `8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda`:
1. [build_index.js closes the display before writing its final summary](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/build_index.js#L186-L190).
2. [writeLine](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/build_index.js#L96-L103) routes `--progress jsonl` back into `display.log`.
3. [display.close](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/shared/cli/display.js#L224-L231) calls `safeStream.close`, and [the safe stream rejects subsequent writes](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/shared/cli/display/stream.js#L12-L18).

Therefore the success summary/detail lines are silently dropped for `--progress jsonl`. The explicit embeddings-cancellation branch similarly closes then writes its terminal message.

The accepted `--progress json` alias has a second mismatch: [normalizeProgressMode](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/shared/cli/display/terminal.js#L5-L10) maps it to JSONL, but the final writer tests only the original literal `jsonl`. It therefore appends raw human text after JSONL progress events instead of a valid structured record. The documented option includes both aliases.

There is also shared TTY cleanup loss: `createDisplay.close` marks its stream unwritable BEFORE calling `term.showCursor()` and `term.eraseLine()`. [resolveTerminal](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/shared/cli/display/terminal.js#L14-L25) binds terminal-kit to that same safe stream, so cleanup escape writes are suppressed. Initial hideCursor occurs while writable, but the paired showCursor cannot be emitted through the closed proxy.

## Required lifecycle contract
- Separate retiring the live frame from retiring output admission, or provide a shared finalization method that writes the final outcome and terminal cleanup before closing the adapter.
- Preserve closed-stream/EPIPE safety. Do not reopen a genuinely closed underlying stream or keep listeners indefinitely.
- Derive output routing from the normalized display mode, not a second independent check of raw argv.
- Emit exactly one terminal outcome in every supported mode, including success, explicit cancellation, failure, skipped/pending work and errors during cleanup. Coordinate its semantic content with #1328's result-driven summary owner; this issue is about delivery/order/framing. #1334 owns responsive layout/resize projection.
- Keep JSON/JSONL streams parseable end-to-end and do not send a raw-text fallback into an already-selected protocol channel.
- Make close idempotent, restore cursor before releasing the writable proxy and retain original failures when output cleanup fails.

## Acceptance tests
1. A minimal successful build under `--progress jsonl` includes the final outcome with build/attempt identity; every nonempty protocol line parses.
2. `--progress json` has the same terminal framing and no raw `[DONE]` suffix.
3. Cancellation and failure have terminal records exactly once and no contradictory success.
4. Instrument the actual writable stream for TTY close: hideCursor is paired with showCursor before the adapter stops accepting writes. Repeated close adds no duplicate cleanup.
5. Broken pipe, stream destroyed, throwing terminal cleanup and normal non-TTY completion remain safe.
6. Exercise the build CLI's real finalization order, not only standalone display.log or a formatter unit test.

## Dedup / scope
#302 (closed) established shared logging routing; this is a concrete remaining close-order regression. #1310 owns compact/literal rendering, #1314 durable failure evidence. Current live display/close/JSONL and cursor searches found no matching focused owner.

Source-traced audit only. No full Node 26 / Windows application run or implementation was performed.

## Operator problem

A successful command exit is not proof that a new complete searchable index was built. Explicit stage runs, intentionally disabled embeddings, service-queued embeddings, unavailable queue admission and partial capability publication need accurate outcomes. Today's CLI prints the same generic success phrase and can attach counts from unrelated prior work.

## Current-head source evidence
- [build_index.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/build_index.js#L136-L190) discards most of `buildIndex`'s result, unconditionally starts with `Index built in ...`, and enriches it from mutable repository-level `preprocess.json`.
- Explicit [stage3 and stage4 branches](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/integrations/core/build-index/index.js#L201-L240) run only embeddings or SQLite, not the preprocessing pipeline that produced those counts.
- [runEmbeddingsStage](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/integrations/core/build-index/stages.js#L185-L197) can return `embeddings.skipped: true`; [service enqueue handling](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/integrations/core/build-index/stages.js#L247-L286) can return queued jobs, partial admission or no admitted jobs. These are not synchronous completion of all requested capabilities.
- [writePreprocessStats](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/index/build/preprocess.js#L369-L378) is best-effort and can leave an older file in place. [The snapshot](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/index/build/preprocess.js#L357-L361) has repo/timestamp/mode counts but no selected build/attempt identity. The final CLI reader does not verify identity or freshness.
- The successful [stage result](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/integrations/core/build-index/stages.js#L1002-L1015) already contains buildRoot, buildId, runtimeAttemptId, stage and modes. Reuse that ownership rather than inferring from the global cache after the fact.

Concrete cases: an explicit stage3 command with embeddings disabled still reaches `[DONE] Index built ...`; stage3/4 can print old source counts; a failed best-effort preprocess stats update can make a new build report a previous run's counts. These conclusions are source-traced, not a new full build run.

## Required outcome model and rendering
1. Produce a canonical typed/JSDoc-documented outcome from the owning build/stage/receipt layer. Include repo, build/generation and attempt identities, requested/completed/skipped/pending/failed stages/capabilities, actual validation/publication result, and authoritative receipt/evidence links.
2. Distinguish `stage completed`, `existing generation enriched`, `jobs queued`, `skipped by configuration`, `not admitted`, `cancelled` and `index published`. A DONE label may describe a completed command, but its sentence must not imply work/readiness it did not accomplish.
3. Show counts only if produced by or qualified to the selected run and modes; otherwise say unavailable or omit. Do not silently turn absent numbers into credible zero counts, or reuse the mutable preprocess snapshot as truth.
4. Human and structured summaries consume the same outcome. Keep the human terminal result short, with full copyable build/evidence paths and actionable reasons available immediately.
5. Recovery/open suggestions must come from capability validation and the supported recovery planner (#1322), not guessed commands, cache scavenging, pointer changes or an automatic full rebuild. Do not promise no rework when resume prerequisites are not met.
6. Report existing graph-ready data independently of failed/disabled embeddings without promoting an invalid generation or advertising the current viewer a selector it does not support.

## Tests
- Full build; explicit stages 1–4; code-only/prose-only; intentionally disabled embeddings; queued jobs; partial/full queue rejection; cancelled/failed stage; prior-current generation retained.
- Pre-seed stale preprocess counts from another attempt, then run stage3/4 or simulate a stats-write failure: no stale counts claimed.
- Summary identity matches the returned receipt and selected per-mode publication, including split-generation modes.
- Semantic output parity between human, JSON/JSONL, quiet and verbose modes.
- Known supported recovery/open action only; unavailable capabilities get exact actionable reasons.

## Boundaries / dedup
#1322 owns recovery planning/execution; #1319 stage reuse, #1320 preprocessing snapshot reuse and #1321 capability sealing supply authoritative facts. This issue owns ordinary CLI summary semantics and avoids duplicating those models. #1314 owns failure evidence, #1310 compact display. #1326 owns final-output close/framing. #1334 owns responsive terminal projection. ## Reproduced mismatch
Running the canonical workspace build from repository A contaminates every selected repository's Node startup environment with A's runtime configuration, even if A is not in the workspace. Per-target configuration then loses to these synthesized values because it is treated as an external environment override.

Bounded actual-resolver probe, starting with an empty environment:
- A config: runtime.maxOldSpaceMb=512, uvThreadpoolSize=2, nodeOptions="--trace-warnings".
- Target B config: runtime.maxOldSpaceMb=8192, uvThreadpoolSize=16.
- Wrapper environment becomes NODE_OPTIONS="--trace-warnings --max-old-space-size=512", UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE="2".
- B requests 8192/16 but resolves effective 512/2 with source external-env; its patch cannot repair the inherited settings.

This can impose an unexpectedly tiny heap or excess memory budget across concurrent builds, leak unrelated startup flags, and make the same workspace behave differently depending on the shell's working directory.

## Live source chain
Audited PR #572 head `8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda`.
1. [runScript]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/bin/pairofcleats.js#L1069-L1086 ) selects an explicit repo/root or resolveRepoRoot(process.cwd()). Workspace build has no allowed --repo target.

[resolveDispatchRuntimeEnv]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/bin/dispatch-runtime-env.js#L10-L18 ) loads that root's config; for tools/workspace/build.js it uses the [generic runtime patch]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/bin/dispatch-runtime-env.js#L46-L49 ).

[Runtime envelope precedence]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/src/shared/runtime-envelope/resolve.js#L193-L244 ) correctly treats existing NODE_OPTIONS/UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE as externally authoritative. These values were actually synthesized for another repository, not supplied by the user.

The real exported envelope and env-patch helpers reproduced the mismatch without launching children. Wrapper/child provenance is source-traced.

## Reproducible state-transition defect
Current PR #572 head: `8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda`.

The native loop maps a raw key to an InputCommand using the current overlay, then delays command execution by a global 25ms interval. A later key can therefore be decoded before an earlier key changes the modal context. FIFO command storage does not preserve FIFO key semantics.

Deterministic reproduction for a native reducer/dispatch test:
1. Have an ordinary command just dispatched, so last_input_at is less than 25ms old, with overlay None.
2. Deliver a Press `/` to open local find. It queues SearchOpen, but dispatch is throttled and the overlay remains None.
3. Deliver a Press `q` before that pending transition executes. It queues Quit, not SearchChar('q').
4. Advance the dispatch clock: SearchOpen opens find; the next dispatch executes Quit.

A fast terminal input burst intended to begin a query can consequently execute a global shortcut. Other shortcut letters can change focus/actions or be dropped instead of entering the draft. Conversely, keys decoded in a closing search overlay remain SearchChar commands after SearchCancel executes. This is distinct from supporting bracketed paste or adding cursor editing: it affects ordinary Press events and the core ordering of modal transitions.

## Evidence
- [modal-dependent mapping occurs at enqueue time](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/crates/pairofcleats-tui/src/main.rs#L3650-L3787)
- [queue stores already interpreted commands](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/crates/pairofcleats-tui/src/main.rs#L3116-L3120)
- [25ms throttle before popping one command](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/crates/pairofcleats-tui/src/main.rs#L3789-L3803)
- [Quit and modal changes dispatch without revalidating context](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/crates/pairofcleats-tui/src/main.rs#L3808-L3830)
- [event read precedes dispatch each loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/crates/pairofcleats-tui/src/main.rs#L4078-L4110)

## Requested correction
Preserve ordered raw-key/modal semantics, for example by queueing keys and interpreting them against the state produced by preceding keys, or by applying lightweight modal/text transitions synchronously and limiting only expensive commands. Do not silently discard valid type-ahead or turn text into shortcuts. Use a clear ownership policy shared by the native direct-handler overlays and queued overlays. Keep global Ctrl+C/release/repeat handling explicit; this ticket does not change shutdown ownership.

## Acceptance
Use a fake clock and the same production enqueue/dispatch path. Cover previous command → / → q, open/close/reopen, palette entry and selection, queued keys crossing into settings/search, and repeated characters. Assert no unintended global action and exact final draft. Include events on both sides of the throttle boundary. Existing single-overlay tests are not sufficient because the bug requires a pending overlay transition.

Related #1285 owns text editing and bracketed paste; #743 owns protocol-drain fairness. This issue owns keyboard event ordering across modal transitions. Verification is exact current-source state tracing, not an executed Rust/native test; no implementation changes.

Revalidated after PR #572 advanced to `480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc` on 2026-10-22: all implicated runtime/report owner blobs are identical to the pinned sources below. The finding remains applicable; bounded probes were not relabeled as a new full-suite run.

## Confirmed false-green path
A typo in a benchmark waiver's expiry is converted to `allowedUntil:null` and treated as an active waiver forever, with no policy-load error. Omitting expiry has the same result. A record containing only an ID is also accepted and matches every issue because every scope selector is optional.

For a real failed-task shape, these malformed waivers produce `aggregateResultClass:"passed_with_degradation"`, aggregate `exitCode:0`, and `productionClean.status:"pass"`. The failure is still counted in repo totals, but the authoritative verdict and clean gate are green.

This violates the explicit owner/justification/expiry/exact-failure contract established by completed #242 and the time-bounded waiver requirement of completed #356. Those features exist; this issue is the narrow validation hole in their current implementation.

## Current source and propagation
Verified PR #572 head `8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda`.
- [Expiry parsing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language/verdict.js#L46-L52) makes invalid or missing input null.
- [Waiver normalization/loading](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language/verdict.js#L300-L342) checks only that an ID exists, accepts the normalized record, and reports no invalid-expiry/required-field error.
- [Matching](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language/verdict.js#L345-L352) treats absent scope as wildcard.
- [Active/expired classification](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language/verdict.js#L395-L402) expires only a finite timestamp in the past; null/invalid dates enter `activeWaivers`.
- [Report builder](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1928-L1929) directly loads this file and evaluates the verdict, which is returned as `output.run`.
- [CLI exit propagation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tools/bench/language-repos.js#L764-L785) consumes that aggregate exit code.
- Existing [waiver test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/8685a0decb70fde42f32896f52825009c5970dda/tests/perf/bench/language-waiver-exit.test.js) covers a complete future-dated valid record, not malformed or incomplete records.

## Minimal reproduction and controls
Imported the unchanged live verdict module with its actual dependency-free diagnostics and extraction-quality helpers. Wrote tiny synthetic waiver JSON files and evaluated one task:
```js
{ repo: 'fixture/repo', language: 'javascript',
  failed: true, failureReason: 'bench', failureCode: 1 }
```
The complete waiver included `id`, `owner`, `justification`, `failureClass:'benchmark_failed'`, repo and language. Only expiry varied.

| Waiver | Load errors | Active | Aggregate exit | Clean gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| None, control | none | 0 | 1 | fail |
| Valid 2099 timestamp, control | none | 1 | 0 | pass |
| Expired 2000 timestamp, control | none | 0 | 1 | fail |
| `2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z_typo` | none | 1 | 0 | pass |
| Missing `allowedUntil` | none | 1 | 0 | pass |
| Only `{id:'oops'}` | none | 1 | 0 | pass |

Malformed and missing dates normalize to null and never appear in `expiredWaiverIds`. This is not a claim that explicit, valid waivers should fail the permissive gate.

## Repair and acceptance
- Validate the waiver document and every row before use. Require a valid finite expiry, owner, justification and an explicit bounded failure/diagnostic scope; fail closed through the existing `waiver_policy_load_failed` path for invalid policy.
- Preserve a missing or invalid field as a validation error, not an implicit indefinite/global permission. If a wildcard policy is supported, make it explicit and still time-bound.
- Validate schema version and duplicate IDs consistently so the reported matched waiver identity is unambiguous.
- Cover valid future and expired controls, malformed/missing/null expiry, invalid date strings, missing owner/justification/scope, duplicate IDs, and mixed valid/invalid records. Test the report builder and CLI exit consumer, not just a rewritten normalization function.
- Require malformed policy to remain non-clean and nonzero while correctly scoped valid policy retains existing supported behavior.

## Deduplication and limits
Reviewed all-state waiver/allowedUntil/expiry searches and the completed original owners #242 and #356. No current issue owns malformed waiver admission. This is separate from missing benchmark measurements (#689/#752) and wrong-scope release reports (#691).
Probe runtime Node v26.10.0 is below the current 26.12.1 baseline. No benchmark corpus, subprocess fleet, full test suite, readiness bypass or production code changes. The pure policy module and both helper dependencies were the verified live sources.

## Verified defect

At live PR #572 head `480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc`, the evaluator forwards the dataset's mode to core search but selects the returned arrays with a different, incomplete mode policy. A successful records-only search is evaluated as zero hits. Broader modes silently discard extracted-prose and records results.

## Reachable mechanism

- [Eval search and payload selection](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/eval/run.js#L101-L120) forwards `--mode records` / `--mode all`, then recognizes only code, prose, and extracted-prose when selecting arrays. The fallback returns only code + prose.
- [Authoritative search-mode resolution](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/src/retrieval/cli-args.js#L152-L179) admits records and all, and includes extracted prose for prose/both/default.
- [Dataset loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/eval/run.js#L136-L158) treats this silently emptied list as successful observed retrieval and computes ordinary recall/MRR/nDCG.
- [Bakeoff caller](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L809-L827) consumes the resulting quality summary.

## Bounded reproduction

Executed the complete unchanged eval runner source, injecting a synthetic coreSearch response and only CLI/display/filesystem boundaries:

1. Dataset: `[{query:"record",mode:"records",relevant:[{file:"record.json"}]}]`.
2. Search request correctly includes `--mode records`; synthetic successful response is `{records:[{file:"record.json"}]}`.
3. Report says `totals.hits=0`, recall@1=0, MRR=0 and nDCG@1=0.

Control: the same single expected hit in `payload.extractedProse` is scored perfectly with mode extracted-prose, but mode all discards it and scores zero. No rank merging or cross-mode score convention is needed to demonstrate this: each control contains exactly one actual hit.

Runtime Node 26.10.0, below the repository's 26.12.1 pin. This is isolated source/control evidence, not a bootstrapped project-suite, real-model, index or platform qualification. No production code changed.

## Repair and acceptance

- Share canonical normalized mode resolution between the request and evaluation response selection.
- Honor supported selected result arrays, or explicitly reject a mode the evaluator does not support before executing searches. Never represent a successfully returned selected cohort as an empty retrieval.
- Define broader-mode metric cohorts/ranking explicitly. Do not silently concatenate incomparable score spaces or infer a new cross-mode ranking while fixing array selection.
- Add tiny fixtures for records, extracted-prose, prose, both/default and all, including single-hit controls and mode normalization.
- Ensure silver and gold use the same selected cohort; a genuine zero-hit response still scores as zero.

## Non-duplication

Live all-state eval/mode/records searches and the existing evaluation inventory were checked. #692 owns overlapping judgment credit; #749 owns duplicate comparison keys; #1119/#1144 own new oracle/paired-statistics capabilities. This is an existing response-projection defect, not another evaluation epic.

## Verified defect

At PR #572 head `480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc`, the default resumable embedding bakeoff reuses old quality summaries when the evaluation dataset has changed in place, or even been deleted. Matching a pathname is being treated as matching the evaluated input.

## Reachable mechanism

- [Output settings/signature](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L509-L532) contains datasetPath and queriesPath, not their contents or evaluated-input identities.
- [Resume loader](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L630-L665) compares JSON settings and only requires a truthy eval field for an eval-enabled completed model.
- [Completed models skip the entire loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L667-L693), including both rebuilding and evaluation.
- [Documented default](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/docs/benchmarks/embedding-model-bakeoff.md#L39-L51): resume is enabled for the default quick profile.

## Bounded reproduction

The exact source-extracted outputSettings, isModelReportComplete and loadResumedModelReports blocks ran against ordinary temporary JSON files:

1. Write dataset A and a matching checkpoint containing one completed model with MRR=1 / recall@10=1.
2. Unchanged dataset: resume accepts one model, as intended.
3. Replace the same dataset path with a different query and a different relevant file: resume still returns the original perfect summary.
4. Delete the dataset: resume still returns that summary.
5. Control: changing topN in saved settings rejects reuse.

No build, inference or corpus search was run. Node 26.10.0 was used for this isolated probe; it is below the repository's 26.12.1 pin and is not supported-runtime/bootstrap/full-suite qualification.

## Required repair

Bind completed evaluation reuse to a versioned evaluation-input identity rather than path strings. At minimum include canonical selected dataset bytes/labels and applicable query input, resolved repo identity, metric/matching policy and the index/model generation actually evaluated. Missing/unreadable inputs or unavailable required identity must not certify a fresh current evaluation.

Preserve safe partial resume, and avoid rerunning expensive work solely because an unrelated output field or timestamp changed. Distinguish a historical receipt from a newly evaluated result rather than relabeling old scores as current.

## Acceptance

- Changed query, judgment, mode or selected dataset contents at the same path invalidate affected summaries.
- Missing/unreadable datasets cannot be silently skipped as successfully evaluated.
- Identical semantic inputs retain valid reuse under the chosen documented content identity.
- Different repo/index/model/input-format identities cannot reuse the same quality result solely because CLI settings match.
- Keep passing controls for unchanged settings/data and partial completed-model resume; cover legacy checkpoints without the new identity.
- Use small fixture/checkpoint tests, not a model/corpus campaign.

## Non-duplication

All-state bakeoff/resume and evaluation searches found no owner for this existing stale-result reuse. #1119 adds oracle adapters, #1144 adds paired uncertainty, and #632 owns representative evidence gathering. This is the current bakeoff receipt validity bug, not those broader programs.

## Current repair credit; bind reuse to the experiment that actually ran

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the original pathname-only resume defect is substantially repaired. [evaluationInputIdentity](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L512-L544) hashes dataset contents and selected policy scripts. [evaluationFileIdentity / bakeoffGenerationIdentity](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/evaluation-identity.js) use contained reads, canonical JSON identity and per-mode manifest/state hashes. [Resume admission](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L658-L675) requires both input and a non-null matching current generation. The [updated resume test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/embedding-model-bakeoff-resume.test.js) correctly rejects unknown generation and retains a positive reuse case backed by a published fixture generation. Do not describe those controls as absent.

Two current gaps remain within this issue's original requirement to bind reuse to actual evaluated inputs/configuration:

1. **The saved generation is read after evaluation, not returned by it.** [The eval/report handoff](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L825-L862) keeps only evalReport.summary, then awaits directorySizeBytes and currentModelGeneration before stamping resumeIdentity. If a normal concurrent publication changes A to B after eval searched A but before that late identity read, A's scores are saved under B. A later invocation observing B can accept them. Likewise dataset identity is captured once before potentially long builds, whereas the eval child rereads the pathname; the saved input must identify the bytes evaluated, not a previous read. These are source-derived schedules, not executed races.

2. **Current query configuration is not an admission input.** outputSettings captures selected CLI knobs and script/data identities, but no effective retrieval policy from the current user configuration/auto policy. The retained index generation's state hashes describe how that index was produced, not a later query-only configuration change. Current search independently [loads user configuration and auto policy](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/run-search/plan-runner.js#L159-L186), including [search.rrf and retrieval.graphRanking choices](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/normalize-options.js#L303-L318). Changing a query-time ranking setting without rebuilding the same retained index need not change the current resume key, yet it can change the score a fresh eval would observe.

### Repair and small proof plan
- Preserve and admit the actual per-query/run execution and selected-input receipt from eval (#1658), including observed generation and effective semantic query policy. Do not manufacture that receipt from an unrelated later current pointer.
- Resolve a single compatible experiment plan for build/eval/reuse, or explicitly mark mixed/unknown execution as non-resumable. Freeze/pass dataset input where supported, or validate the returned content identity against the planned identity and reject mismatch. A before/after pointer check alone is weaker than a pinned immutable result receipt.
- Include a narrow, versioned effective retrieval-policy identity, not raw config/environment or every cosmetic setting. New query weights/routing/matching/cutoff changes invalidate affected quality summaries; unrelated display changes need not.
- Tiny controlled test: eval returns A's receipt, publish B before checkpoint creation, then rerun under B. A's summary must not become reusable as B.
- Same dataset path modified while a build phase is held must either remain frozen to A or produce a B-qualified eval/checkpoint; it cannot save B metrics with A input identity.
- Change a query-only ranking policy with the same index generation and CLI settings; reuse must be rejected. Keep unchanged-data/config/generation positive resume and missing-input/unknown-generation controls.
- The existing resume test disables eval, so it proves generation presence/reuse admission but cannot prove this actual-evaluation handoff. Extend a focused inert-child test with independently specified receipts; no model download or corpus campaign is required.

This audit is source-only. No implementation, tests, build or inference ran. Keep the completed content-hash repair and address these remaining authority boundaries in this owner rather than adding duplicate stale-resume issues.

## Defect

An ordinary AWS Inspector finding can contain multiple vulnerable packages, but normalization retains only `vulnerablePackages[0]`. Every other affected package disappears from the canonical JSON, rendered Markdown, promoted record metadata and context-pack finding when raw retention is at its default off. There is no omission warning.

This is loss within a supported source format, not a request to add a new importer. AWS explicitly defines [vulnerablePackages as an array](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/v2/APIReference/API_PackageVulnerabilityDetails.html); its [Finding contract](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/v2/APIReference/API_Finding.html) even distinguishes partial fixes across packages.

Verified live PR #572 head: `480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc`, 2026-10-22.

## Production path

1. [Documented AWS ingestion](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/docs/guides/triage-records.md) calls [normalizeAwsInspector from the ingest loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/triage/ingest.js#L83-L97).
2. [Package normalization](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/src/integrations/triage/normalize/aws-inspector.js#L73-L94) selects only element zero and emits one `record.package`.
3. [Raw retention](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/dict-utils/paths/triage.js#L28-L34) is off by default. The normalizer does not preserve the source package array elsewhere.
4. [Markdown rendering](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/src/integrations/triage/render.js) only receives that one package. [Field promotion](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/src/integrations/triage/record-utils.js#L3-L11) likewise obtains packageName/packageEcosystem from the singleton.
5. [Records indexing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/src/integrations/triage/index-records.js#L136-L174) tokenizes that Markdown and promotes the sibling JSON, so an omitted package unique to the source array cannot contribute its name or version to the index. [Context packs](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/480f35d7a90e9e962e0286fe424e7b88a2ca2cbc/tools/triage/context-pack.js) load the already-lossy JSON.

## Bounded current-source proof

Ran unchanged, directly fetched AWS normalizer, Markdown renderer and field promoter under an isolated helper runtime.

Authored one finding with stable findingArn and two packages:
- `firstlib`, version `1.0`
- `secondlib`, version `2.0`

Observed:
- Canonical package name: `firstlib`.
- `JSON.stringify(normalized).includes('secondlib')`: false.
- `renderRecordMarkdown(normalized).includes('secondlib')`: false.
- Promoted packageName: `firstlib`; parse warnings: empty.
- Positive control containing only secondlib correctly retains secondlib.
- Reversing the source array switches the canonical package to secondlib while the finding's recordId stays unchanged. Reimporting a reordered equivalent finding therefore changes which package is visible, rather than preserving both.

This executes normalization/render/promotion, not a full index/search run.

## Repair and acceptance

- Preserve all admitted affected-package occurrences with their source association, rather than choosing by array position. A compatibility singleton may remain, but must not be the only retained evidence or imply complete coverage.
- Define a deterministic representation and migrate the renderer, metadata filtering and context-pack consumers together. If producing child records, retain the parent finding identity and deterministic occurrence identity so repeated imports do not duplicate findings or orphan decisions.
- Keep package name/version/location associations intact; do not flatten unrelated package attributes into misleading combinations. Do not treat retaining an unindexed optional raw blob as a complete fix.
- Add zero/one/multiple-package, same-name/different-location, reordered array and repeat-import fixtures. Verify canonical persistence, rendered/indexed evidence, package filters, decision/context linkage and explicit partial diagnostics for malformed entries.
- Preserve legacy singleton input compatibility and state any reimport/rebuild requirement.

## Ownership and qualification

All-state Inspector/package, vulnerablePackages and triage identity searches found no matching owner. #805 owns CVSS arrays and scoringVector; #804 owns generic derived-ID collisions. Neither preserves Inspector package multiplicity. The native fixedInVersion mapping is independently defective even for a single package and should be repaired without conflating it with this collection contract.

## Confirmed consumer defect
At PR #572 head `506e56451020bfdb864f68b2235aa4a2f12a7a82`, the workspace artifact browser loses the original read failure when the owned iterator also fails during release. The catch path is `await closeEntry(entry); throw error`: a rejecting close prevents the original throw.

The current terminal cleanup policy is valuable and must remain: a failed reader release poisons the browser and remains observable from idempotent service close. The missing requirement is to preserve **both** that terminal cleanup evidence and the original read/cancellation/integrity failure, rather than replace the latter.

## Pinned source
- [Read/validation catch](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/506e56451020bfdb864f68b2235aa4a2f12a7a82/src/map/workspace/catalog.js#L153-L173): `next()`, row admission and generation checks share a catch that lets `closeEntry` replace the primary error.
- [Single close-flight and poisoned-browser state](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/506e56451020bfdb864f68b2235aa4a2f12a7a82/src/map/workspace/catalog.js#L36-L48) retain only the cleanup failure and remove the entry after settlement.
- [Service close](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/506e56451020bfdb864f68b2235aa4a2f12a7a82/src/map/workspace/catalog.js#L89-L103) drains active operations and rethrows terminal cleanup failure; preserve this ownership behavior.
- [Existing reader-close failure tests](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/506e56451020bfdb864f68b2235aa4a2f12a7a82/tests/map/workspace/reader-close-failure.test.js) verify cleanup visibility and one return call, but the active-read case expects only the release failure. It does not assert preservation of the initiating read outcome.

## Executed bounded reproduction
Under Node **26.12.1**, executed the exact current `createArtifactBrowser` function body in an isolated VM with inert manifest/configuration collaborators and real promises/AbortController. The injected owned iterator rejects `next()` with one frozen primary Error, then rejects `return()` with a distinct frozen cleanup Error.

Two fixtures:
1. Primary `ERR_ARTIFACT_INTEGRITY`, status 409.
2. Primary `AbortError`, code `ABORT_ERR`.

Both produce:
- the read rejects with the **cleanup object alone**;
- no primary identity, `cause` or aggregate member survives in the returned error;
- the original code is absent;
- service close still rejects with cleanup, and `return()` is called exactly once.

This proves controller-level failure composition, not a real corrupt-index incident or browser/HTTP outcome. A direct full-module test was not run because this read-only source checkout lacks its installed AJV dependency; no dependency or production checkout changes were made.

## Repair
1. Compose read and cleanup outcomes at the existing catch/close owner. Keep an explicit “primary exists” flag; do not use truthiness to infer whether JavaScript threw a value.
2. Retain the original failure object and its classification as the authoritative read outcome. If frozen/non-extensible errors require a wrapper, use an explicit typed aggregate/cause contract containing the original and cleanup objects. Do not spread arbitrary error fields, invoke getters to copy ownership, mutate frozen errors, or stringify away evidence.
3. Keep cleanup failure independently terminal for the browser: no new reads, no cursor resurrection, no second `return()`, and idempotent `close()` must still expose the cleanup failure. Preserving the primary must not turn failed resource retirement into success.
4. Define a small reusable primary-plus-cleanup composition primitive if no suitable neutral helper exists. Existing domain-specific ownership/error helpers show the pattern, but the map viewer must not depend on embedding lifecycle internals merely to combine errors.
5. Ensure the API adapter can classify the original read failure while retaining terminal cleanup diagnostics. Cancellation is not successful empty data; integrity/generation failure is not a generic unexplained release error.
6. Document the read outcome versus browser health distinction in the workspace reader contract and update the current tests accordingly.

## Tests / acceptance
- Exact original read failure survives when cleanup succeeds.
- Cleanup-only failure remains visible and poisons the reader exactly as today.
- Simultaneous decode/integrity/generation/cancellation failure plus cleanup failure retains both identities, with documented primary classification and terminal browser health.
- Cover frozen Error objects, an ordinary non-Error thrown value, and hostile optional diagnostic accessors without replacing the authoritative failures.
- Exercise active read during service close, cursor continuation, natural completion, idle expiry and duplicate close. Return/close happens once; every active operation settles; failed release never revives a cursor.
- At the API boundary, assert the response/evidence distinguishes the original failure and secondary release failure. No “complete” page or silent retry from the current index is returned.
- The existing successful paging/generation/cursor and cleanup-only tests remain valid; only the double-failure expectation changes to preserve information.

### Deduplication / scope
Searched the complete issue inventory and current viewer/artifact cleanup owners. #585 is dead cleanup-owner recovery before ordinary cache reads; #1081 is artifact filesystem cleanup reporting; neither owns this workspace iterator error-composition seam. This does not alter index build publication, embedding lifecycle, renderer architecture or scientific/semantic artifact content.

## Verified accounting hole: one edge can hide an unbounded candidate scan

Source-traced at PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. No tests, benchmarks, index builds or runtime search were executed. This is an operation-count/control-flow finding, not a measured latency claim.

Search context expansion supports `maxWorkUnits`/`maxWallClockMs`, but charges once per relation edge, not for the potentially large candidate lists expanded from that edge. Rejected candidates do not advance the budget, so output caps do not bound work.

### Concrete production route and counterexample

- [The real mode adapter](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/run-search-session/mode-expansion.js#L108-L142) computes allowed IDs from active filters, passes them with prepared context indexes/options to `expandContext`, and publishes its stats.
- [`registerCandidate`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/context-expansion.js#L283-L339) returns immediately for primary IDs, filtered IDs and missing metadata. These attempts neither consume work nor reach output-cap checks.
- [`handleEdges`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/context-expansion.js#L390-L413) calls `consumeWork()` once for the edge, then iterates every target without another budget check. [Import targets](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/context-expansion.js#L482-L504) are all chunk IDs in an imported file. Export/usage names can similarly map to many declarations.
- [Direct-name fallback](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/context-expansion.js#L517-L530) also iterates every same-name declaration after one edge charge. [Repository-map fallback](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/context-expansion.js#L531-L553) checks `maxNameCandidates` only after skipping ineligible IDs; an arbitrarily long rejected prefix remains uncharged.
- The [shared work budget](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/graph/work-budget.js#L65-L89) checks elapsed time only on a consume cadence (default 256). One edge followed by many targets cannot trigger another elapsed-time check.

A discriminating fixture can use one seed, one import edge to a generated file containing N chunks, a prebuilt context index, and `allowedIds = new Set([seedId])`. With `maxWorkUnits=2`, the edge consumes one unit and all N target membership checks still execute; every target is rejected, `added=0`, and there need be no work-budget truncation. Increasing N increases hidden work while the reported budget use stays one. The same shape exists with one common call name and N same-name candidates. This follows directly from the loops; it was not executed during this audit.

## Repair owner and constraints

- Introduce one request-local admission/iteration owner that charges **attempted candidate examinations**, including duplicates, primary hits, filtered entries and missing metadata, before performing the work. Keep relation-edge visits, candidate attempts, admitted hits and preparation work distinct in stats.
- Check elapsed time inside high-fanout target loops, not only at the next edge. Bound the overshoot by a documented small batch, and make cancellation observable through the same owner if the public request supports it.
- Preserve the existing semantics of output caps and `maxNameCandidates`; do not silently redefine an eligible-candidate cap as a scan cap. A scan/work stop needs its own truthful partiality reason.
- Use eligible membership/index summaries or cached filtered bucket views only when their generation/filter identities are exact. Do not create a whole-corpus filtered copy for every small query merely to avoid the inner loop.
- Preserve deterministic prefix ordering, reason priority, shared candidate deduplication and allowed-ID filtering. Report unknown omitted counts conservatively rather than scanning an unbounded tail to count them.
- Keep prepared graph/context lookup construction and the mode adapter's filter-set construction separately attributed. Moving uncounted work before the budget is not a fix.

## Tests that discriminate the failure

1. One import edge with a large target bucket and all targets filtered out; instrument membership/candidate visits. A tiny budget must bound attempted visits, not merely `workUnitsUsed` and output length.
2. Same fixture with a long rejected prefix and one eligible target at the end: tiny budget returns explicit partiality, not an unqualified empty result; sufficient budget finds the target.
3. Repeat for direct call-name matches, repository-map fallback, exports, usages, duplicate/primary candidates, and missing metadata. Include zero/one/exact budget neighbors.
4. Inject a deterministic clock/cancellation witness during the inner loop and assert bounded stop even with fewer than 256 relation edges.
5. At sufficiently large budgets, exact ordered hits/reasons match the uncapped reference. At exhausted budgets, cap metadata identifies the actual work that stopped.
6. Through `createModeExpander`, verify the same accounting/partiality reaches CLI results.

The [current work-budget test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/context-expansion/context-expansion-contract-matrix.test.js#L137-L167) supplies 50 distinct edges, each resolving to one target. It is useful for edge limits, but cannot catch this one-edge/many-target shape. Add a compact adversarial fixture rather than another expensive full-repository run.

## Performance acceptance and dedup

Use counted candidate examinations/Set probes and retained bytes as deterministic acceptance first. Later measure cold index preparation, filtered preparation and warm expansion separately across bucket size/selectivity/output-cap distributions; do not claim a speedup from an unexecuted audit.

## Bug

Semantic find/detail can label a mixed-source response `status: "complete"` when one returned source lacks required extraction/analysis coverage.

Both services concatenate coverage rows from selected sources, then require only that the aggregate extraction array and aggregate analysis array are nonempty and every **present** row is complete. That does not prove phase coverage exists for every source represented in the response. Complete rows from source A satisfy the nonempty checks for an uncovered or syntax-only source B.

This is a source-confirmed counterexample at PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, not an executed reproduction or a claim that a particular user generation has this shape. The bug changes evidence qualification, not the identity of returned records.

## Pinned evidence

- [detail.js, per-request collection](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/detail.js#L71-L82): for each previously unvisited partition, coverage rows are appended by phase. The partition is marked visited even if no rows were returned. No per-source/partition missing-phase fact is retained.
- [detail.js, terminal status](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/detail.js#L185-L189): nonempty aggregate analysis/extraction arrays plus all-present-rows-complete and no frontier are sufficient for complete.
- [find.js, collection and status](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/find.js#L65-L76) has the same aggregate-only test. A source that contributes zero coverage rows does not add a partial row or warning.
- [artifact-store.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/artifact-store.js#L320-L331) and [sqlite-store.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/sqlite-store.js#L55-L73) return coverage for source-related physical partitions. They preserve available rows but do not fabricate a missing-phase marker. The consumer must evaluate presence, not just every returned row.
- This is an admitted/tested absence condition: [seed-discovery.test.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/storage/semantic/seed-discovery.test.js#L26-L68) builds actual artifact and SQLite stores without coverage and asserts that every page remains partial. It currently exercises all-missing coverage, not a mixture with a complete source.
- [trace.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/trace.js#L83-L94) already checks both required phase classes for each coverage lookup and retains `state.analysisIncomplete`; [its final status](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/trace.js#L145-L150) includes that fact. Find/detail are inconsistent with this existing conservative consumer policy.
- [semantic-find runner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/integrations/tooling/semantic-find.js#L35-L48) and [semantic-detail runner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/integrations/tooling/semantic-detail.js#L44-L58) publish the services' returned envelopes. This is not solely an unused helper.

## Discriminating fixture

In one pinned generation, return one valid record from each of two distinct source identities:
- A: complete syntax and complete analysis coverage.
- B: either no coverage rows, or complete syntax only and no analysis rows.

Request both refs through detail with sufficient limits to finish in one page and no missing-record/provider-evidence frontier. The aggregate arrays contain A's complete phases, so the current status predicate can return complete despite B's missing evidence. Repeat with a find selector that matches operations in both sources.

Controls:
- B alone must be partial, as the existing all-missing test already intends.
- A plus B must remain partial. Adding complete unrelated evidence must never upgrade uncovered evidence.
- If B has its own required complete phase evidence, the combined response may be complete, subject to the existing response-budget and frontier rules.
- Explicit partial/deferred rows must remain partial too.

## Repair shape

- Evaluate completeness **per selected coverage scope**, then combine those results conservatively. Respect the store's source-related physical partition projection; do not require every analysis partition independently to own a syntax row when syntax lives in its sibling source partition.
- Preserve why a scope is incomplete: missing syntax, missing analysis, explicit partial/deferred/unsupported coverage, or query/response limits. Do not synthesize a complete empty analysis.
- Share a small coverage evaluation owner across find/detail/trace rather than three subtly different aggregate predicates. Keep the raw physical-partition provenance in the response.
- Keep response enumeration completion separate from extraction/analysis completeness. A fully delivered page can still contain incompletely analyzed evidence.
- Define and test continuation semantics explicitly: page-local coverage versus whole-request accumulated qualification must not be conflated. If overall status describes the drained request, carry a bounded incomplete/unknown summary in continuation state, not unbounded raw coverage arrays.
- Preserve existing no-match caution; this fix must not start treating an exhausted selector as proof that no behavior exists.

## Acceptance and tests

1. Add the two-source mixed-coverage matrix with explicit expected statuses, not artifact-versus-SQLite equality as the only oracle.
2. Exercise both actual store backends using the existing small recovery fixture pattern. Include source-associated syntax and analysis partitions to verify correct scope grouping.
3. Test both ref orders, enough limits for one page, and a forced two-page request. Assert response state, overall status, retained coverage and the documented continuation qualification.
4. Keep fully covered positive controls, all-missing controls, explicit partial/deferred controls, and missing-record frontier cases.
5. Add a monotonicity check: adding complete evidence from another source cannot erase an existing unknown/incomplete qualification.
6. No full repository indexing or timing assertions are required; the fixture needs only a few records/coverage rows and deterministic limits.

## Related scope

#1138 requests independent freshness/completion explanation; #1348 concerns durable producer omission coverage; #1528 concerns independent semantic qualification. This issue is the concrete current **consumer-side false-complete aggregation** after otherwise valid store reads. It does not ask producers to invent missing evidence or broaden analysis claims.
