## Source-established resource-bound gap

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, `createSqliteSemanticStore` exposes and validates `maxRowBytes` and correctly uses it before returning direct node/coverage payloads to JavaScript. Its related-member path bypasses the same bound: every related SELECT returns unrestricted `payload`, `.all()` materializes the entire page, and only then does JavaScript parse and validate each row.

This affects related names, occurrence companions, operands, ownership and edges used by semantic detail/trace/find. Final response-byte and row-count limits do not bound the bytes already hydrated and parsed.

Source inspection only; no SQLite runtime, project suite, index build or production-memory measurement was executed.

## Evidence

- [Store configuration and direct node read](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/sqlite-store.js#L15-L45): default row allowance is 1 MiB; configuration is validated; SQL uses `CASE WHEN length(CAST(payload AS BLOB))<=? THEN payload ELSE NULL END`, with an explicit output-limit error before JSON parsing.
- [Related SQL and hydration](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/sqlite-store.js#L117-L157): all five related queries select raw payload, the call supplies only owner/window parameters, `.all()` returns all selected values, and `JSON.parse(stored.payload)` has no byte admission.
- The [semantic schemas](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/contracts/schemas/semantic.js#L1-L16) do not provide an equivalent global byte bound. For example [lookup value](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/contracts/schemas/semantic.js#L107-L109) is an unrestricted string, and occurrence flags/context text can also make valid records large.
- [Detail](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/detail.js#L103-L132) retrieves occurrence companions and names through `getRelatedPage`, then applies its output admission. [Neighbor reads](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/neighbors.js#L23-L39) similarly retrieve edge pages before trace admission.
- The [artifact backend](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/semantic/artifact-store.js#L333-L355) sends `maxRecordBytes` to its row reader for related canonical members. This is an actual backend-boundary difference, not merely a request to reduce a documented response cap.

## Tiny discriminator

Construct a valid semantic fixture with one lookup/name row whose UTF-8 JSON payload exceeds a deliberately small configured `maxRowBytes` (for example a 2 KiB name with a 1 KiB bound). Call the actual SQLite store's `getRelatedPage(nameRef, 'semantic_lookup', { limit: 1 })`.

Expected: an explicit size/admission failure before exporting or parsing the oversized payload. Current source returns and parses the full value. A small configured bound makes this test cheap; no giant corpus or real memory exhaustion is needed.

Also use a related occurrence row accessible both via `getRecords` and via its expression's `getRelatedPage(..., 'semantic_records')`: the first route enforces the row bound while the second route bypasses it. This compares two production paths for the same authored row.

## Repair architecture

- Apply a shared encoded-byte admission policy to every payload-producing semantic SQL path, including related rows. Keep UTF-8 byte size distinct from JavaScript string length.
- Reject over-limit rows with the existing structured output-limit classification. Do not silently skip the row, advance a continuation over it, or turn it into absence.
- Bound aggregate hydration bytes as well as each row and the row count. A 512-row page of individually admitted 1 MiB payloads is not a small response just because it is eventually truncated to 64 KiB.
- Prefer bounded/iterative selection or a byte-admitted page strategy over unrestricted `.all()`. Preserve deterministic order, offset/cursor progress and owner checks.
- Keep native database work and exported/parsed bytes separate in diagnostics. SQL length checks bound JavaScript hydration; they are not a claim that SQLite performed zero internal work.

## Tests and acceptance

1. Real in-memory SQLite fixture, valid oversized lookup and occurrence rows, small configured bound, explicit `ERR_SEMANTIC_OUTPUT_LIMIT` before parsing/export.
2. Boundary-equal and multibyte strings prove byte semantics; corrupt payloads remain integrity failures rather than fabricated empty pages.
3. Multiple individually small rows exceed the aggregate hydration budget without advancing past unreturned evidence.
4. Drive detail names/companions and trace edges through the production store to prove request limits cannot be bypassed by related hydration.
5. Preserve artifact/SQLite ordered result parity for admitted fixtures and continuation replay/cancellation behavior.
6. Record hydrated bytes/rows in the focused fixture. Do not accept only a final `JSON.stringify(result).length <= cap` assertion, since that occurs after the current expensive allocation.

[Existing detail-hydration coverage](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/storage/semantic/detail-hydration.test.js#L58-L85) usefully checks final bytes, row/record counts, pagination and artifact/SQLite parity, but uses small payloads and never configures a discriminating row bound.

## Dedupe

Searched semantic hydration/row allowance/maxRowBytes and reviewed #1140. That issue owns optional offline query-plan/index experiments, not enforcing an already advertised reader bound. #1425 concerns final semantic-find response size; #1430 concerns artifact operation-index reader reuse. Neither covers unrestricted SQLite related-payload hydration.

## Current-head counterexample

At PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, continuous best-effort progress updates can postpone build-state persistence indefinitely even when storage is healthy. The lag used by heartbeat warnings also measures the newest logical update, not the oldest unpersisted work.

This is a source audit, not an executed long-running benchmark.

### Data flow

- [queueStatePatch, lines 418–475](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/build-state/patch-queue.js#L418-L475) cancels the current timer on every best-effort patch and starts a new trailing-edge debounce. Progress/heartbeat patches use 500 ms, or 1000 ms for a large merged patch. No maximum pending age participates in the flush decision.
- [createBuildCheckpointTracker](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/build-state/progress.js) emits nonblocking best-effort progress on batch thresholds. Multiple producers share one root's patch queue. A stream arriving more often than the debounce period keeps resetting the timer until a quiet gap, a required write, or explicit closeout.
- [buildPendingTelemetry, lines 264–282](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/build-state/patch-queue.js#L264-L282) calculates `pendingLagMs` from `lastLogicalUpdateAtMs`; queue admission just set that timestamp. The returned lag therefore remains near zero while the oldest pending state can be arbitrarily old.
- [heartbeat.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/build-state/heartbeat.js) gates its durability-lag warning on that `pendingLagMs`, despite separately receiving the age currently named `pendingSinceMs`.
- Both nonblocking heartbeat/progress tests inject the persistence function. The heartbeat test supplies `pendingLagMs: 50000`; it never obtains lag from the production patch queue and therefore cannot detect the reset behavior.

A deterministic counterexample is to enqueue a heartbeat, then merge progress every 100 ms for several seconds with a fast successful `applyStatePatch`. No debounce write need start during the stream. A process interruption loses the live stage's recent best-effort snapshot; external progress readers see old state, and the intended lag warning need not fire. Required writes and final barriers are separate and do not cure the live-stream case.

## Required design

1. Retain coalescing and nonblocking callers, but schedule a flush at the earlier of the trailing debounce and an absolute maximum age established by the oldest unpersisted patch. New arrivals must not move that maximum deadline.
2. Keep one serialized persistence owner per build root. Do not create a write per event or accumulate one detached write per tick behind slow I/O. Coalesce the next pending snapshot while an owned write is in flight; preserve required durability and event order.
3. Distinguish oldest pending age, active-write age, newest logical update age, and last durable acknowledgement. Name units/meaning explicitly. Base health warnings on logical-to-durable lag, not idle time since the newest enqueue.
4. Tie telemetry to the actual batch. Completion of an older detached write must not reset timestamps/counts belonging to a newer pending batch.
5. Preserve failure recovery, required-write ordering and the explicit captured-tail flush barrier already present. Do not conflate healthy continuous input with storage lock/backpressure failures.

## Bounded proof plan

Use a virtual clock plus the production patch queue and fake persistence; no long soak is needed.

- Enqueue best-effort progress faster than the debounce for several maximum-age windows. Assert durable writes occur during the stream, the most recent snapshot is eventually persisted, and write count remains coalesced/bounded.
- Include heartbeat and two mode-progress producers on the same root; no producer may indefinitely starve the others.
- Hold the first persistence promise, enqueue more updates, then release it. Confirm the newer batch keeps its own age/contents and no unbounded detached-write backlog forms.
- Assert lag increases while work remains unpersisted, resets only for acknowledged work, and drives a real heartbeat warning through the production queue.
- Cover ordinary quiet-tail flush, required update during pressure, explicit flush, retryable lock failure, and shutdown without weakening existing ordering/barrier tests.
- Separate correctness assertions from timing measurements; record enqueue count, write count, maximum pending age and maximum in-flight/queued batch count.

## Dedupe / repair credit

Closed #295 owns the original bounded heartbeat-health goal. This is a narrow remaining scheduling/measurement defect after its nonblocking/coalescing work. #875's previously missing detached-write barrier is visibly repaired at this head; do not reopen that claim. Watch rebuild scheduling already has a maximum wait in `watch.js`; preserve its independent semantics rather than assuming it protects the build-state patch queue.

## Defect and scope

However, its [execution](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/sqlite-helpers.js#L717-L737) makes a single synchronous `stmt.all` call; no chunk-size loop or elapsed/deadline check uses those settings.
- [Post-query hydration and term queries](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/sqlite-helpers.js#L738-L767) add work with no deadline check. [The receipt](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/sqlite-helpers.js#L768-L777) echoes `timeBudgetMs`; `truncated` is determined only by the row-cap comparison. `overfetchChunkSize` is never used after normalization.
- [The prose routing contract](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/docs/specs/prose-routing.md#L49-L54) describes 150 ms as an overfetch bound. [The budget-named test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/backend/rankSqliteFts-overfetch-cap-budget.test.js#L9-L44) merely asserts that the reported field equals 150. It proves default plumbing, not bounded execution.

The [query-cache identity](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/run-search-session/cache-policy.js#L42-L46) also includes both controls, so changing an ineffective control can miss the cache without changing the underlying execution policy.

## Impact

Operators and benchmark authors cannot use these knobs to bound FTS tail work or vary batch size as advertised. A query can finish after the requested allowance with no budget-exhausted disposition, and a benchmark can mistake a printed budget for a verified control. A row LIMIT bounds emitted rows, not necessarily the scanning/sorting/native work required to produce them.

## Narrow architecture

- Give the FTS execution owner one explicit work/deadline contract, distinguishing requested allowance, actually supported/enforced mechanism, observed elapsed work and termination reason.
- Either implement these controls with a supported bounded/cancellable execution strategy, or explicitly deprecate/reject/report them as unsupported. Do not silently retain tuning knobs that only affect metadata/cache keys.
- If paging/iteration is used, preserve native tokenizer and Boolean/literal eligibility **before candidate-window admission**, stable tie order and weighted ranking semantics. Do not reintroduce #600's rejected-prefix candidate loss.
- Do not equate JS timer expiration with cancellation of a blocking database call. Qualify any SQLite progress/interrupt capability or isolated worker owner, including cleanup and late completion; a post-hoc elapsed check can report an overrun but cannot claim a hard latency bound.
- Include metadata hydration and per-term membership queries in the same declared allowance, or explicitly report separate bounded phases.
- Expose partial/budget outcomes truthfully; do not silently turn budget exhaustion into successful empty hits or claim exhaustive completion. Preserve the existing fallback and eligibility contracts.

## Discriminating tests and measurement

1. Keep the current default-value test, but name it as configuration/diagnostic plumbing.
2. Add a deterministic injected-clock/execution-boundary test that advances past the allowance while work remains. Assert the selected policy stops further dispatch or reports a precise supported overrun/partial result, rather than merely returning `timeBudgetMs=150`.
3. Configure distinct chunk sizes and assert actual bounded dispatch/iteration changes if the feature is supported; otherwise assert explicit unsupported/deprecation behavior.
4. Add a small real SQLite fixture for cancellation/deadline behavior and independent expected ordered IDs, with zero/one/two-page cases, native query error, row-cap exhaustion, and literal/negative eligibility.
5. Benchmark SQL execution, term checks, metadata hydration, total latency and cleanup separately. Compare equivalent results and state the backend/build/cancellation capability; report deadline overrun distribution, not only configured budget. No full index or model campaign is needed.

## Dedupe / current credit

All-state FTS+time, SQLite+deadline and overfetch searches found no exact runtime owner. #675 concerns provider declaration drift; #600 owns eligibility placement; #1122 and #1583/#1585 concern ANN planning deadlines. Current SQL eligibility pushdown and real row-cap enforcement are present and should be retained. This issue is the existing FTS time/batch-control contract, not a generic new benchmark or scheduler.

## Current-head stale analyzer reuse

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the daemon dictionary cache identifies file content only by normalized pathname, byte size and mtime. A same-size dictionary replacement with preserved metadata reuses old words without reading the new dictionary. The scoring analyzer version prefix prevents an old case-policy cache hit, but does not establish the current input bytes.

### Source-backed mechanism

- [buildDictionaryFileSignature](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/dictionary-wordlists.js#L236-L249) returns `path:size:mtimeMs`. It also turns every stat failure into `:missing`, not just a permitted absent optional file.
- [resolveRuntimeDictionaries, lines 244–284](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/runtime/dictionaries.js#L244-L284) hashes those rows, takes a daemon cache hit and skips both base and code-dictionary loaders.
- On a miss, signatures are collected **before** independently opened word streams, then the loaded sets/shared payload are cached under the earlier signature at lines 305–314. There is no receipt binding the signature to the exact successful read.
- The [wordlist test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/shared/dictionary-wordlists.test.js) explicitly checks the current metadata-only signature shape, not content-qualified warm reuse.

Minimal source-derived counterexample: warm a daemon with dictionary bytes `alpha\n`; replace with `bravo\n` at the same path and preserve the reported size/mtime. The next resolver call selects the old cached `alpha` vocabulary. This affects actual tokenizer input, not merely telemetry. No runtime reproduction was executed during this audit.

## Required identity and data flow

1. Create a dictionary-input receipt from the exact completed byte read: selected scope/language, source identity, content digest, decoding/normalization policy and completion outcome. The resulting word sets/shared representation must be tied to that receipt.
2. Use metadata only as a change-detection hint, not proof for externally mutable dictionary files. Managed immutable dictionaries may reuse a verified generation/content receipt under their existing storage lease; externally mutable inputs must be revalidated at the warm-hit boundary.
3. Derive the aggregate analyzer identity from ordered/framed input receipts and semantic scope. Bind common versus language-specific membership, normalized policy version and selected input set. Do not concatenate ambiguous arbitrary path strings as the sole structured identity.
4. Share hashing with the successful load where possible; avoid a full hash pass followed by an unrelated pathname read. Changed/failed reads must not publish a mismatched identity. Preserve original descriptor/lease ownership and containment policy.
5. Propagate the new identity to consumers of `dictSignature`, shared dictionaries and dependency-qualified lexical checkpoints. Version/migrate old metadata-only cache entries conservatively; never silently call them verified.
6. Preserve permitted optional absence separately from stat/read failure. Coordinate complete-read admission with #1598, but do not consider that fix sufficient for a successful same-metadata content replacement.

## Bounded proof plan

- Through the actual runtime resolver plus recording daemon cache, warm `alpha\n`, replace with same-size `bravo\n` under an injected unchanged metadata observation, then require the new vocabulary and changed receipt.
- Cover unchanged input warm reuse, base/common/language dictionaries, changed selected scopes, normalization policy change, optional missing input and EACCES/stat failure.
- Inject replacement between identity observation and stream opening, and a change during read. Accept a consistent verified snapshot or reject; never tag different words with the earlier identity.
- Assert old metadata-only entries cannot satisfy the new receipt contract, and prove exact worker/shared-view versus inline vocabulary agreement.
- Measure bytes read, hash/parse counts and retained representations separately. An immutable-managed-input fast path should prove avoided reads from its retained generation authority, not from a benchmark-only mtime assumption.

## Dedupe / scope

All-state searches for dictSignature, dictionary signature/mtime/content found no matching runtime dictionary owner. #848 owns repaired case/Unicode normalization; #1183/#1451 concern downstream lexical/bundle reuse; #1369 concerns artifact-family reuse. #1598 is partial/failed reads, whereas this issue also occurs on two fully successful loads. Source-only audit, no implementation or runtime campaign.

## Current-head cancellation gap

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the build's AbortSignal reaches dense and phrase/chargram assembly, but stops at the token/field postings materializer.

- [buildIndexPostings](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/indexer/steps/postings.js) passes `runtime.abortSignal` to `buildPostings`.
- [buildPostings](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/postings/index.js) forwards it to dense and phrase/chargram work, but does not pass it to `buildTokenAndFieldPostings`.
- [token-field.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/postings/token-field.js) has no signal or abort checks while expanding/sorting vocabularies, cloning/normalizing posting pairs, building all fields and clearing the input maps.
- [createCooperativeYield](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/postings/constants.js#L35-L52) only schedules setImmediate. Yielding lets cancellation arrive; it does not observe it.
- [normalizeTfPostingList](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/build/postings/id-lists.js) can synchronously traverse/copy one large common-term posting list between those yields.

Thus aborting at a token/field yield can still allow the remaining sparse materialization and destructive map clearing to finish before any outer owner observes cancellation. This report does **not** claim a canceled generation necessarily publishes; its demonstrated source gap is failure to stop expensive admitted producer work promptly.

## Required repair

1. Thread the build signal into token/field assembly and observe it at entry, before admitting each bounded unit, after actual yields/awaits and before returning a successful result.
2. Bound cancellation latency inside large single-term normalization and vocabulary sorting, not just between terms. Use bounded sorted runs/merge or an admitted worker/chunked path when necessary; avoid one promise per posting pair and retain the repaired no-yield synchronous fast path from #1210.
3. Define ownership of source maps and partial output explicitly. On cancellation, do not return a success-shaped result. Either retain still-owned inputs for the permitted retry contract or make the attempt terminal and discard partial materialization; do not blindly replay against partly consumed maps.
4. Maintain exact token-ID mapping, deterministic ordering, TF/doc-length statistics and safe field names. Do not drop common terms, sample postings or relax validation to hit a cancellation target.
5. Keep reservations through actual local/worker settlement. A request cancel does not justify releasing memory/CPU ownership while a delegated normalization or sort remains active.

## Small proof plan

- Inject a cooperative-yield gate into real token/field assembly, abort at the first yield and assert no later field/term normalization starts and the promise rejects as cancellation.
- Include pre-aborted input, cancellation after token vocabulary preparation, during a large common-term normalization, during field assembly and just before success.
- Record source-map and partial-output ownership on each path; ensure a retry cannot silently treat a cleared map as an empty successful index.
- Assert unchanged uncanceled exact artifacts and operation counts. Use tiny forced batch boundaries rather than huge fixtures or wall-clock sleeps.
- Report maximum work admitted after abort and peak active normalization bytes. Preserve #1210's synchronous no-yield behavior in the normal path.

## Dedupe / qualification

All-state postings cancellation searches found #1048 queue admission and #1360 packed writer encoding, not this Stage2 materializer. #1364 owns field artifact sharding, not propagation of the producer's AbortSignal. Source-only audit, no runtime campaign or implementation.

## Source-derived report defect

PR #572 head rechecked on 2026-10-23: `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. Source inspection only; no live search, quality benchmark or test execution.

[The evaluator](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L41-L45) sets:

`ks = [1, 3, 5, 10].filter(k => k <= Math.max(10, topN))`

Consequently it **always reports all four cutoffs**, including when `--top 1` or `--top 5` was selected. [The search call](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L63-L77) requests only `-n topN`, and [metric calculation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L99-L117) treats absent ranks beyond that requested window as ordinary misses. It also reports unqualified `mrr` although only a bounded returned prefix was observed. Conversely `--top 20` still has no @20 metric.

These numbers are valid only as scores of the deliberately depth-limited returned system output, not measurements of the underlying ranking's unobserved @10 prefix or full reciprocal rank. The [documentation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/docs/benchmarks/evaluation.md#L15-L16) says top N results to evaluate and [names the metrics as Recall@k/MRR/nDCG@k](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/docs/benchmarks/evaluation.md#L51-L55); the report does not attach an under-observed/lower-bound status to the excess cutoffs.

For an independently fixed ranking whose first relevant hit is rank 2, `--top 1` emits recall@3/@5/@10 and MRR equal to zero without ever requesting that rank. `--top 10` can report positive values under the same metric labels. The fetch-depth intervention has silently changed the evidence behind a purported common cutoff. Do not confuse a true exhausted list of one hit with an intentionally requested one-hit prefix.

## Preserve current repairs

- Cohort selection rejects missing/failed arrays and output-budget hit omissions rather than counting them as retrieval failures.
- Metrics use unique ranks, stable document identity and one-to-one judgment assignment.
- Mode-cohort macro metrics and saved vector/fusion/task replay are explicitly separated.
- [The live quality smoke fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/eval/quality.test.js) uses `--top 5` but checks only @5, so it cannot catch the unsupported @10 report.
- [The actual-runner admission fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/eval/response-evidence-admission.test.js#L30-L39) fixes top to 10, so all its cutoffs happen to be observed.

## Repair boundary

1. Define an explicit evaluation plan with requested retrieval depth, metric cutoffs and effective observed/exhausted depth per cohort. Keep ranking-system parameters distinct from a reporting cutoff.
2. Either request enough results for the largest reported cutoff, or publish only cutoffs no larger than the admitted request depth. If deliberately reporting a shallower system's @k, label that estimand and depth-limited policy explicitly so it is not compared as an equal-depth ranking measurement.
3. Name bounded reciprocal rank `MRR@depth` or include its censoring/cutoff receipt. An absent relevant hit beyond the observed prefix is not evidence of its global rank.
4. Preserve known exhaustion separately from truncation, unavailable execution and output omission. Do not fabricate extra results or silently expand expensive retrieval to an unrequested depth without an explicit evaluation plan.
5. Bind the metric/depth policy into report identity and paired-comparison admission, and report the selected matching policy alongside it. Never average runs with different evidence depth as though they share one estimand.

## Small discriminating tests

Use the current actual-runner module-hook seam with an independent fixed ranked list, where the search stub returns only the requested `-n` prefix.

- Relevant hits at ranks 1, 2, 4, 6 and 11; top values 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20.
- Assert search request depth and every advertised metric cutoff/denominator/qualification together, not just one convenient @5 value.
- Separate a legitimately exhausted short list from a truncated requested prefix.
- Keep missing cohort, failed search and output omission negative controls, which must remain unavailable rather than zero quality.
- Exercise silver/gold and independently ranked mixed cohorts with the same declared depth policy.
- Pair two reports with incompatible metric/depth policies and require explicit incompatibility or separately named estimates rather than a numeric delta.

## Dedupe

All-state searches for eval cutoff, Recall@k and evaluation topN found #692 (judgment double-counting, now repaired in current source) and broader evaluation research, not this requested-depth/report-label mismatch. This is not a request for a larger benchmark campaign or a new ranking algorithm.

## Current defect

At PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, a saved fusion sweep can evaluate and select a candidate depth larger than the captured channel prefix. The replay silently uses the shorter saved list while retaining the larger requested depth as the selected policy. There is no channel-exhaustion receipt establishing that the absent tail is actually empty.

This is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed reproduction or a claim that an existing campaign selected the wrong winner.

## Evidence and impact

- [Capture]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/evaluation/fusion-replay.js#L119-L174) admits bounded ordered hit arrays and saves their ranks/scores. [The strict record schema](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/contracts/schemas/fusion-replay.js#L12-L34) has no requested retrieval depth, exhausted status or captured-prefix frontier.
- [Replay admission and slicing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/evaluation/fusion-replay.js#L204-L217) accept any integer sparseDepth/denseDepth from 0 through4096, independent of captured length, then call slice(0, requestedDepth).
- [The receipt](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/evaluation/fusion-replay.js#L265-L273) retains the requested setting and its policy key. Actual membership counts are reported, which is useful, but do not distinguish exhausted channels from unavailable ranks.
- [Sweep evaluation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/evaluation/fusion-sweep.js#L107-L119) charges min(capturedLength, requestedDepth). [Selection and terminal report](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/evaluation/fusion-sweep.js#L132-L190) can freeze such a policy and return complete:true without qualification about its unsupported depth.

For example, capture a genuinely truncated sparse top2, retain the same dense channel and request sparseDepth:100. The code evaluates sparse top2, not sparse top100. A relevant or high-scoring rank3 is not available to the replay. A grid containing that setting can still select it; equivalent truncated results at depths2 and100 can tie and be ordered by policy hash. The report explicitly excludes retrieval/model/index I/O from measured cost, correctly, but that disclaimer does not make the depth100 quality observation identifiable.

The same risk appears when only some query captures are too shallow. Silently clipping each query produces heterogeneous effective policies under one selected grid setting.

## Repair architecture

1. Extend the existing capture contract with per-channel requested depth, captured count, admitted ordering/prefix semantics and a trustworthy exhaustion/coverage status. Unknown completeness is not exhausted.
2. Permit depth ablations within a captured prefix. Permit greater requested depth only where an authoritative exhausted channel proves the returned list is complete, or explicitly label the experiment as clipped-prefix-only and do not select/export it as evidence for the larger retrieval policy.
3. Reject an unsupported grid up front, or report an explicit unevaluable candidate/query outcome. Do not drop unsupported queries and compare winners over different, undisclosed task sets.
4. Retain requested versus effective depths and availability reasons in replay/sweep receipts. Bind this contract to schema, policy/checkpoint and frozen selection identities. Reuse the existing bounded capture/admission and partial-result owners rather than adding a second sweep engine.
5. Document which experiments are counterfactual replay of an observed prefix and which are qualified retrieval-depth comparisons. Do not infer live latency or unseen scores from saved lists.

## Small discriminating tests and acceptance

- A truncated top2 capture plus requested depth3/100 must not yield an unqualified complete comparison or selected larger-depth policy.
- The same short list with independently supplied exhausted-channel evidence can be admitted for a larger request without inventing candidates.
- Sparse and dense boundaries are tested independently, including depth0, exact captured depth and one past it.
- Mixed query captures with unequal available depths do not silently change the comparison population or effective policy.
- A hand-authored rank3 changes the expected winner when the deeper list is actually captured. This distinguishes a real depth comparison from two labels for the same top2 prefix.
- Existing baseline replay parity, no-test-label selection, immutable capture, cancellation and deterministic restart fixtures stay intact. [The current sweep fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/eval/fusion-replay-baseline-and-sweep.test.js#L68-L105) only uses an in-prefix depth grid and therefore does not discriminate this failure.
- Admission should be O(records × configurations) small metadata work, bounded by existing limits, without invoking providers or capturing extra vectors merely to reject an unsupported experiment.

Related: #1120 owns the implemented sweep capability; this is a narrow current contract defect in that implementation. #1641 concerns live metric cutoff versus requested result depth, not this saved-candidate availability boundary. No production ranking default change is requested.

## Defect and evidence

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, [resolveUtilizationPct](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L262-L278) collects utilizationPct, overallPct, utilization.overallPct and utilization.overall into one list, then chooses scale=1 only if the numeric value is greater than1. Values at or below1 are multiplied by100 regardless of the field's declared unit.

Consequently utilizationPct:1 is reported as100%, utilizationPct:0.5 as50%, and utilizationPct:1.01 as1.01%. The conversion is discontinuous and reverses the apparent order of ordinary low-utilization samples. [Summary averages, extrema, quantiles and timeline](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L634-L645) all consume these transformed values.

The [existing bounded-sample fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/tooling/bench/runner-utilization-cap.test.js#L8-L33) emits utilizationPct=(i %100), including1, but asserts only retained sample/timeline counts. It cannot detect the measurement error.

A related missingness edge is in the same normalization path: [toFiniteNumber](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L211-L214) converts null to0. A supplied utilizationPct:null therefore wins as a measured0 before a valid lower-priority field or cpuUsed/cpuTotal fallback can be considered.

These are direct source-derived examples. No benchmark or project test was executed and no host-utilization result is claimed.

## Fix boundary

- Normalize by field/schema units, not magnitude. Percentage-named fields stay percentages, including fractional percentages and exactly1. A documented ratio field is scaled by100 under its own contract.
- Admit only the permitted numeric representation; preserve absent/null/nonfinite/invalid samples separately from measured zero. Continue to a valid fallback only when the selected source is unavailable, and retain the chosen source/unit in a bounded receipt.
- Keep scheduler token occupancy distinct from measured CPU/per-core utilization. The current cpuUsed/cpuTotal fallback is useful, but should not silently claim hardware CPU measurement merely because the aggregate is called perCoreUtilization. This scope labeling can be versioned without redesigning scheduler telemetry.
- Deliberately version any report/schema change; do not rewrite old receipts or break existing benchmark log lines. Preserve bounded retention.

## Discriminating tests

1. Percent field values0,0.5,1,1.01,50,100 round-trip in the same unit and remain monotone.
2. A separately declared fractional/ratio source0.5 normalizes to50, without changing utilizationPct:0.5.
3. null/absent/invalid percent field plus valid token counts reaches the correct qualified fallback; all unavailable yields no measurement, not measured zero.
4. Feed a tiny known trace through the actual runner and assert sample values, mean, extrema and percentile with independent expected constants, not just sample count/type.
5. Retain the >2048 sample cap test separately. Inspect low-valued samples in the retained suffix so the numerical assertion is not accidentally outside the window.

Related #689 owns omitted thresholds/missing measurements in check-guardrails, not this runner's unit conversion. #820/#1332 concern telemetry attribution elsewhere; this issue repairs the concrete benchmark normalization boundary.

## Same runner measurement boundary: preserve duration, wait and clock-domain meaning

Continuing the current-head audit, keep these closely related telemetry qualification repairs with this runner owner rather than creating one issue per transformed field. Source inspection only; no claim that a production benchmark has already emitted mixed clock domains.

1. **Service duration is currently substituted for stall.** [Artifact aggregation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L558-L586) selects stallMs ?? queueDelayMs ?? waitMs ?? durationMs and puts those values in artifactStallDurationMs. An artifact carrying only durationMs:40 becomes a 40ms stall observation, although the input did not say any of that time was blocked. queueDelay and other waits also need explicit phase/scope rather than silently conflating unlike quantities. Null duration passes Number(null) as zero. The [guardrail consumer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/check-guardrails.js#L116-L124) trusts the stall metric as a stall threshold, and #1655's A/B scorer consumes it.
2. **Completion order mixes unqualified timestamps.** [runOne](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L395-L435) stamps parent script timing with Date.now() epoch milliseconds; [artifact ingestion and the criticalPath sequence](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L565-L622) accepts child startedAtMs/endedAtMs without declared origin or conversion, then sorts both together. A legitimate child-relative 5..45ms interval and an epoch parent interval cannot be chronologically compared from those bare values. Even with compatible clocks, completion-order sorting is not a dependency-derived critical path.
3. **Stage overlap is an estimate, not observed overlap.** [resolveStageOverlapRow](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L352-L370) computes max(0, parseMs+inferMs+writeMs-totalMs). It has no interval unions or dependency information, and may substitute whole subprocess runtime for totalMs. That formula can be useful as a labeled excess aggregate-work estimate under a compatible scope, but does not establish actual overlapping wall-time or causal critical-path delay.

### Focused architecture and acceptance
- Define a small versioned adapter/receipt for value, unit, observation scope, clock origin and availability. Preserve service duration, queue admission wait and specific blocked phases separately; absent wait remains unknown, not the artifact's whole duration.
- Collect elapsed durations with a monotonic clock. Keep wall-clock timestamps for correlation. Convert child-relative intervals only with an explicit compatible origin/anchor; otherwise retain a local timeline and mark cross-process ordering unavailable.
- Label the current completion list as a completion timeline and the aggregate-stage formula as an estimate, or add actual interval/dependency evidence before calling them measured overlap/critical path. Do not add a large graph framework merely to retain an honest diagnostic.
- Tiny independent cases: duration-only artifact has known duration and unknown stall; explicit stall:0 stays a measured zero; queue wait versus service time stays distinguishable; null/negative/invalid observations are unavailable or rejected; two same-origin intervals order correctly; a relative child interval is not silently compared with epoch time; parent clock adjustment cannot yield negative elapsed duration.
- An independent interval fixture with gaps and concurrent work must not let the arithmetic excess-work estimate masquerade as interval-union overlap. Existing parser/noise metamorphic tests remain valuable but do not prove timing semantics.
- Preserve the established human-readable log format and version JSON/schema fields deliberately. Keep #689's repaired missing-threshold/missing-observation checker behavior and #1655's sweep admission separate. No benchmark campaign or test suite was executed.
### Aggregation coverage also needs an explicit estimand

[collectUtilizationSamples](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L287-L301) retains atMs, but [the summary](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L634-L644) takes an unweighted arithmetic mean of sampled values. Samples are appended in script order through [a global rolling cap](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L305-L318), so a late high-sample script can evict every observation from earlier scripts. The aggregate is neither a duration-weighted utilization estimate nor an equal-script mean, and its coverage changes with trace emission density and suite order. Zero retained samples also produces avgPct/min/max/quantiles:0, so the repaired guardrail reader can still receive upstream invented zero observations.

Keep a clearly named retained-sample statistic if useful for diagnostics, with window/source coverage and omitted counts. For a run-wide occupancy or efficiency claim, define the desired time/workload weighting, use compatible timestamp intervals and per-script scope, and accumulate bounded online aggregates separately from the capped display timeline. Do not average incomparable token/hardware sources. Unknown duration/coverage yields an explicitly limited sample statistic, not a time-average claim.

Add independent tiny controls: same equal-duration trajectories with different sample densities; reversed script order after crossing the timeline cap; empty trace versus measured all-zero trace; irregular timestamps with a hand-calculated duration-weighted mean. A bounded timeline must not silently redefine a statistic labeled run-wide. This is a measurement-contract repair, not a claim that the current sample mean arithmetic is wrong for its narrower retained-sample estimand.

## Defect

The generic benchmark suite runner can classify a failed subprocess as an allowed skip merely because stdout or stderr contains “skipped” or “skipping”. That skip then takes precedence over the process failure in aggregate status, allowing exit0.

Current source: PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. This is a source-derived control-flow counterexample, not a newly executed failed benchmark.

## Exact path

1. [runOne](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L395-L444) correctly retains a nonzero/null exitCode and sets ok:false. Timeout detection is separate.
2. If suite output requirements are unmet, [lines521–532](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L521-L532) set skipped:true whenever allowSkip and a substring match are present. They do not require a clean zero exit or exclude process failure/signal.
3. [The summary](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L538-L542) checks timedOut, then skipped, then ok. A non-timeout failed child with skipped:true therefore contributes only to skipped.
4. [Final exit](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L738-L739) depends only on summary.error and summary.timeout. A run containing such a row and no other failures exits0, even though its detailed row still says ok:false.

An eligible suite entry that prints a skip-looking diagnostic but exits1, or terminates by signal without a timeout, must remain failed. Partial work or an error message mentioning a skipped substep is not a terminal whole-benchmark skip.

The path is enabled today by [Sweet16's filter-index-build entry](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/suites/sweet16.js#L39-L45). Its [normal unavailable-roaring branch](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/index/filter-index-build.js#L14-L17) intentionally prints a skip message and exits0; preserve that valid case. This issue does not claim that branch itself currently exits nonzero.

## Repair

Centralize terminal outcome precedence: timeout/signal/spawn/nonzero failure cannot be overridden by a textual skip. Admit an allowed skip only from a successful subprocess and a recognized structured or narrowly parsed terminal skip receipt. Retain skip reason separately from missing expected-output errors. An incidental substring in logs must not waive a process failure.

Use the existing runner/report schema and suite policy. Do not weaken the language benchmark ledger/verdict implementation or add another general benchmark framework. Existing log lines can remain compatible while an explicit machine-readable terminal receipt is added.

## Tests

- allowSkip=true, expected output absent, recognized skip, exit0: skipped.
- Same output but exit1: error, aggregate exit nonzero, original exitCode retained.
- Same output but signal termination: failure, not skipped; timeout remains timeout.
- “skipped” appears in an unrelated diagnostic, including a failed substep: cannot authorize a whole-benchmark skip.
- Required entry without allowSkip remains failed when metrics are absent.
- Mixed successful/valid-skip/failed children produce mutually exclusive terminal counts and the correct aggregate exit.

[Current generic runner fixtures](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/tooling/bench/bench-runner-fixture.js#L29-L47) launch direct --scripts entries, with no suite expectations or allowSkip, and stop when the runner exits nonzero. Add a focused suite/outcome test seam that can assert the failure result without converting it into an early test-process exit.

Deduplication: closed #242 and #280 own language-corpus aggregate verdict/ledger work. This is the separate tools/bench/bench-runner.js skip-precedence path, not a claim those completed owners are absent. No actual benchmark workload or native dependency is needed for the regression.

Related terminal-outcome evidence at the same pinned head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523` (source audit, no execution):

Please preserve the underlying subprocess failure receipt when centralizing outcome admission, rather than repairing only skip precedence. [runOne's catch](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L413-L443) keeps `error.result` but drops the actual error class/code/message whenever that result exists. The final result/report also omits `signal`. The shared [sync owner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/runner-sync.js#L69-L100) supplies a normalized result for spawn/capture errors and throws the actual cause separately. Thus a launch or output-buffer failure can be reduced to `exitCode:null`, `timedOut:false` and a generic benchmark error, with no original reason in the saved report. The fallback message at lines417–422 does not help because the normalized result already exists.

Capture is also part of the outcome contract, not just debug formatting. [The sync owner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/runner-sync.js#L21-L24) defaults to a 1,000,000-byte buffer and [passes it to spawnSync](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/runner-sync.js#L48-L61). The generic runner provides no alternate bounded output plan. A sufficiently verbose benchmark may hit the capture buffer independently of workload correctness, yet the report cannot identify that class after the catch drops its cause. Do not fix this by simply allowing unlimited output or interpreting a retained log tail as a complete metric stream.

Extend the normalized row with explicit execution/capture failure kind, original signal, safe bounded cause text/code and capture completeness where known. Keep the process result and metrics admission separate. Shared sync/async capture receipts should use one documented schema where feasible; do not fabricate observed-byte counts the sync API does not provide. A separately bounded structured result artifact can decouple metrics from verbose diagnostic storage.

Add tiny controlled failure fixtures for unavailable executable/spawn error, output-buffer error, signal termination and ordinary nonzero exit. Assert the saved machine-readable report distinguishes each and cannot classify any as an allowed skip; preserve a valid zero-exit skip and a verbose-success path under an explicit bounded capture policy. This is the same terminal outcome owner as the issue, not a separate generic subprocess rewrite.

Additional current caller for this terminal-outcome owner, at `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`:

After queries complete, [tests/perf/bench/run.test.js invokes report-artifacts and substitutes {} whenever its status is nonzero](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L738-L749). It does not retain the child's error/signal/stderr or an artifact-collection failure receipt. Since corruption is then null, the corruption.ok===false check is bypassed, and [the normal output contains successful query summaries plus artifacts:{}](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L772-L782). A launch, capture, signal or ordinary nonzero failure becomes indistinguishable from absent optional artifact data. A zero-exit empty object similarly has no required shape admission.

Do not discard valid query timings merely because artifact collection failed, but preserve phase status and distinguish partial evidence from a fully qualified benchmark. The experiment plan should decide whether this artifact/validation phase is mandatory; required failure must prevent acceptance, while optional failure is explicit with unavailable coverage. Reuse the current subprocess result/capture owner and bound diagnostics, rather than silently falling back to {}. Keep genuine artifact corruption failure behavior.

Add tiny injected-report-child cases: ordinary nonzero, signal, launch/capture error, malformed JSON, zero-exit wrong shape, and a valid report. Assert the query samples survive as partial where allowed, exact collection failure is retained, and no failed/unobserved corruption check is represented as successful validation. No actual child or benchmark was executed in this audit. This extends the existing failed-subprocess truthfulness owner, not a new benchmarking framework.

## Current defect

Live canary environment receipts are collected in the parent process context, before the effective child runner context is resolved. Per-canary environment/cwd overrides can change the workload and selected toolchain without changing the recorded environment snapshot.

Source: PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. No probes, canaries or project tests were executed in this audit.

## Evidence

- [runVersionProbe](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/canaries.js#L149-L177) resolves Windows command invocation using process.env and runs with process.cwd()/process.env.
- [Snapshot construction](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/canaries.js#L179-L224) reads buildBenchEnvironmentMetadata(process.env). Its process-lifetime cache key includes only the declared environment object and inferred probe IDs.
- [Runner resolution](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/canaries.js#L559-L607) independently expands runner.cwd and runner.env. runBenchRuntimeLiveCanary obtains the environment snapshot first at line590, then resolves the runner at593 and executes with {...process.env,...env} and the selected cwd.
- The result embeds that earlier parent snapshot as the run's environment. Effective overrides are not present in its runner summary.

For a supported runner.env override to a PAIROFCLEATS_* setting or PATH, or a runner.cwd selecting a different repository-local toolchain, the child can execute under B while its receipt/probes describe A. Two entries with the same declared prose contract and probe IDs but different overrides reuse the same snapshot. This is not a claim that the current canned manifest already exercises all those overrides; the admitted runner contract supports them.

An additional identity issue in [buildBenchEnvironmentMetadata](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/logging.js) is that selected keys are inserted in Object.entries(env) order, then JSON.stringify is hashed without canonical key ordering. Equivalent key/value environments assembled in different orders can produce different fingerprints. The outer canary fingerprint embeds this order-sensitive metadata.

## Repair architecture

1. Resolve one immutable effective runner plan first: executable, arguments, cwd and final child environment, including token expansion and supported platform behavior.
2. Feed that same plan to version probes, selected-environment capture and child launch. Distinguish parent/bootstrap evidence from child/workload evidence rather than labeling one as the other.
3. Key any bounded probe/snapshot reuse by the effective probe environment, cwd/toolchain selection and resolved executable identity, with an explicit freshness policy. A changed PATH or supported child override must not reuse another plan's receipt.
4. Canonicalize selected keys before hashing and version the fingerprint semantics. Keep operational run-instance paths separate from comparable environment dimensions where appropriate, while retaining their provenance.
5. Preserve allowlisted/redacted environment capture. Do not serialize the entire environment, credentials or arbitrary secret variables just to improve reproducibility.
6. Keep optional/synthetic provider probes explicitly scoped. A reduced node-only fixture must not claim a real provider was exercised, and an informational unavailable probe need not automatically fail an unrelated workload.

## Tests

- Two plans with identical declared environment text but different allowed child setting values produce distinct effective receipts.
- A stub probe records its received cwd/env and must see exactly the child's selected values; changing PATH selects the intended fake tool without running external providers.
- Same effective environment assembled in reverse insertion order has the same canonical fingerprint.
- Cache reuse occurs for truly equivalent plans, not across cwd, PATH, executable or relevant override changes.
- The report retains parent/child evidence scope and unknown/probe-failure states; no missing probe becomes a version match.

[The current environment test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/language-report-environment-metadata.test.js) verifies existence and transport of the fingerprint/selected values, while [the live runner test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/bench/bench-runtime-live-canary-runner.test.js#L13-L24) checks fingerprint presence and a probe-ID array. Add actual context/equality oracles rather than another truthiness assertion.

Closed #433 delivered metadata/probe/report infrastructure and remains credited. This is a narrow effective-context and cache-identity defect in that infrastructure. #385 owns whether compatible, genuinely executed evidence can qualify blocker closure.

- [scoreRun](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L139-L151) turns absent duration/stall/utilization observations into zero and adds a finite 1,000,000 penalty per error/timeout. It does not check completed workload identity, required successful scripts, skipped work, required measurement coverage or correctness. A short failed variant can score below a sufficiently long successful variant; this is a hard eligibility condition represented as an arbitrary tradeoff.
- [runVariant](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L179-L224) runs bench-runner with --json and --quiet. On nonzero exit, absent stdout JSON is replaced with an error:1/results:[] object. The [main loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L249-L271) prefers that object over the on-disk report. [bench-runner actually writes its complete report before exiting nonzero](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/bench-runner.js#L729-L739). Thus a failed run's retained timings, failure details and script coverage are not used by the sweep, despite its reportPath being advertised.
- Every run is sorted by score and [the first is always recommended](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L270-L309). An all-failed matrix still has a bestConfig and normal successful completion of main. An allowed-skip workload can also compete as though it did equivalent work.
- The [current contract test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/tooling/bench/ab-sweep-contract.test.js#L18-L81) is useful plumbing coverage, but its child ignores every swept knob and prints fixed telemetry. Assertions prove only a matrix and a numeric recommendation exist, not that an invalid run is excluded or that a known better equivalent run wins.

## Repair within the existing runner/sweep owners
1. Separate admission from objective scoring. Admit only successful, correctness-qualified runs with the declared required workload completed, compatible source/corpus/index/configuration identities, and enough observed metrics for the selected objective. Explicitly classify failed, timed-out, skipped-required, partial, missing-report and incompatible variants.
2. Define required versus optional suite members. An optional backend unsupported for the whole experiment may be excluded by an explicit common-workload policy; do not reward a variant for omitting work that another executed. Report the measured denominator and exclusions.
3. Retain the actual structured report when a child exits nonzero, together with child exit/signal/status and parsing errors. Do not replace a present report with synthetic empty results. Never treat a successful JSON parse as process success.
4. If no variant is eligible, emit recommendation:null with a machine-readable insufficient/failed-experiment outcome and an appropriate failing CLI status. Do not label the least-bad failed configuration as recommended.
5. Record requested and effective knob receipts. Some scripts do not consume every knob, so distinguish applied, unsupported and unverified settings rather than claiming all matrix points represent different effective workloads.
6. Make the objective explicit and versioned. Missing stall or utilization is not zero; only use optional terms under a declared common comparison policy. Token occupancy is not hardware CPU efficiency. Prefer duration/work-completion goals and hard correctness/resource constraints over automatically rewarding busy CPUs.
7. Keep reports bounded and reuse existing benchmark metadata and status contracts; this does not require a new benchmarking framework or expensive repeated model/corpus runs.

## Small discriminating tests
- Supply independent reports for an equivalent slow success and a very fast failure; the failure must never win, regardless of duration or penalty magnitude.
- All failed, all required-skipped, missing required metrics, malformed/missing report and workload-mismatch matrices produce no recommendation with exact eligibility reasons.
- A tiny fixture exits nonzero; bench-runner then writes its report before returning failure. Assert its actual failed-script details survive in the sweep receipt, not error:1/results:[] substitution.
- A tiny knob-aware fixture reports applied settings and a deliberately known ranking with equal work/correctness. Assert the known winner and eligible denominator, not just a truthy bestConfig.
- Optional unsupported work is comparable only under the explicitly selected common-workload policy; one-sided missing work cannot win.
- Preserve the existing successful plumbing test and test-gated environment path.

## Related work and audit limits
#1648 fixes utilization units; #1649 fixes failure-to-skip classification upstream. Neither makes incomplete runs eligible for optimization. #1625 concerns production scheduler autotune, not this offline A/B sweep. #689's current checker now preserves omitted thresholds and missing values; reuse that principle rather than reverting it here. Searches for ab-sweep/recommendation/benchmark owners found no matching eligibility owner. No implementation, tests, benchmark or project process was run.

## Current reproducibility defect

The live judged-evaluation report records requested settings and file paths but discards the execution identity already returned by retrieval. It also omits the selected matching mode, even though that changes the meaning of a relevance hit. As a result the saved report cannot distinguish materially different retrieval experiments or establish that its macro average describes one corpus/configuration generation.

Source-only audit of PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; no model, search, test or benchmark was run. This does not assert the current metric arithmetic is wrong.

### Evidence
- [tools/eval/run.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L63-L78) requests JSON and optional requested backend/ANN flags, then returns the full core payload. [The results loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L98-L124) retains counts and metrics only. [The final report](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L154-L167) records backend from argv (often auto), ann from the requested flag, repo/dataset paths and policy strings, not the observed retrieval backend, fallback/fidelity, generation or cache evidence.
- Retrieval already [constructs a receipt before optional stats](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/render.js#L370-L405). [buildRetrievalMetadata](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/output/retrieval-metadata.js#L79-L116) exposes selected/requested backend, selection reason, fallback-derived status, per-mode freshness and cache facts. [Freshness includes build ID, artifact surface version, profile and signature](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/output/retrieval-metadata.js#L31-L49). These should not be lost at this consumer.
- The runner [resolves matchMode and uses it](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L46-L61), but never emits it. [exact versus substring matching](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/match.js#L21-L28) gives different relevance for a name such as greet versus greeting while both reports advertise the same relevancePolicy. A dataset pathname is likewise not the identity of its selected queries and judgments.
- Each core call invokes a new search request. The current search implementation correctly [pins all possible mode joins before its first request await](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/run-search/plan-runner.js#L323-L368), so this is **not** a claim of within-request pointer drift. However, eval starts another request for every case and neither pins a run-wide generation nor compares/retains observed per-case identities. A publication or effective config change between cases can therefore go unreported in the aggregate.
- Current [response-admission tests](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/eval/response-evidence-admission.test.js#L65-L96) use the actual runner to reject missing/failed/omitted-hit outcomes and preserve explicit empty results, with cleanup before publication. Credit and retain these repairs. They do not assert backend/generation/matching-policy provenance in saved output.

## Fix at the report boundary
1. Capture a compact versioned per-case execution receipt from the actual search result: selected modes, requested versus observed backend, fallback/fidelity and bounded reason, source/index generation and profile/signature identity. Do not copy arbitrary diagnostics or whole index metadata into each result.
2. Add actual ANN/exact/dense execution coverage where needed for claims about that route, rather than treating --ann as proof of use. Reuse the retrieval owner's observed state; do not infer actual execution from installation/configuration.
3. Bind selected ordered cases/queries/judgments, matchMode, cutoff policy and metric version to an immutable evaluation-input identity. Keep the human-friendly path, but do not use it as content identity.
4. Define a run consistency policy. Prefer an existing retained/pinned generation mechanism for a controlled run where supported; otherwise preserve each case's generation and mark/partition mixed-generation or configuration results explicitly. Do not present an unqualified single-system macro average after silently changing the evaluated system.
5. Keep exploratory descriptive scores possible with an explicit unqualified/unknown provenance outcome. Missing identity is not a numerical zero or proof of reproducibility, and such reports must not satisfy a strict comparison or regression gate. Historical/replay sections retain their existing separate evidence scope.
6. Use bounded interning of repeated receipts so a long query set does not duplicate large metadata. Preserve passive admission and immutable captured scalars; do not execute getters or reread mutable dataset objects after awaits.

## Small discriminating acceptance tests
- Feed the actual runner identical hits with auto->memory and auto->sqlite observed receipts. Scores may match, but saved execution identities and backend descriptions must differ.
- Provide a successful fallback-derived payload and ensure the report preserves that fact; a requested backend or ANN flag cannot upgrade it to qualified primary-backend evidence.
- Two queries with stable generation produce a qualified common identity. A second query with a new generation/configuration is rejected for strict comparison or explicitly mixed/partitioned, without losing either observation.
- Same path with different selected labels/query text yields a different evaluation-input identity. exact and substring matching always produce distinct recorded matching policies even when this particular dataset happens to score equally.
- Missing generation/route evidence yields explicit unqualified reasons while preserving already-admitted numerical observations. It cannot be admitted by a strict comparison consumer.
- Keep existing empty-hit, output-budget, cohort and cleanup tests. Add a tiny real retrieval-adapter receipt handoff witness where practical, not an expensive model/corpus campaign.

## Deduplication
#632 owns representative qualification; this is its concrete existing live-report provenance handoff. #1441 owns stale bakeoff resume, #1641 cutoff depth, #1440 mode projection, and #1119/#1120 saved oracle/fusion evidence. Those are not substitutes for retaining the observed system identity of newly issued live judged queries. The current model-comparison corpus mismatch guard and current per-request mode-root pinning are positive controls, not regressions asserted here.

Metric-coverage addition for the same live-report receipt boundary, verified at `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523` without execution:

[The current reducer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/run.js#L100-L151) correctly leaves an unjudged cohort's metrics null and averages only judged cohorts/cases. Gold metrics are calculated per case/cohort but have no top-level summary or eligible count. A ten-case report with only one judged case therefore advertises cases10 alongside metrics computed from one case unless a consumer rederives coverage from every result.

This matters at the existing bakeoff handoff: [only evalReport.summary is retained](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L825-L842), losing the per-case judged/unjudged and gold coverage. Preserve null/unknown through bakeoff retention/rendering; display n/a with a bounded reason rather than0 when no measurement exists. A strict quality gate should declare required judgment coverage rather than infer it from total searched cases. Supporting gold-only exploratory data does not require silently selecting it as silver; label the chosen evidence tier explicitly.

Small reducer/consumer controls: one judged + nine unjudged cases; mixed judged modes within a case; gold-only labels; explicit zero-hit judged search; all-unjudged; --skip-eval; and a legitimate measured zero. Assert both exact score and denominator/availability after the actual bakeoff projection, not just in the standalone metric helper. This is receipt/consumer correctness, not a request to penalize unlabeled cases numerically or redefine the current cohort macro.

## Source-verified defect

The embedding bakeoff's explicit no-sampling option does not override an inherited sampling environment. The report can say embeddingSampleFiles:0 / profile:full while the child still embeds only a positive sampled subset.

Audited PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; no build, inference, model download, benchmark or test was executed.

### Reachable path
1. [Fast-path resolution](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff-lib.js#L129-L149) correctly resolves --full-run to embeddingSampleFiles:0 and honors explicit --embedding-sample-files 0. [bootstrapRuntime](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/dict-utils.js#L92-L98) starts from process.env, and [runtime environment patching](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/runtime-envelope/env-patch.js) preserves unrelated inherited variables.

With an inherited positive value such as 7, an explicit zero leaves 7 intact.

[The production sampling resolver](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/build/embeddings/runner.js#L965-L976) prefers a finite environment sample limit over configuration; [the normal embedding path](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/build/embeddings/runner.js#L2220-L2251) actually selects that limited file set when it is smaller than the corpus.

[outputSettings](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L521-L542) records the resolved CLI/profile zero, not the effective inherited limit. The requested/report value is zero; the constructed child environment still carries 7. No hypothetical malformed input is required.

## Repair boundary

- Resolve/freeze one small plan used for child launch, report and resume compatibility, rather than reporting CLI defaults separately from inherited execution. Reuse the existing embedding execution-plan owner.

1. Pure resolver -> real child-plan/environment construction -> actual production sampling resolver: inherited 7 plus explicit zero must produce disabled sampling; assert the final plan and effective limit, not only the CLI field.
2. Same inherited state plus --full-run without an explicit positive override follows the documented no-sampling default.
3. Full-run plus explicit positive 3 remains sampled at 3 with the requested seed. Ordinary quick defaults remain 50.
4. A three-file, test-gated stub fixture with inherited limit1 and explicit zero retains all three eligible files in the sampling receipt; positive1 retains one. Independently assert selected identities/counts, not merely a log or a truthy success.
5. Report, checkpoint and child execution agree on effective sampling. Changed inherited state cannot leave two materially different experiments with the same claimed sampling configuration.

The same bakeoff constructs per-model build/eval environments with PAIROFCLEATS_EMBEDDINGS=stub when --stub-embeddings is selected ([toModelEnv](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L328-L342)). Add a tiny child-launch seam asserting build, eval and compare receive the same selected stub intent, plus a negative control that disallows invoking a real provider.
