## Source-verified report ownership defects

Current benchmark artifacts are addressed by shared mutable names rather than an invocation identity. This can overwrite prior evidence, mix concurrent A/B measurements, and destroy a reusable bakeoff checkpoint during an interrupted write.

Audited PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. These are source-derived schedules; no concurrent process, interrupted write, benchmark or test was executed.

### A/B sweep: every invocation shares the same per-variant report names
- [main](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L247-L267) always uses ROOT/.testLogs/bench-ab-sweep, and [runVariant](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/ab-sweep.js#L170-L179) names children run-001.json, run-002.json, etc.
- The parent reads the child path after completion and associates it with its own current variant without a run/variant receipt check. Two ordinary invocations from the same checkout can write the same file. A can finish its child, B overwrite run-001.json, then A read B's payload and score it as A's configuration.
- Even sequential runs overwrite the paths advertised by older saved sweep reports, so reportPath no longer denotes the raw evidence for that historical recommendation.
- This remains after #1655 fixes failure eligibility and reading the actual failed report.

### Bakeoff: mutable checkpoint publication has neither atomicity nor an owner fence
- [Default checkpoint selection](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L202-L208) uses one .testLogs/embedding-bakeoff.latest.json path; explicit --checkpoint/--out can also be shared.
- [Every phase/model/final publication](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L619-L640) writes through writeJsonFileResolved. [That helper](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/json-file.js#L13-L20) ultimately calls fs.writeFile on the destination, not a temp-file atomic replacement. An interruption after truncation can lose the last complete resume checkpoint.
- [Resume parsing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/embeddings/model-bakeoff.js#L658-L679) catches all read/parse failures and starts with no resumed models. Thus a torn checkpoint can trigger expensive repeated work instead of retaining the previous completed entries and an explicit unreadable-checkpoint outcome.
- Concurrent writers can also replace each other's phase/completion state. The per-index build lock does not own this report path across separate model caches or between subprocess phases.

## Repair through existing persistence owners
1. Allocate a unique invocation directory and immutable experiment/run ID. Per-variant files belong beneath it; include run ID, variant ID and workload/config identity in both child receipt and parent admission. Reject an unrelated receipt even if its filename looks expected.
2. Retain immutable raw reports referenced by saved recommendations. A latest convenience pointer may change, but historical reportPath must remain bound to its original bytes or content digest.
3. Publish checkpoints atomically through the existing atomic-write owner, retaining the prior complete checkpoint if serialization/write/rename fails. Do not globally change every generic JSON writer without auditing those callers.
4. Define checkpoint writer ownership: unique per-invocation checkpoints plus an explicit compatible resume/import path, or a lease/lock/CAS revision for an intentionally shared checkpoint. Do not use a stale read plus unconditional overwrite as merge/ownership.
5. Make corruption, incompatible identity, active other writer and absent checkpoint distinct. Historical successful entries should not silently disappear into a generic empty resume result; report the problem without fabricating work completion.
6. Keep cleanup scoped to settled owned invocation artifacts and coordinate existing storage retention policy. No global benchmark directory deletion or unbounded permanent accumulation.

## Small independent acceptance
- Interleave two tiny sweeps at child-write/parent-read barriers. Each parent must consume only its own receipt and retain its original raw files.
- Run a second sweep sequentially; all paths/digests in the first saved report still resolve to its original evidence.
- Inject failure between temp write and publish; the previous bakeoff checkpoint remains complete and parseable. Truncation/partial content is never admitted as a normal empty checkpoint.
- Two writers targeting the same explicit checkpoint are serialized or receive an explicit ownership conflict; late A cannot replace newer B under stale ownership.
- Test unique-run cleanup, cancelled/failed terminal reports and valid unchanged resume without expensive corpus/model execution.

## Deduplication
#607 is service-queue artifact cleanup across partitions; #875 is build-state drain; #897 is checkpoint-index sidecar commit; #821 is triage's JSON/Markdown pair. This owns benchmark invocation/report namespace and bakeoff checkpoint publication. Coordinate #1441 input validity, #1655 sweep eligibility and #1661 phase lifecycle rather than duplicating their logic.

## Current failure and cost paths

Source-traced at PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; no canary/benchmark process was executed.

[runBenchRuntimeLiveCanary](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/canaries.js#L589-L681) bypasses the existing bounded subprocess output owner and leaves payload admission outside its attempt cleanup boundary:

1. Lines 597–610 push every stdout/stderr callback chunk into unbounded arrays. The shared [async runner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/runner-async.js#L297-L305) sends the whole stream to callbacks even though its own [collector](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/options.js#L135-L204) correctly retains only a bounded tail and records dropped-byte/encoding evidence. The canary therefore retains all output in addition to the shared capture. Joining the arrays and serializing the returned full streams adds further peak copies. The five-minute timeout is not a byte bound.
2. Lines 632–640 read the entire result artifact and parse JSON outside the spawn try/catch. A child can exit successfully after leaving a malformed/truncated JSON artifact, or an artifact read can fail. That exception bypasses the removal at line 654 and never becomes a structured per-canary outcome. The [CLI's serial loop](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language-canaries.js#L37-L78) then exits through its top-level catch without writing the accumulated summary; previously completed results and subsequent selected canaries have no terminal report.
3. The spawn catch at lines 612–627 always removes the temporary work directory and keeps only an error message. The repaired [subprocess termination owner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/subprocess/runner-async.js#L79-L117) can reject with `cacheOwnershipPending` and a qualified termination receipt when actual close is not yet observed or tree cleanup failed. The canary drops that distinction and releases its attempt work path before the child owner's release is established. This is not a claim that normal timeout rejection leaves children alive: the current shared owner already waits for escalation and bounded close, and that behavior must be preserved.

## Fix architecture

- Make one attempt scope own process execution, bounded diagnostic capture, result-artifact admission, parse/contract evaluation and temporary-directory lifetime.
- Reuse the shared bounded capture and its receipts instead of keeping unlimited callback arrays. If live streaming is desired, forward bounded frames without retaining them, or spool diagnostics to a run-owned bounded artifact. Report observed/retained/dropped bytes and whether diagnostics are incomplete.
- Bound result-artifact bytes before/full-during admission using the existing contained/bounded reader; schema/parse/read failures become explicit non-closure-ready per-canary outcomes. A valid separately bounded result artifact may still be authoritative when diagnostic logs were truncated; truncation must not automatically invalidate independent complete evidence, nor turn a log tail into complete metrics.
- Put cleanup in an ownership-aware finalization path. Preserve pending termination evidence and retain/quarantine the owned temporary path until the existing child owner releases it. Do not defeat pending ownership with an unconditional `finally rm`.
- Define whether cancellation stops the remaining lane, versus a malformed individual result allowing later entries to run. In either case atomically publish the completed/failed/interrupted coverage already observed, not a success-looking partial lane or no report.
- Preserve current fail-closed nonzero/signal/timeout behavior: the async subprocess default rejects these already. Do not introduce a new process supervisor or replace the shared cleanup machinery.

## Small discriminating tests and performance acceptance

The current [runner test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/bench/bench-runtime-live-canary-runner.test.js#L13-L47) covers successful fixture baseline outcomes. Add bounded fixture cases for:
- output many times larger than the capture cap, including stderr and a split multibyte sequence: retained report/log bytes remain O(configured cap), counts expose truncation, and a valid bounded result is still evaluated correctly;
- exit zero with malformed, oversized or unreadable result JSON: typed failed outcome, no closure, completed earlier rows retained and selected-unrun rows explicitly accounted for;
- normal timeout versus a controlled shared-runner rejection with unconfirmed close: retain the latter's lifetime receipt/path until exact release, then clean up once; an unrelated run's directory is never removed;
- one valid result as a positive control.

Use tiny deterministic children/controlled lifetime fixtures, not real repositories or a full benchmark campaign. Check bounded retained bytes and operation counts rather than fragile process-RSS thresholds.

## Ownership / deduplication

#385 owns whether canary evidence proves a production blocker improved; #1651 owns effective child environment identity; #677 owns the shared subprocess contract. Those are not substitutes for this concrete canary consumer's unbounded storage and unsettled attempt-result/resource lifecycle. Existing #357/#378 replay/live-harness infrastructure is credited, not requested again.

## Existing query-list consumers can evaluate a different workload from the requested one

Source-only audit of PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; no query, parity gate or model comparison was executed.

### 1. JSON entries are silently coerced into unrelated queries

[normalizeJsonEntries](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/shared/query-file-utils.js#L11-L30) uses `String(entry)` in its default/stringify mode. [compare-models](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/compare-models.js#L263-L276) and [memory/SQLite parity](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L182-L194) explicitly select that mode.

A JSON list such as `[{ "query": "greet" }, { "query": "clamp" }]` becomes two identical `"[object Object]"` searches. Null/boolean/numeric entries likewise become `"null"`, `"false"`, etc., and JSON whitespace strings remain admitted. The helper has a separate query-field mode, but these consumers do not use it. This is not a claim that object-form lists are promised by the comparison docs: unsupported input must be rejected, not accepted as a different workload. The repository's judged evaluation datasets do use query-bearing objects, making accidental reuse a plausible operator path.

### 2. An explicitly selected invalid parity file silently falls back

[readQueryFileSafe](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/shared/query-file-utils.js#L61-L74) turns every read/JSON parse error into an empty array. The parity runner correctly [rejects a nonexistent explicit path](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L163-L168), but an existing malformed/unreadable/empty explicit file reaches [the fallback query list](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L169-L185). It only prints a warning and then runs/enforces a different set. [The report](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L338-L345) still names the requested queryFile; it has no structured requested-versus-effective source/fallback disposition. This can produce a successful parity gate for fallback words rather than the intended regression cases.

The current consumers retain ordered result rows, so this is **not** a claim of a Map overwriting duplicate query strings. Coercion can nevertheless collapse distinct intended tasks into repeated identical requests and distort weighting/cache warmth.

## One shared admission owner

- Replace coercive query parsing with a small versioned admitted query-plan contract used by comparison, parity and benchmark consumers. Support documented string lists/text lines and, if intentionally supported, explicit query-field records. Reject other JSON shapes and blank queries with path/entry-index diagnostics before expensive index/model work.
- Distinguish absent optional default input, explicit input failure, and a deliberately selected fallback plan. An explicit malformed/unreadable/empty file must fail closed by default. A fallback, if requested, must be a different named effective plan and cannot certify the requested file.
- Freeze the actual ordered selected requests, normalization policy, limit and source-content identity once. Preserve deliberate repeats through stable case/occurrence identity and report their weights; do not silently deduplicate or merge same-text cases across modes/filters.
- Reuse #1658's evaluation-input receipt format where appropriate and retain the human-readable filename separately. Avoid creating another result store or another parser per command.
- Preserve useful default smoke fallback only under its explicit policy, with machine-readable provenance; do not remove the current missing-explicit-path guard.

## Small independent acceptance

1. Two JSON query objects are either intentionally admitted as greet/clamp or rejected before any child search; neither may become object-string queries.
2. Null, booleans, numeric entries, whitespace-only strings, malformed JSON, empty arrays and unsupported top-level objects have explicit outcomes.
3. An existing invalid explicit --queries file cannot run fallback words or pass --enforce. The report/exit identifies the input failure; no model work is launched.
4. A valid text/JSON string list, including a literal string `"[object Object]"`, preserves its intended text. Deliberate repeats remain distinguishable occurrences with explicit weighting rather than accidental identity collisions.
5. An explicitly permitted missing-default fallback records the actual effective set and source policy. Same path changed contents and different selected limits change the workload identity.

All can use a tiny query-recording child or argument-plan seam. No corpus, model download or benchmark campaign is required.

## Dedupe

#1658 owns observed live evaluation execution/judgment identity; #713 owns corpus-qualified hit comparison; #749 owns duplicate **hit** metric keys. This issue is the earlier query-file admission/fallback boundary shared by the existing comparison and parity tools.

## Missing retrieval results can become perfect parity

At PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the memory/SQLite parity harness admits a zero-exit JSON object as a search result without validating the requested result cohorts or hit-retention evidence.

- [The CLI harness](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/shared/search-cli-harness.js#L151-L208) correctly rejects nonzero/signal exits and invalid JSON, but JSON parse success alone is not a successful retrieval response contract.
- [Parity result projection](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L251-L274) uses `memPayload.code || []` and equivalent fallbacks for both code/prose sides. A missing/null cohort becomes an explicit empty list.
- [summarizeMatch](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L228-L244) opts into `treatBothEmptyAsPerfect:true`. The shared [summary helper](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/hit-comparison.js#L118-L135) therefore returns overlap1 for those synthesized empty lists.
- [Aggregation/enforcement](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L289-L319) averages these scores; [the gate](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L355-L390) accepts overlap1, delta0 and null rank correlation. A zero-exit child returning `{}` for each backend can therefore pass the parity thresholds without returning either requested cohort. A response explicitly carrying `ok:false` with no arrays takes the same route.
- The same projection does not inspect `outputBudget.omittedHits`, so a hit-truncated response can be scored as a complete backend ranking. It also drops the comparison helper's `comparable`/unknown-identity qualification from the projected summary.

This is a source-derived harness counterexample, not a claim that ordinary production search currently emits `{}`, nor a claim an actual parity run passed falsely.

## Reuse the repaired admission boundary

The live judged evaluator already [requires successful response status, explicit selected arrays, dense hit rows and exact output hit-retention evidence](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/eval/cohorts.js#L19-L44). Preserve this repair and adopt a shared small retrieval-result admission owner for parity and comparison, without importing labels or a cross-mode scoring policy into the parity helper.

1. Build the requested canonical mode/cohort plan and require each selected array explicitly. Missing/failed/malformed outcomes are unavailable, never fabricated zero-hit successes.
2. Keep a legitimate explicit empty result distinct. Both-empty parity can remain descriptive under the declared policy, but report its zero-hit coverage separately from positive-hit witness coverage.
3. Require complete hit-retention evidence for an underlying top-window parity claim. If deliberately comparing delivered/truncated responses, label that different estimand and do not certify full backend parity.
4. Preserve stable-identity comparability/unknown counts from the shared hit owner and count unavailable comparisons separately. Strict enforcement cannot pass with absent required observations.
5. Qualify the actual observed backend/fallback/generation receipt, not only requested CLI flags, using the shared receipt work in #1658/#713. Two fallback-memory responses must not be labeled an observed memory-versus-SQLite experiment.
6. Apply the same admission to [compare-models' Array.isArray-or-empty projection](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/compare-models.js#L323-L335), which also otherwise normalizes missing arrays and absent timing evidence into ordinary report values. Its valid preflight corpus guard does not validate the child's response outcome.

## Focused tests

Use the existing configurable search-child seam or the shared harness injection, with tiny authored stable-ID responses:
- valid explicit empty arrays on both sides: admitted zero-hit parity with zero-hit coverage, not a missing-response failure;
- missing/null/non-array selected cohort, `ok:false`, malformed row, or omitted-hit receipt on either side: unavailable/failure and nonzero strict gate, never perfect parity;
- valid stable positive-hit controls plus deliberate one-side ranking difference: correctly pass/fail thresholds;
- unknown hit identity: preserve incomparable, not an ordinary numeric quality score;
- requested SQLite but observed fallback-memory receipt: no qualified cross-backend pass;
- mixed valid and unavailable queries: retain every row and exact eligible/unknown denominators rather than averaging only convenient successes.

Do not weaken current nonzero/signal/JSON handling or the repaired stable distinct-hit comparison. No actual project, backend or model execution was used in this audit.

## Deduplication

#749 owns duplicate hit-key arithmetic; #713 owns stable corpus/generation comparison; #1668 owns query-file admission; #683 owns a different language-rollout report gate. This issue is the concrete retrieval response-to-parity admission defect and shared consumer repair, not a new parity framework.

## Score-delta reports conflate unavailable measurements and incompatible score spaces

Current PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, source inspection only.

[resolveRetrievalHitScore](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/hit-comparison.js#L20-L32) silently selects the first finite value from `score`, `scoreBreakdown.selected.score`, `sparseScore`, or `annScore`, then returns0 if none exists. It returns no source-stage/type/space identity. [compareRetrievalHitLists](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/hit-comparison.js#L73-L76) subtracts those values for shared hits and returns avgDelta0 when there are no shared hits.

Consequences at existing consumers:
- Two stable matching hits with no observed score are reported as zero score difference, not missing evidence.
- Disjoint hit lists also report avgDelta0 despite having zero paired score observations.
- One side's final/model/fused score can be subtracted from the other's fallback sparse or raw ANN value without a compatible score-domain check.
- [compare-models](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/compare-models.js#L407-L430) averages those deltas as scoreDeltaAvg across queries/models. [Parity enforcement](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L289-L307) and [its max-delta gate](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/retrieval/parity/equivalence.test.js#L355-L378) consume the same unqualified number. Fixing result-array admission in #1669 does not supply score evidence for otherwise valid hits.

Equal corpus identity or a common numeric range does not establish equivalent scoring policy. Production already distinguishes [raw sparse, raw ANN, RRF and blended outputs](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/pipeline/fusion.js#L79-L144), including active-channel weights and metric-specific ANN calibration. Pure dense mode intentionally preserves raw provider ordering. Those repairs are valuable; this issue is not a request to replace the production calibration, nor to change model rankings until their numbers happen to match.

## Shared metric admission, not another ranking algorithm

1. Return a qualified score observation: finite value plus authoritative stage/type and available model/metric/normalization/calibration/fusion policy identity. Missing is null/unknown, not0. Do not silently substitute a different score component unless the comparison explicitly selects that component.
2. Admit numerical deltas only under a declared compatible score-space policy. A descriptive cross-model raw-score difference may remain available if explicitly labeled with both spaces; it must not be presented as calibrated relevance disagreement or reused as a parity tolerance without that contract.
3. Keep rank/membership comparison independent. Monotone score rescaling can preserve rank exactly while changing numerical deltas; no claim of relevance loss follows without judged evidence.
4. Expose paired-score count, missing/incompatible counts and aggregation unit. Zero pairs means unavailable delta, not measured equality. Distinguish query-macro from pooled matched-hit averages so a one-shared-hit query does not silently carry the same assumed evidence as a full window.
5. Preserve null through summaries/human formatting and make strict max-delta enforcement require its declared measurement coverage, not skip missing observations as healthy. Reuse existing score receipts/explanation owners, avoiding per-hit unbounded metadata copies.

## Discriminating tests

- Same stable identity with score0 on both sides is valid measured delta0; missing scores on either/both sides are not.
- Empty intersection yields no paired score delta and an explicit count0.
- One final-score observation versus one fallback sparse/ANN-only observation is incomparable unless that exact component pairing was requested.
- Same scores with conflicting score type/model/calibration identity cannot satisfy strict numerical parity.
- Known compatible same-model backend scores preserve the current absolute-delta calculation.
- A monotone-rescaled two-hit ranking retains perfect rank agreement while the score report honestly exposes its different space; no false quality conclusion.
- Actual model-report and parity reducers preserve missingness and counts; do not test only the scalar resolver.

These can be tiny offline hit fixtures and consumer seams. No model, ANN/native backend, search or test execution was performed by this audit.

## Dedupe

#685 owns metric-aware production ANN fusion (current code credited), #1570 owns sign-unsafe boosts, #1576 owns stale final-score explanations, #713/#749 own hit identity and duplicate arithmetic, and #1669 owns response admission. This is their shared comparison consumer's score-domain/measurement-support boundary.

## Generated “adversarial” queries do not exercise their authored Boolean operations

Source-derived at PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; no generator, query parser or benchmark was executed.

[formatQueryValue](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/query-generator.js#L187-L192) escapes quotes/backslashes and wraps **any complete value containing whitespace** in double quotes. [The strategy builder](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/query-generator.js#L301-L344) passes entire compound query expressions through it:

- API adversarial OR: `maybeJoin(apiHint, 'OR', name)` becomes e.g. `"middleware OR createRouter"`. The production [lexer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/query.js#L75-L98) reads this as one phrase, not an OR node.
- Symbol adversarial exclusion: `name + ' -' + riskTag` becomes e.g. `"createRouter -retry"`, again one phrase rather than an included name and excluded term.
- Type/API/behavior strategies that insert their own quotes are escaped and wrapped a second time. The current phrase lexer terminates at the next matching quote without treating backslash as an escape; this formatting does not round-trip the author's compound expression through that grammar.

A row is still labeled `variant:"adversarial"`, and the generated corpus records/counts that label. It may exercise phrase/lexical behavior, but the apparent Boolean stress is not established by the emitted query.

[The current test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/query-generator-language-family.test.js) asserts count, family weights, nonzero adversarial labels and deterministic string output. It never parses the generated strings or checks independent expected Boolean eligibility, so this semantic mismatch is invisible.

## Narrow repair

- Represent the generator's intended query structure separately from literal values. Quote/escape leaves according to the actual public query grammar; compose OR/negation/phrase nodes outside those leaf quotes. Do not pass a finished Boolean expression through a literal-value formatter.
- Validate generated query semantics with the production parser before publishing the workload, and retain a compact intended/observed query-shape class in generation metadata. If an intentionally literal phrase includes OR or a hyphen, label it as that, not as proof of Boolean-operator coverage.
- Align escaping with the parser's supported grammar. Unsupported literal quote/backslash cases must be explicitly rejected or represented by a supported form, not silently changed into a different parse.
- Keep existing deterministic seed/weight behavior and bounded generation; no new parser or external query-building dependency is needed.

## Discriminating acceptance

Using a tiny independently authored candidate fixture:
1. The OR strategy produces an OR AST with the intended two leaves, and admits either branch in a three-document eligibility witness.
2. The exclusion strategy contains the intended NOT leaf; a document with the excluded token is rejected while the positive control remains eligible.
3. Literal phrase controls containing the text OR or a hyphen remain phrases when intentionally requested.
4. Quotes/backslashes, dotted symbol names and signatures containing parentheses either round-trip to the intended supported query or produce explicit generation rejection.
5. Fixed seed still yields deterministic output, but tests also assert actual operator/phrase distribution and semantics, not only the generator's self-assigned `variant` field.

No model, backend or full corpus is needed. This is generator-to-parser contract coverage, not a claim that retrieval's Boolean evaluator is wrong.

## Scope / dedupe

#1668 owns admission of user-selected query files; #632 owns representative workload evidence. This issue is the current query producer changing its own intended operators into literal text. Existing production query grammar and eligibility owners should be reused, not replaced.

## Current defect

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the benchmark computes safe query-worker plans separately for each backend, then executes every plan concurrently. The aggregate run therefore does not obey the resource plan shown to the user.

- [runQueries calls resolveAdaptiveQueryWorkerCount with backends:[backend] for every backend](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L560-L585), giving each call the same requested concurrency and its own full host-memory allowance.
- [The planner explicitly computes a 40%-of-host budget and remainingBudget/remainingRequested](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/query-runtime.js#L109-L170), but these counters cannot constrain sibling calls.
- [All backend pools run concurrently](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L660-L674). With enough small queries/artifacts, requested concurrency 4 creates memory 4 + sqlite 1; [the report records max(pool sizes)=4, not aggregate 5](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L697-L708). The default selects both backends.
- The memory issue is not just terminology: under the current estimates an 8 GiB host with 400 MiB memory artifacts and 4 GiB SQLite files independently admits memory 3 (~3000 MiB estimated) and SQLite 1 (~3072 MiB), against each plan's ~3276 MiB budget. Their simultaneous combined estimate is ~6072 MiB. This is source arithmetic, not measured RSS or an observed OOM.
- Policy classification also diverges: [backend selection treats sqlite, sqlite-fts and fts as SQLite](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/query-backends.js#L1-L5), but sizing recognizes only the sqlite prefix, [serialization only exact sqlite](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L281-L296), and [retirement only exact sqlite](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L587-L594). The accepted fts alias can therefore receive the no_query_backends plan with no SQLite byte estimate.

## Fix boundary

1. Resolve one explicit experiment execution plan across every selected backend and canonical resource class. It must contain aggregate concurrency/memory estimate, each pool's allocation, sharing/isolation assumptions and retirement policy.
2. Decide and document whether the CLI concurrency is global or per-backend. If per-backend is intentionally retained, still enforce an independent aggregate resource ceiling and report both quantities honestly. Do not keep calling one backend's maximum the whole run's effective concurrency.
3. Reuse the existing planner/pool owners, including backend-group support, rather than create another scheduler. Merely passing all backends to the helper is not sufficient: its minimum-one-per-backend fallback can still exceed a requested budget of 1. Stage backend work sequentially when simultaneous minimum capacity cannot fit, or emit a qualified oversize/unsupported plan; do not silently drop a backend.
4. Canonicalize aliases once and explicitly identify whether sqlite-fts deliberately needs a different lifecycle. Do not accidentally disable a safety policy based on spelling. Preserve current empty-mode admission and query coverage receipts.
5. Keep estimates labeled estimates. Retain configured/requested, planned and observed active counts; a memory estimator is not a hard guarantee about actual RSS.

## Discriminating acceptance

- Test the actual run-plan composition, not only the helper with a combined backend list. Default memory+sqlite, all backends, aliases, one backend and concurrency 1/4 must agree with their aggregate receipt.
- Use instrumented fake workers with a barrier to independently count simultaneous workers and starts. With a global limit 1, both requested backends eventually execute but never overlap.
- Deterministic byte inputs reproduce the budget example above; allocations are admitted against one shared allowance, with explicit behavior when one required worker alone is oversize.
- Preserve existing generation ownership, close/queued-request settlement and worker recycling tests. The current [query-runtime.test.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/query-runtime.test.js#L24-L87) already checks the combined helper and omitted-vs-zero artifact sizing; add the missing caller composition witness.
- A tiny bounded run should retain per-backend and aggregate active counts plus peak process-tree RSS, without claiming a throughput improvement or increasing caps to hide the mismatch.

Dedup: #106's generation-safe callback/retirement repair is present and is not reopened. #632 owns experiment representativeness and warm/cold interpretation; #1648 owns telemetry units/clock semantics. All-state query-worker, adaptive-query and benchmark-memory searches found no current aggregate-plan owner. Source audit only; no project execution or implementation.

## Current evidence and limitation

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, the language report turns an unjudged nonempty-result statistic into ranked recall/ranker remediation. The report correctly leaves suggestions unaccepted; this is not a claim of automatic production tuning. The defect is the evidence and causal meaning assigned to its recommendations.

- [The benchmark defines hitRate as searches returning any code/prose result](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L640-L656), divided by the selected query count. It does not compare those results to relevant targets or expected-empty judgments. #1440 separately owns its missing extracted-prose projection.
- [computeLowHitSeverity](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/regression.js#L49-L110) takes the best backend's nonempty frequency, average result count, and queryWallMsPerSearch. No query-intent expectation, judgment coverage or measured retrieval-stage attribution enters the severity.
- [buildRankedRemediationSuggestions](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1150-L1228) always proposes rebalancing intent weights for a low-hit repository, targeting the query generator and benchmark repository configuration while labeling the component ranker. It calls low result density sparse recall, attributes it to tokenizer/chunk boundaries, and advises tightening rerank depth based on query/search latency.
- That alleged latency is [total concurrent batch wall time divided by all searches](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/run.test.js#L660-L678), including pool setup/teardown. It is amortized wall cost/inverse throughput, not an individual query's latency or rerank time. Changing concurrency alone can change this recommendation without any query getting faster.
- [Miss-taxonomy labels are attached after suggestions are calculated](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1265-L1307), not used to establish the proposed cause. The existing [report fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/reports/bench-language-low-hit-remediation-report.test.js#L88-L142) checks suggestion existence/order, not diagnostic discrimination.

Consequences follow directly from these definitions: an intentionally no-match workload can be called low-recall; arbitrary irrelevant results improve hitRate; changing the generated intent mix can improve the reported baseline without changing retrieval. These are counterexamples to the inference, not claims that a measured production repository has suffered those outcomes.

## Repair within the current report/fixture owners

1. Keep nonempty-result frequency as a useful availability/smoke metric, explicitly named and scoped. Do not relabel it recall or relevance. Preserve unknown expected outcomes separately from known positives and expected negatives.
2. Separate diagnostic hypotheses from evidence-backed recommendations. A low unjudged hit rate may suggest inspecting workload validity, coverage or query parsing; it cannot by itself rank a tokenizer, chunking or rerank change as the established remedy. Retain evidence, contradicted/missing evidence, applicability and reason for abstention.
3. If changing the benchmark generator/intent weights is proposed, classify it as workload design, not a retrieval improvement. Version the changed workload, freeze an independent matched holdout, and do not call the changed-denominator result a post-change quality gain.
4. Use selected backend/mode and query-stratum observations rather than collapsing to the maximum backend hit rate. Admit comparable outcomes/coverage before suggesting a backend-specific remedy.
5. Use actual per-query response/service latency or measured rerank-stage cost for latency recommendations, with cache/concurrency scope from #632 and aggregate execution admission from #1675. Keep batch wall-per-completion as throughput cost, not a substitute for latency.
6. Scores must be labeled heuristic priorities unless calibrated evidence exists. Continue the present explicit unaccepted/pending loop; do not turn this issue into automatic tuning or a requirement to judge every throughput-only query.
7. Make taxonomy counts honest: [the current projection adds lowHitByBackend and byBackend](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1231-L1262), although low-hit labels are a subset of all labels. Preserve separate counts/denominators or explicitly label a weighted priority, rather than present the sum as an occurrence count.

## Small discriminating tests

- Equally low nonempty rates for known negative queries, known positive targets missing, and unjudged queries produce different qualified diagnoses. Expected-empty success must not imply recall failure.
- Arbitrary irrelevant hits cannot improve judged quality or authorize a recall-improvement claim.
- Hold retrieval outputs fixed and change only workload weights: report workload change, not product quality improvement.
- Hold each query's service/rerank latency fixed while varying concurrency; inverse throughput changes, but latency-based rerank advice does not.
- Give two fixtures identical aggregate hit counts but contradictory direct cause evidence; either recommendations reflect the evidence or remain explicitly unverified hypotheses.
- A label observed on four total searches, three of them zero-hit, reports total=4 and zero-hit=3, not seven independent observations.
- Preserve the existing report-shape/ordering fixture as plumbing coverage and add these independent negative controls through buildReportOutput.

Dedup: #1655 owns eligibility for generic A/B sweep winners, not this language-report diagnostic generator. #632 owns representative relevance evidence; this is the concrete consumer that currently overinterprets an available smoke statistic. #1648 remains the telemetry-unit owner. No implementation, benchmark, model or test was run.

## Defect

At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, supported legacy benchmark reconstruction can combine an old result's counters with the repository's current metrics. Re-rendering the same saved report after another index run can change its reconstructed historical throughput.

Native embedded ledgers/indexing summaries are preferred, and the default report path is read-only. Those current repairs are valuable and must remain. The remaining defect is temporal source identity, not an accusation that ordinary reporting rewrites JSON.

## Concrete source chain

- [show-throughput resolves missing ledgers using payload repoPath and saved throughput/indexing counters](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/analysis.js#L525-L564).
- [buildThroughputLedgerForTask defaults to loadRepoIndexMetrics(repoPath)](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/stage-ledger.js#L423-L432). [That loader uses current user configuration and the mutable metrics/index-{mode}.json files](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/stage-ledger.js#L386-L398), without a recorded attempt/generation check.
- [Counters prefer the saved throughput entry](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/stage-ledger.js#L81-L96), but [durations prefer the newly loaded mode metrics over the saved totalMs fallback](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/stage-ledger.js#L436-L460). The resulting row can therefore be a mixed-attempt ratio.
- The language aggregate [uses the same fallback ledger builder](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1662-L1670), and [buildStageTimingProfileForTask independently reads current repository metrics](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/metrics/stage-ledger.js#L402-L412).
- Adjacent legacy feature-metric reconstruction [loads mutable feature-metrics-run.json/feature-metrics.json from a cache or repository root](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/load.js#L88-L109). Its mtime/size cache invalidation is useful for current reads, but does not prove those measurements belong to the historical report.

Source-derived counterexample: saved report A contains 100 chunks and totalMs=1000 but no native ledger. The same repository's live index metrics now belong to B and contain totalMs=10000. Reconstruction selects A's 100 chunks and B's 10000ms, producing 10 chunks/s instead of A's 100 chunks/s. No project process was run to claim an observed reproduction.

The generic fallback provenance identifies that reconstruction happened, but not which immutable attempt supplied each input or that the sources disagree. Opt-in materialization can persist this reconstructed ledger into the old report, after which a later read regards it as an existing native ledger.

## Repair architecture

1. Treat a saved benchmark result as an attempt-owned evidence snapshot. Prefer its embedded scan profile, throughput, timing and indexing receipts without reading unrelated current repository state.
2. Permit external reconstruction only from a generation/attempt-qualified artifact reference with matching recorded identity. A repository path, current pointer or matching file timestamp alone is not that identity.
3. Keep missing historical facts unavailable. If an operator explicitly requests enrichment from current state, emit a separate qualified view with source-attempt identities and exclude mixed observations from historical performance comparisons.

## Current finding
At PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, a throughput report can silently exclude unreadable/corrupt expected input files and still emit an ordinary successful summary, while admitting unrelated truthy JSON as benchmark runs. The input boundary also synchronously reads and retains every JSON payload before latest/repository selection, with no per-file or aggregate byte allowance.

This is source/data-flow evidence, not an executed malformed-file or memory-pressure reproduction.

## Exact paths and counterexamples
- [load.js:35–40](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/load.js#L35-L40) catches every read/parse error and returns null. Missing-after-inventory, permission denial and malformed/truncated JSON become indistinguishable from absent input. It uses unbounded readFileSync.
- [show-throughput.js:586–605](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L586-L605) lists every .json and fully parses it inside files.map **before** calling selection. The repaired early selector prevents excluded runs from participating in aggregates, but does not avoid reading/retaining their bodies.
- [selection.js:13–16](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/selection.js#L13-L16) admits any truthy payload, not a validated benchmark-run shape. [analysis.js:488–505](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput/analysis.js#L488-L505) manufactures a repo/history identity from its filename if no run identity exists.
- Therefore a folder containing one healthy run and one unreadable/corrupt run silently reports only the healthy run with no discovered/rejected-input receipt. Replacing the second file with an unrelated JSON object such as {generatedAt: a later date, note: 'not a benchmark'} makes it an admitted run; with --latest 1 it displaces the actual measurement. No hostile content is needed.
- [show-throughput.js:637–660](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L637-L660) counts the admitted payload and outcome/provenance contributions; [742–746](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L742-L746) calls a folder with zero readable runs 'No benchmark JSON files found', even when files existed and all failed to load. The machine envelope has no input admission outcomes.
- [materialize-throughput.js:61–65](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/materialize-throughput.js#L61-L65) uses the same null result to skip failures and can finish with zero write failures despite unreadable requested inputs. Wrong-kind but truthy payloads reach mutating materializers instead of being excluded by an input contract.
- [buildComparison:1648–1672](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/reports/show-throughput.js#L1648-L1672) correctly rejects a nonzero baseline child, but trusts its zero-status output as a usable report without checking input completeness/schema. A successfully produced partial baseline thus inherits the same silent missingness. This does not claim JSON syntax errors are swallowed here; JSON.parse can throw.

## Required architecture
1. Add a small shared result-input admission owner used by report and explicit materialization. Return typed outcomes: valid supported run, recognized non-run artifact, unsupported version, missing/unreadable, malformed, too large, cancelled. Keep filename, bounded cause and source identity in the receipt; do not store arbitrary file contents.
2. Recognize supported current/legacy result envelopes explicitly. Do not require every old file to have a new schemaVersion, but do not treat any object/string/array as a run. Distinguish a legitimate failed/zero-work benchmark record from an unrelated document; failure records remain visible, not silently dropped.
3. Expose discovered, selected, admitted and excluded/failed input counts/reasons. Default human inspection may emit useful partial results if clearly labeled; CI/gating/comparison must not interpret partial evidence as a complete passing cohort. Define strict versus allow-partial policy deliberately.
4. Bound owned reads and overall retained payloads. For --latest N, process enough bounded metadata to perform its documented timestamp/identity selection, retain at most the needed candidates, then load expensive selected sections. Do not substitute filename/mtime ordering or drop legitimate older-format inputs merely to optimize. If metadata requires JSON parsing, sequential bounded reading still avoids files.map retaining every full payload.
5. Preserve cancellation/deadline between files and expensive derived work. Reuse existing bounded JSON/file readers and numeric/schema adapters rather than creating another unbounded generic loader. Separate invalid-input diagnosis from fallback reconstruction (#1680).
6. The baseline comparison should consume the same typed report model/receipt, or validate the versioned child response including input completeness before computing deltas. Keep partial sides explicitly unknown, not a valid empty baseline.

## Small discriminating acceptance
- One real healthy fixture + one truncated JSON + one unreadable/missing-after-inventory file: correct healthy measurements survive, the failures are independently counted and neither complete/passing status nor 'no files found' is emitted.
- Add unrelated object/array/string JSON, a supported legacy run and a legitimate failed/empty run. Verify latest-N cannot select the unrelated document and that supported failure records are not discarded.
- A baseline with one rejected requested run cannot produce an unqualified comparable receipt. Zero-exit wrong-schema child output is rejected; explicit valid empty and explicit partial remain different.
- A large excluded input cannot cause unbounded allocation/retention. Instrument bytes/read ownership and candidate retention on many tiny runs plus one over-limit file; no full benchmark needed.
- Assert no default report writes; materialization does not touch rejected/non-run inputs and reports read/admission failures separately from write failures.
- Preserve current early repo/latest admission, stable timestamp ties and repaired format-independent regression ranking.

## Deduplication / limits
#279 owns output DTO/serialization and profile projections; #277 owns legitimate observation/baseline eligibility; #770 owns selected run/mode semantics; #1680 owns historical generation identity; #1254 owns repeated log/JSONL scans in the different language-report reducer. This issue owns the result-folder **file-to-run admission and bounded loading** boundary. No production implementation, test run, benchmark or real credential access was performed.

## Current source finding
PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, verified 2026-10-23. Source review only; no benchmark/process/test execution.

The process-level confidence producer can report **high 100.0% with zero progress observations**, while replay can turn an explicitly unknown score into numeric zero. This is diagnostic truthfulness, not evidence that the watchdog itself incorrectly permits a hang.

## Concrete paths and positive coverage
- [Process initialization](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/process.js#L1366-L1386) starts all sample arrays empty and heartbeat/stall counters at zero. [Component calculation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/process.js#L1462-L1522) then sets `stallRate=0` when both counters are zero and unconditionally sets `stallEventsScore=1`. The other components remain null.
- [Shared weighting](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/logging.js#L858-L929) omits unknown components but admits the stall score independently of its zero sample count. A silent successful child therefore produces score 1 and bucket high when the [forced exit snapshot](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/process.js#L2098-L2116) is built. A plain non-progress line also reaches this producer through [handleLine](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/process.js#L2040-L2059). A lone task-start similarly supplies no interval evidence but can produce a reassuring interactive confidence message.
- The score is based on completed intervals and historical queue/in-flight samples, not current observation age. [Emission](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/process.js#L1555-L1574) labels an elapsed check periodic but runs only when called by incoming lines, stall events or exit. A previously healthy sample is not a continuously refreshed liveness guarantee; an unfinished silence is not included in its interval statistics.
- [Report parsing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L711-L741) uses `Number(parsed.score)`, converting JSON null to 0 while retaining bucket unknown. [Aggregation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/bench/language/report.js#L1027-L1063) then admits that invented zero into average/minimum and low-confidence details.
- Credit the existing null guards in `classifyBenchProgressConfidence`/`formatBenchProgressConfidence` and the [pure empty-input regression](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/language-progress-confidence.test.js#L89-L95). They correctly preserve unknown at that layer. The [real child integration fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/perf/bench/language-process-progress-confidence.test.js#L31-L84) exercises positive telemetry and persisted output, but no empty/stale case; its `Number.isFinite(Number(score))` oracle would also accept null as numeric zero.

## Repair architecture
1. Give the measured heuristic an explicit observation contract: active phase/task, observation window, sample sufficiency, last-observed age and unknown/stale state. Keep a heuristic score distinct from a calibrated probability or proof of useful forward progress.
2. Do not award a no-stall score before there is an eligible observation interval. Preserve legitimate zero and partial telemetry, but do not renormalize a zero-evidence component into 100%.
3. If live freshness is displayed, use the existing owned watchdog/activity clock and a bounded refresh owner, without adding another competing timeout policy. Otherwise label the snapshot as last observed and show its age. Historical healthy intervals must not erase current silence.
4. Use the same finite-or-unknown score admission at producer and report boundaries. Unknown rows remain visible in coverage/counts, but do not enter numeric denominators or rank as measured low confidence.
5. Keep existing JSONL fields/log layout compatible where possible; version any semantic change and add explicit coverage/freshness fields rather than relying on color or reassuring text.

## Discriminating acceptance
- A tiny silent child and a child with only ordinary text return/persist unknown confidence with zero eligible samples, not high 100%.
- One task-start without an interval remains insufficient; a real healthy interval sequence produces the independently expected score and coverage.
- A deterministic clock-driven fixture advances from healthy observations into silence, then recovery. Displayed freshness and evidence state change without manufacturing work, while watchdog decisions retain their existing independent policy.
- Replay a valid row with score null/bucket unknown next to a measured score 0.8: numeric average/min/max remain 0.8; unknown count remains one. Real score zero is retained.
- Strengthen the integration assertion to check primitive numeric type plus finiteness only when observed; assert the actual summary and JSONL receipt, not just existence/schema/string bucket.
- Bound refresh rate and listener/timer ownership; no additional full-suite or long-duration sleeps are needed.

## Boundaries
#1334 owns terminal layout, #285/#115/#121 watchdog behavior. This owns the current confidence calculation and replay semantics, not a watchdog rewrite. Existing pure helper fixes and positive integration coverage must be retained. Live all-state confidence/progress-confidence searches found no matching calculation owner.

## Current defect and user impact
At PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523` (2026-10-23), triage context packs silently drop all hits returned by an explicit extracted-prose search. The saved evidence projection also discards the search receipt needed to locate and qualify retained hits later. Source-only audit; no triage/index/search/model execution.

## Exact producer → consumer mismatch
- [buildRepoEvidence](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/context-pack.js#L97-L120) searches CLI modes code, prose and **extracted-prose**, then reads `result.payload?.[mode]`.
- The real [search renderer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/render.js#L373-L405) publishes the extracted-prose array under **extractedProse**, while code/prose use matching names. Thus a successful extracted-prose result with one hit becomes an empty hits array in the saved pack, without an evidence-search warning.
- The [MCP triage_context_pack handler](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/mcp/tools/handlers/triage.js#L90-L121) launches this same CLI. This is not only an unused helper.
- The [existing context-pack fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/triage/context-pack.test.js#L77-L129) builds code only and requires merely some evidence hit across all queries/modes. A healthy code hit lets it pass while every extracted-prose hit is lost.

## Related loss in the same evidence projection
[Saved pack/query assembly](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/context-pack.js#L66-L85) and [pickEvidenceHit](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/context-pack.js#L151-L162) retain display fields and scores but no explicit searched repository root, hit chunk identity/range, or per-query retrieval freshness/backend/fidelity receipt. [The search renderer already attaches retrieval metadata](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/cli/render.js#L388-L405); [its freshness owner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/retrieval/output/retrieval-metadata.js#L31-L49) publishes available build/generation identity. That evidence is discarded rather than unavailable upstream.

A retained relative file/name/snippet is not an exact source locator across two repos with the same path or a later generation. The finding's routing repo field and pack generatedAt are not substitutes for the repository actually searched or the generation actually observed. Do not invent hashes or source verification that the underlying search did not provide.

## Repair contract
1. Use one explicit CLI-mode → payload-key mapping at the search-consumer boundary. Validate the selected payload shape instead of treating an unexpected key as successful zero results.
2. Define a compact typed triage evidence projection retaining the query mode, actual repository identity, per-query success/empty/unavailable state, actual backend/fidelity/freshness receipt, and available hit identity/range. Reuse canonical search metadata rather than a second mode taxonomy or generation resolver.
3. Preserve source qualification through JSON persistence and MCP delivery. A historical saved hit can remain useful, but navigation/re-reading must verify its source identity or mark it stale/unavailable instead of silently reading current same-path bytes.
4. Keep preview snippets bounded and explicitly lossy; do not use them as exact source support. Distinguish known source range from unknown range.
5. Keep outer warnings, but bind any unavailable/failed search outcome to its query/mode receipt. A real empty search and dropped/incompatible payload must not be identical.

## Discriminating tests
- Tiny fixture with a token present only in an extracted comment, with independent expected file/chunk identity: direct selected-mode search returns it and the actual triage pack retains it under the extracted-prose query. Include code/prose positive controls and a genuinely empty result.
- Inject a malformed/missing selected array at the boundary: explicit outcome diagnostic, not successful empty evidence.
- Two repos sharing src/util.js plus a changed generation: saved evidence identifies the searched repo and observed generation; stale navigation does not substitute another/current source.
- Assert the serialized hit's stable identity/range and per-query backend/freshness values equal the real search receipt, including explicit unknowns. The oracle must not be “some hit exists.”
- Exercise the existing MCP argument handoff and returned artifact reference without a model download or full corpus.

## Scope and current credit
#1440 owns the analogous evaluation consumer; this is the independently implemented triage consumer. #810's history optimization is now implemented through bounded concurrency, top-k heaps, contained reads and explicit incomplete-history diagnostics; do not reopen its old unbounded-read claim here. #1130 is new context-selection annotations, not this existing search-result projection. Live all-state triage/extracted/pickEvidenceHit/source-citation searches found no matching owner. No implementation.

## Current source and scope

Source-only audit of PR #572 at `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. This is a defect in the implemented private nonrecursive adjacency pilot, not a request to implement the broader incremental database in #1516. No repository edits, fixture execution, or runtime reproduction were performed.

Credit the existing behavior: owned immutable view handles, exact occurrence/support multiplicities, one-of-many support removal, separate support versus membership changes, checked base roots/worlds, conflicting replay rejection, explicit incomplete captured domains, and no publication or recursive-closure claim.

## Concrete split between receipt and consumed input

In [applyAdjacencyDelta](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/semantic/views/adjacency-delta.js#L68-L123):

1. The caller's batch and edits are validated and byte-counted (lines 70–80), then the batch digest is computed (line 81).
2. Base identity is checked, but no private copy of the batch exists.
3. Reading `signal.aborted` (line 89, and again inside the update loop) is an observable caller effect. The API does not require a native, effect-free AbortSignal.
4. The function then rereads caller-owned edits, endpoints, source refs, `toWorld`, `batchId`, and `capturedDomainComplete` to construct the next view and ledger.

An allowed input-level counterexample is a base support with multiplicity 2, a batch requesting -1, and an aborted getter which returns false but changes the still-public edit to -2 after its digest was computed. Coalescing consumes -2 and removes the support, while the ledger records the original -1 digest. Replaying the original -1 content against the returned view is classified as an identical replay even though that is not the transition consumed. Similarly, mutation of destination world or captured-domain completeness after validation can produce a view under a different world/closure statement than the digest admits. This is a source-traced counterexample, not an executed result.

The private ownership of the old view does not repair the ownership of the incoming transition. No durable publication corruption is alleged: this API currently returns private, unpublished handles.

## Fix architecture

- Introduce a small owned-batch admission boundary. Capture the complete batch with the existing passive canonical data encoder and an explicit aggregate byte budget before polling cancellation or running other caller effects. Validate, hash, coalesce, apply, and construct the ledger from the same private value.
- Reuse [canonicalSemanticJson's bounded path](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/semantic/identity.js) and the ownership pattern already used by [the finite capsule checker](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/semantic/capsules/finite-may-check.js), rather than another bespoke recursive clone. Reject accessor/decorated/sparse inputs without invoking their accessors. Do not stringify an unbounded batch and check its size only afterward.
- Preserve the original operation's cancellation source, but it must not be able to rewrite admitted transition semantics. Cancellation before completion leaves the original view authoritative and the batch unconsumed. No partially constructed next view or receipt should escape.
- Bind the returned root, support changes, membership changes, destination world, completeness, and replay ledger to that one capture. Do not hash the original input and apply a second read or independently recopied projection.
- Audit bootstrap admission for the same passive-input requirement. Existing row validation and shallow `[...rows]` are not a general owned-array contract.
- Document whether replayed batches are reported before cancellation, as today; do not accidentally change replay semantics while repairing ownership. Preserve the 1024-entry ledger/checkpoint-required boundary and all existing old-reader behavior.

## Small independent proof plan

Extend [adjacency-delta.test.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/indexing/semantic/adjacency-delta.test.js), without a broad campaign:

1. Use a two-count support and a one-shot nonaborting cancellation getter to mutate the original edit after entry. The result must reflect the originally captured -1 batch, or reject without consuming it, never pair -1's digest with -2's transition.
2. Independently mutate destination world, captured-domain completeness, batch ID, and edit payload at the first and later polls. Assert all returned identities/closure statements and replay behavior belong to the same original capture.
3. Retain the old handle and enumerate both old/new occurrence bags with the existing cursor; compare with a hand-computed count and clean bootstrap, not just a changed root string.
4. Exact original replay is idempotent; changed content under the same original batch ID is rejected. Cancellation still leaves no consumed batch and no replacement handle.
5. Getter-bearing/decorated input arrays/objects are rejected without invoking getters; aggregate byte overflow fails before clone/application. Keep ordinary native AbortController and already-aborted cases.

#1516 remains the research owner for generalized maintained views, publication, checkpoint recovery, and qualified recursion. This issue is the current small producer ownership repair.

## Defect

The mutating `triage-decision` command does not use the bounded, contained record reader already used by triage context/history. It also does not bind the requested record ID to the record it actually reads before creating a durable decision.

Current PR572 head verified: `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. Source audit only, not a runtime reproduction.

## Exact production path and current protections

- [decision.js lines44–58](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/decision.js#L44-L58) resolves a record name, then calls unrestricted `fsPromises.readFile(findingPath, 'utf8')` and `JSON.parse`. Every read/parse failure is presented as “Finding record not found.”
- [resolveRecordArtifactPathSafe](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/context-pack-paths.js#L14-L24) correctly rejects slash/backslash traversal and lexical escapes. It does not inspect the filesystem object, prevent a symlink at an otherwise valid basename, or bound bytes.
- [decision construction](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/decision.js#L63-L90) accepts the parsed value without record-shape or identity admission. It links to `finding.recordId || findingId` and proceeds to the durable writer.
- The adjacent [context-pack selected-record reader](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/context-pack.js#L181-L190) now delegates to [readTriageHistoryRecord](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/history.js#L10-L18): an existing 16 MiB `readVerifiedContainedFile` boundary with object admission. This is a real repair to credit and reuse, not a request to reimplement a filesystem sandbox. That shared helper still does not validate requested-versus-embedded record identity.
- [The existing descriptor-bound primitive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/contained-file.js#L19-L79) validates containment, no symlinks, regular-file and opened-object identity. Its bounded read/closure contract should be preserved.

## Concrete consequences

1. A valid basename `finding-a.json` that is a symlink is followed by the decision command, despite the command's apparent records-directory boundary. This requires a local filesystem entry; no remote attacker, arbitrary remote exploit or actual sensitive-file access is asserted.
2. A syntactically valid but non-record object such as `{}` can create a decision with empty finding facts and `findingRecordId` taken from the requested basename. An oversized file is fully read/allocated before parsing.
3. If `finding-a.json` contains `recordId: "finding-b"`, asking to decide A durably associates the decision with B without disclosing or rejecting the mismatch. The context pack can likewise label the outer pack A while embedding B.
4. Legitimate repeated imports can replace the current finding under the same stable ID: [record-writer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/triage/record-writer.js#L18-L34) has a special fallback-hash conflict check, but otherwise writes the selected ID. A saved decision contains selected copied fields and a mutable finding-ID reference, not a receipt identifying the admitted observation. This makes later audit reconstruction ambiguous when source facts change. This last point is an audit-lineage contract gap, not a claim that all copied fields are missing or that saved decisions currently enforce vulnerability suppression.

## Repair architecture

- Factor a typed `loadTriageRecordSnapshot(recordsDir, requestedId, ...)` boundary from the repaired contained reader. Bound bytes before allocation, parse once, validate the supported record shape/kind/version and compare canonical requested/embedded identity. If legacy ID-less records remain supported, make that explicit and lower-trust rather than silently inventing equivalence.
- Return the admitted record with a compact observation receipt derived from those same bytes: record ID, source/identity provenance, content digest or existing immutable version, and observed update/version metadata. Do not reread the path to hash it after validation.
- The decision writer must use that admitted snapshot and persist the receipt alongside its finding link. Context/history can use the same identity-aware boundary without acquiring mutation authority. Retain a stable finding link plus observation identity; do not automatically retarget a decision to the newest finding.
- Preserve typed missing, malformed, unsafe-path, too-large, changed-during-read, cancelled and native-resource-pending outcomes. Only actual absence should become “not found”; failure must not publish a partial decision or authorize a fallback reader.
- Share the helper with the existing record lifecycle instead of a new storage framework. Package projection is #1445, routing precedence #803, paired JSON/Markdown publication #821, and repo-versus-record indexing namespaces #1638; those do not cover this selected-record admission boundary.

## Small discriminating acceptance tests

- Extend [decision path safety](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/tooling/triage/decision-finding-path-safety.test.js) beyond its existing `../outside-finding` negative test. Use only tiny synthetic disposable files: normal valid record, in-root symlink to a synthetic outside sentinel, requested A/embedded B, primitive/array/empty-object records, malformed JSON, and a deliberately tiny configured byte limit.
- Assert the exact typed failure and **no new decision artifacts**, not merely nonzero exit. Preserve the existing valid traversal rejection and positive normal decision.
- Through the actual decision CLI, save a decision for observation A1, replace the finding with A2 under the same stable ID, then verify the saved decision still identifies A1's admitted bytes. A fresh decision must identify A2, with no duplicate copied raw payload needed.
- Exercise same-byte verification and close/error ownership using the existing contained-reader test adapters; do not weaken or swallow a resource-pending failure.
- Cross-check requested/embedded identity in context packs, and keep explicit legacy compatibility controls.
- No indexing/model/provider work is necessary. Bounded read/hash cost is O(admitted bytes) once; no new corpus scan or independent full-file reread.

All-state triage/decision/admission/symlink/lineage searches found no matching owner. #810's bounded history implementation is the reusable positive baseline. No implementation, tests, deletion or sensitive data access performed for this report.
