## Current source defect

The supported `suggest-tests --maxWallClockMs <n>` option is parsed and forwarded, but the implementation never reads or enforces it. Large live discovery/reverse-import work therefore ignores an explicitly requested time budget.

Audited PR572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. Source trace only; no long-running traversal or timing experiment was executed.

## Exact accepted-value path

1. [SUGGEST_TESTS_OPTIONS](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/shared/operator-cli-options.js#L101-L116) declares `maxWallClockMs` as a number.
2. [runSuggestTestsCli lines55–68](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/integrations/tooling/suggest-tests.js#L55-L68) normalizes it into `capOverrides` and merges the effective caps.
3. [The actual report call](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/integrations/tooling/suggest-tests.js#L83-L93) passes those caps.
4. [buildSuggestTestsReport lines340–359](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/graph/suggest-tests.js#L340-L359) projects only depth/nodes/edges/work/candidates/suggestions/seeds. It omits maxWallClockMs, even from the emitted effective-cap receipt.
5. [Live directory discovery](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/graph/suggest-tests.js#L98-L174) and [reverse-import BFS](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/graph/suggest-tests.js#L420-L478) have no elapsed-time/deadline check. Discovery's entry bound and the traversal's optional count caps are useful protections but not enforcement of the accepted time option.

The core function's `now` argument is a generated-at timestamp callback, not an execution deadline. Replacing its date stamp or merely logging the requested limit would not repair the work boundary.

## Why it matters

An operator can deliberately request a short suggestion budget on a large repository and still perform the same work as an unbounded-time invocation. This is incidental analysis used for deciding what to inspect/run, not a request to run a full suite. Returned-list size does not bound directory/native-call latency or the reachable graph.

#147 owns assigning sensible work budgets to risk-guidance callers. This issue owns honoring the time cap already accepted by the standalone/shared suggestion command; a caller cannot fix an option the callee discards.

## Narrow architecture

- Admit one monotonic deadline/work context from the existing request owner and preserve the effective cap in provenance. Define whether the public option covers the whole command, graph preparation, or suggestion computation; document and expose excluded preparation rather than implying an end-to-end bound that starts late.
- Check that deadline at admission and bounded discovery/traversal checkpoints, preserving current count caps. Use one owner across subphases rather than resetting the allowance for each seed or directory.
- A synchronous native directory operation cannot be forcibly interrupted by an ordinary JS checkpoint. Be honest about the maximum uninterruptible unit, and use existing async/owned bounded I/O where necessary rather than promising a hard wall-clock cutoff from a post-read check.
- On exhaustion, settle owned work and return a typed partial result with completed scope, deadline reason and observed work, or the existing strict timeout outcome. Never return complete/no-match merely because time expired.
- Preserve resource-pending/close failures, deterministic ordering of admitted candidates, and explicit zero/invalid-limit semantics. Do not start fallback work after the same deadline or silently retry with a larger budget.

## Small independent acceptance

- Exercise the canonical CLI option → report path with an injected monotonic clock and bounded directory/neighbor adapters. Advance time during discovery, then independently during BFS; assert the actual next admission stops and the returned provenance/fidelity says deadline-limited.
- Test under-budget complete work, exact-boundary/zero behavior as specified, invalid/nonfinite values, warm inventory reuse and multiple seeds sharing one allowance.
- Include one slow/pending I/O adapter to prove timeout observation does not falsely claim native settlement or admit a fallback reader.
- Assert actual directory/neighbor visits, retained candidates, diagnostic bytes and the request-to-phase timing receipt, not merely the presence of an option in help text.
- Keep tiny deterministic fixtures. No sleeps, broad repository scan or platform benchmark is required to prove the option is consumed; a separate bounded latency receipt may qualify the declared uninterruptible unit.

## Dedupe and current credit

All-state suggest-tests/deadline/clock searches found no exact owner. #371 covers fidelity including live inventory failures, #756 lazy witness retention, #748 count-aware neighbor iteration, #1137 optional semantic/recorded-coverage tiers. Preserve current bounded discovery, freshness, CSR and graph/heuristic distinctions; do not replace them with a second traversal engine.

[Attachment]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/graph/path-capability.js#L57-L81 ) throws `ERR_GRAPH_PATH_CONTRACT`; the CLI wraps the failure as `ERR_GRAPH_CONTEXT`.
4. This check runs on top-level edges regardless of whether witness paths were requested. Disabling `includePaths` does not repair the normal chunk import context.

A minimal source-derived counterexample has a chunk `b` with file `src/b.js`, a retained import `src/b.js -> src/a.js`, an exact matching index signature, seed `{type:'chunk',chunkUid:'b'}`, direction `out`, depth 1, and importGraph selected. Without the capability option the produced edge is `chunk:b -> file:src/a.js`; with it the domain check fails. Incoming imports have the symmetric mismatch. No runtime reproduction or full CLI execution is claimed here.

## Existing implementation and tests to preserve

The current direction repair correctly separates source-oriented endpoints from traversal destination, preserving incoming call-site evidence. [directed-traversal.test.js]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/graph/directed-traversal.test.js#L9-L78 ) meaningfully tests chunk-seeded call/usage/import contexts, reciprocal edges, witnesses, rendered orientation and CSR/legacy parity, but does not enable graph-witness. Conversely [path-capability-publication.test.js]( https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/graph/path-capability-publication.test.js#L9-L49 ) enables the declaration on a call-only cycle and symbolic unresolved edge, not the chunk-to-import projection. Each half is covered independently; their supported composition is not.

## Repair architecture

- Decide and document one typed contract for a chunk seed crossing into its containing file's import graph. Keep canonical import adjacency file-to-file and represent the containing-file/seed projection explicitly, or define a separately qualified projection relation with the exact generation-owned chunk-to-file mapping.
- Reuse the selected graph's existing chunk/file facts. Do not reread the working tree or infer ownership from names to make the validator pass.
- Apply the same projection contract to ordinary context output, witness construction, capability declaration and validation. Merely allowing arbitrary endpoint types under importGraph would erase the advertised relation-domain guarantee.
- Preserve source orientation, incoming/outgoing traversal semantics, caps and no-runtime-feasibility qualification. Do not make existing chunk import queries silently disappear when qualification is enabled.

## Discriminating acceptance

Extend the existing directed-traversal fixture with a matching pinned signature and graph-witness enabled, for out/in/both, includePaths false/true, raw/prepared CSR/legacy inputs, reciprocal imports and mixed call/import depth. Assert actual returned endpoint domains, seed/containing-file association, original import direction and witness connectivity against the known retained relation set. Include a true file seed and a call-only chunk seed as positive controls, and an unrelated file mapping as a negative control. Add one small actual indexed-source CLI fixture so the supported option emits a validated payload rather than a generic error. Preserve exact scope/corrupt-edge controls already present.

## Deduplication / boundaries

All-state graph-witness, import/chunk-seed and relation-domain issue searches were reviewed. #645 owns original edge orientation and evidence lookup; that repair is credited here. #1702 owns downstream/upstream impact meaning. #1135 is the broad path-contract owner, but this is the concrete normal-input domain incompatibility in its current implemented opt-in surface, not an impact-result association amendment. No implementation, project test, provider or user-machine execution was performed.

## Confirmed benchmark identity error

When optional native RE2 is installed—the only case in which this benchmark reports a two-engine comparison—the arm labeled `re2js` actually selects native RE2 too. The reported RE2JS/native contrast is therefore SafeRegex-wrapped native RE2 versus direct native RE2, not the two claimed engines.

Source audit of active PR #572 at `60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e` on 2026-10-24. The implicated blobs are unchanged from the initial `1aa6e757` snapshot. This finding follows the ordinary supported selection path; no production edits, benchmark, native execution or bootstrap bypass was performed.

## Exact path

1. [regex.js:80–95](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/regex.js#L80-L95) constructs the purported RE2JS arm with `createSafeRegex(pattern, flags, {maxPatternLength:0, maxInputLength:0, maxProgramSize:0, timeoutMs:0})`. It does **not** supply `engine:'re2js'`, then unconditionally stores its timings under `results.engines.re2js`.
2. [createSafeRegex:248–273](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/shared/safe-regex.js#L248-L273) reads that missing engine through `normalizeEngine` and passes it to `selectBackend`.
3. [normalizeEngine/selectBackend:42–60](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/shared/safe-regex.js#L42-L60) maps the missing value to `auto`; auto prefers native RE2 whenever available. Explicit `re2js` is already supported and selects the intended backend.
4. [regex.js:97–106](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/regex.js#L97-L106) independently loads the same optional `re2` module for the second arm. Thus availability sufficient to run that second arm also switches the first arm away from RE2JS.
5. The effective engine is already observable as [SafeRegex.engine:63–72](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/shared/safe-regex.js#L63-L72), but the benchmark neither asserts nor reports it.

### Discriminating cases

| Optional native RE2 | Actual first arm | Actual second arm | Report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unavailable | RE2JS | unavailable | one valid RE2JS measurement |
| available | native RE2 through SafeRegex | direct native RE2 | incorrectly labeled RE2JS versus RE2 |

More iterations or larger input cannot repair this comparison: the intended JavaScript engine is never exercised when both arms run.

## Repair

- Explicitly select the requested backend for each arm and verify the effective engine before warmup/timing. An unavailable requested engine remains unavailable; do not silently benchmark a substitute under its name.
- Retain requested/effective engine and relevant package/runtime identity with the result.
- Decide whether this experiment compares engine kernels or public production wrappers. Use equivalent wrapper/state semantics for a kernel comparison, or label the intentional wrapper difference explicitly rather than attributing it entirely to engine performance.
- Preserve the same pattern, flags, input and per-operation state policy across arms. For global regexes, document whether an operation starts at offset zero or advances through matches; check matching-result parity outside the timing loop.
- Keep this repair within the existing microbenchmark and SafeRegex selection API; production auto-selection itself is not the defect.

## Acceptance

- With both engines available, an instrumented small regression proves the RE2JS arm invokes only RE2JS and the native arm invokes only native RE2; the published effective identities agree.
- Without native RE2, the first arm still exercises RE2JS and the second remains explicitly unavailable.
- An effective-engine mismatch fails before timing publication.
- A tiny matching/nonmatching fixture checks the chosen operation semantics and parity; then any scoped performance run reports its actual work count, warmup and measured duration. No large corpus/native campaign is needed to establish the dispatch regression.

## Deduplication and limits

Screened the cached all-state 1–1723 issue corpus and refreshed the latest 100 updated items before filing. No existing issue owns this microbenchmark engine substitution. #1655 concerns A/B recommendation eligibility; #1687 concerns throughput result-file admission; neither repairs this producer. This issue asserts an incorrect benchmark identity, **not** a measured engine speedup or a production regex correctness defect.

<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Source-verified work-count defect

`runSampledBench` executes more measured operations than requested whenever `samples > iterations`. Hash and regex callers nevertheless divide the elapsed time by the **requested** iteration count, so their published throughput has the wrong numerator.

The ordinary bounded invocation shape `--iterations 3 --warmup 0` already reaches this because both CLIs default to 10 samples. This is not an oversized or malformed input case.

Audited PR #572 at `60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e`; shared helper, regex and hash producers are current-source verified. No benchmark or project test was executed.

## Mechanism and exact arithmetic

- [utils.js:62–88](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/utils.js#L62-L88) computes `perSample = Math.max(1, Math.floor(iterations / samples))`, then always visits all `samples` buckets.
- With 3 iterations and 10 samples, `perSample=1` and `remainder=-7`; every bucket executes one operation. Actual measured calls are **10**, not 3. With 1/10, the amplification is tenfold.
- [hash.js:17–30,44–47](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/hash.js#L17-L47) exposes independently accepted iteration/sample options; [92–98](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/hash.js#L92-L98) computes bytes as `payload.length * iterations`, not actual calls.
- [regex.js:148–156](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/regex.js#L148-L156) likewise computes operations/second from the requested count.
- [compression.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/compression.js) uses the same helper and reports the original iteration count, so its declared work also disagrees with execution even though it does not publish the same rate field.

| Requested iterations | Requested samples | Actual measured calls | Reported numerator / actual numerator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 | 10 | 0.1 |
| 3 | 10 | 10 | 0.3 |
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 1 |
| 11 | 10 | 11 | 1 |
| 2000 | 10 | 2000 | 1 |

This table is a deterministic trace of the loop arithmetic, not measured benchmark output. Warmup is separate and does not explain the discrepancy.

## Repair

1. Make the requested-work contract explicit: reject `samples > iterations`, reduce to a reported effective bucket count, or distribute zero-work buckets without including them as latency observations. Whichever policy is chosen, do not silently execute extra measured work.
2. Have the shared owner return actual completed measured operations and per-bucket operation counts; callers use that authoritative count for byte/operation rates and report requested versus effective settings.
3. Keep warmup count/time separate. A failed/incomplete callback must not publish a successful complete denominator.
4. Label the existing bucket-duration distribution as bucket timing, including bucket sizes. It is not a per-operation tail-latency distribution; unequal 1/2-operation buckets must not silently acquire that interpretation.
5. Cover finite positive integral sample/iteration admission at the existing boundary. No new benchmark framework or arbitrary minimum wall-time threshold is required.

## Acceptance

- A counting synchronous callback and an async callback each prove exact measured counts for (1,10), (3,10), (10,10), (11,10) and a divisible control, under the chosen documented policy.
- Verify warmup calls are separate from measured calls.
- A controlled elapsed-time fixture proves hash/regex rates use actual completed work, not requested work when those differ.
- Changing only the number of buckets cannot change the total measured work silently.
- Compression reports the same effective count contract.
- Existing histogram/format behavior retains its documented units; no claim that bucket p95 equals operation p95.

## Deduplication / scope

The refreshed all-state issue corpus through #1723 has no owner for this helper's count conservation. #1724 is the independent regex engine-selection error; #1655 owns A/B result eligibility and #1687 file-to-run admission. This is a small producer/accounting repair, not a claim that current default 2000/10 runs are affected or that a larger real workload was measured.

### Current-head extension: the VFS benchmark sampler has the same count bug

At PR #572 `c470cea9bfaec4ece13c10a20c1d27cbb8af045c`, [tools/bench/vfs/shared.js:41–62](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/c470cea9bfaec4ece13c10a20c1d27cbb8af045c/tools/bench/vfs/shared.js#L41-L62) independently implements the same `Math.max(1, floor(iterations / samples))` allocation and always runs every sample. It also calculates `opsPerSec` from requested iterations rather than completed calls. Fixing only the micro helper would leave this family incorrect.

The [Bloom benchmark](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/c470cea9bfaec4ece13c10a20c1d27cbb8af045c/tools/bench/vfs/bloom-negative-lookup.js#L20-L61) accepts `--lookups 3` with the default ten samples, allocates exactly three negative keys, then indexes that array with the sampler's monotonically increasing callback index. The sampler executes indices 0 through 9: **seven calls use undefined rather than a generated negative key**. [Bloom hashPair](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/c470cea9bfaec4ece13c10a20c1d27cbb8af045c/src/shared/bloom.js#L14-L19) turns undefined into the empty string; Set.has receives undefined. Thus both work count and workload identity are wrong. The separate false-positive pass still iterates only the three actual negative keys.

This is an exact source trace, not an executed benchmark. Ordinary 100,000-lookups/10-samples defaults are not affected.

Other current callers of this owner are `hash-routing-lookup.js`, `token-uri-encode.js` and `vfsidx-lookup.js`; their operation indices must never exceed the admitted input/query inventory either. Reuse one count-conserving synchronous sampler policy where appropriate rather than allowing this duplicate to diverge from the async micro helper.

Extend acceptance with a recording callback that verifies exactly the intended indices, no undefined operand, authoritative completed counts and correctly labeled bucket durations for samples greater than, equal to and less than operations. Keep per-operation and per-bucket statistics distinct. Current-head comparison confirms these files are unchanged from the audited 4b8618 blobs; no project code or tests were run.

### Complete the VFS work-count repair across local samplers and repeated-work rates

Current PR #572 `74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe`, source-verified 24 October 2026. This extends the existing VFS shared-sampler comment without duplicating it.

1. [segment-hash-cache.js:101–133](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/vfs/segment-hash-cache.js#L101-L133) has a **third independent copy** of the same at-least-one-per-bucket formula. Its default is ten samples; an admitted `--segments 3` sequence has only three elements. On the fourth iteration `segments[index]` is undefined and the noncached arm accesses `segment.text` (cached arm would access `segment.key`). Unlike Bloom's empty-string fallback, this path fails instead of completing the declared small benchmark. Reuse the same count-conserving async policy; the common VFS helper fix alone cannot repair it.

2. Several VFS helpers repeat the *whole workload* S times, sum all S elapsed durations, then divide by only one workload's N items:
   - [coalesce-docs.js:135–172](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/vfs/coalesce-docs.js#L135-L172), both baseline and coalescing arms;
   - [parallel-manifest-build.js:113–135](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/vfs/parallel-manifest-build.js#L113-L135), rowsPerSec uses only the final out.length;
   - [merge-runs-heap.js:174–195](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/vfs/merge-runs-heap.js#L174-L195), itemsPerSec omits repeated merges;
   - [partial-lsp-open.js:146–180](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/vfs/partial-lsp-open.js#L146-L180), docsPerSec similarly divides one input inventory by all repeated calls. Distinguish this inventory rate from actual opened-doc/request counts.

For a deterministic accounting oracle of 100 completed items taking 10 ms per repetition, S=1 should give 10,000 items/s and S=5 should still give 10,000 items/s. These formulas instead publish 2,000 items/s at S=5. Same-sample arm ratios may cancel the error, but the absolute rates and comparisons across sample counts do not. This arithmetic was **not executed**, and no wall-clock speed/regression is claimed.

Have the measurement owner accumulate actual completed operations/rows/bytes across repeats, with warmup separate, and use that count against total elapsed time (or explicitly use per-run duration with per-run count). If output cardinality can differ, sum each result rather than multiplying the last count. Preserve workload counts, actual cache hits/opened documents, and the distinct per-sample latency distribution in the receipt.

Extend controlled-clock/count tests to samples 1/3/5 for these repeated-work producers and segments 1/3 versus ten buckets for the local hash sampler. A stable synthetic per-operation cost must not become S times slower merely because more samples were requested. Source-only review; no project execution or bootstrap bypass.

### Qualification audit — 29 October 2026

**Keep open.** Audited PR #572 source at `74ee1bd733133a2d3084b19bbd0535d2346a3295` against this issue's original requirements and existing follow-ups; original acceptance is unchanged.

## The measured warm loop can skip the retrieval work it names

Both search microbenchmark drivers repeatedly issue the same query but clear only their index/SQLite handle caches. They leave the separate query-result cache active and discard the returned cache/execution evidence. With an ordinary `balanced` or `max` quality policy, a successful initial request populates that cache; later samples can replay hits without executing sparse/ANN retrieval or query embedding.

A warm result-cache benchmark is useful, but it is not interchangeable with warm-index retrieval. Increasing iterations, corpus size or duration in the present repeated-query loop can mostly measure more result-cache replays instead of exercising the optimization under study. The stored labels and ANN-backend comparison do not distinguish those workloads.

Source/control-flow audit of PR #572 at `60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e`. Relevant producer/session/policy blobs were rechecked at that head. No corpus, inference, native benchmark or project test was run.

## Current path

- [micro/search.js:62–104](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/search.js#L62-L104) times the same `search(...query...)` repeatedly, discards every response, clears only `indexCache` and `sqliteCache`, and returns `coldMs` plus warm duration statistics.
- [micro/tinybench.js:122–168](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L122-L168) likewise creates sparse/dense/hybrid tasks over one query, clears those two caches once, and records only SQLite entry count as cache evidence. [runSearch:191–204](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L191-L204) discards the search response.
- [normalize-options.js:226–249](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/retrieval/cli/normalize-options.js#L226-L249) enables the separate query cache whenever effective quality is not `fast`. This is reachable through normal configured quality and ordinary [host-dependent auto policy](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/shared/auto-policy/profile.js#L69-L80).
- [run-search-session.js:567–658](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/retrieval/cli/run-search-session.js#L567-L658) performs that lookup. [678–720](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/retrieval/cli/run-search-session.js#L678-L720) gates query embedding on `!cacheHit` and chooses `cachedHits || await runSearchByMode(...)`. A cache hit therefore skips the actual search pipeline.
- The owner [persists successful misses before returning and exposes cache.enabled/hit/strategy](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/src/retrieval/cli/run-search-session.js#L770-L810). The benchmark does not consume that evidence.
- [micro/run.js:245–268](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/run.js#L245-L268) computes a named SQLite-vector-versus-LanceDB warm-latency ratio from these unqualified samples. Backend selection does not establish that either backend executed during those samples.

The preflight uses `explain:true`, so this issue does **not** assume its result shares the ordinary timed key. The first timed miss itself is sufficient to populate the ordinary key for subsequent warmups/samples. An existing compatible disk result can also survive clearing index/SQLite caches, so `coldMs` does not guarantee a query-result miss.

## Repair in the existing benchmark/session owners

1. Declare separate experiment modes for repeated result-cache hits and actual retrieval with warm index/model/runtime state. Preserve useful user-path cache measurements, but label them honestly.
2. For a retrieval-work experiment, use a supported scoped cache bypass/isolated query-cache owner that holds all retrieval/scoring settings fixed. Do **not** change `quality` to `fast` merely to disable caching: that can also change the requested workload. Do not delete user caches as benchmark setup.
3. Retain per-sample/aggregate actual cache-hit counts, effective backend and executed stage/work counters. Reject or classify samples that did not exercise the required path; a configured provider or a preflight hit is not proof of timed provider work.
4. Define coldness precisely: cold process/index/model/result cache are distinct from OS filesystem cache. Clearing two object caches cannot certify all layers cold.
5. For real retrieval throughput/tail comparisons, allow a frozen representative query schedule with enough distinct misses and enough measured stage work/duration to expose the relevant algorithm. Record workload count/identity and variation; do not prescribe an arbitrary large quota or require a heavy campaign for this repair.
6. Keep cache-hit results out of an unqualified ANN-backend speedup claim. An intentionally cached user-path comparison should explicitly state its limited scope.

## Small discriminating acceptance

- With a fixed tiny fixture and quality `balanced`, prove the existing repeated-query path has a first miss followed by hits; retain that fact rather than silently treating every sample as a new retrieval.
- In the new actual-retrieval mode, instrument the existing query-embedding and sparse/ANN owners and require the declared measured call counts on every eligible sample, while preserving warm index/model ownership.
- In explicit result-cache mode, verify the opposite control: the hit count is reported and downstream search is skipped.
- An existing query-cache entry cannot be labeled a cold query miss merely because the index/SQLite maps were cleared.
- Repeat with cache-ineligible/fallback results, backend unavailable, and missing execution evidence: classify them without inventing successful work or zeros.
- Keep returned relevance/output parity fixed across modes; verify cache settings do not silently alter ranking or quality policy.

## Deduplication and limits

Reviewed all-state cached issues through #1723 plus the current updated-page refresh. #1251/#1281 optimize production query-cache behavior; they do not define this benchmark workload. #1655 concerns generic A/B eligibility, #1724 regex engine substitution, and #1725 sampled operation counts. This issue is the search microbenchmark's cache/work-identity boundary, not a production caching bug or a measured performance claim.

## Defect

The tinybench runner publishes percentage deltas against a saved report without checking that the two measurements did the same work. It matches only component names. A saved `search-sparse` result from another repository, query, index, or backend is therefore presented as the current component's baseline with an ordinary numeric delta.

This is not a complaint that the implementation-first branch has deferred full performance qualification. It is a concrete admission flaw in the comparison the runner already emits.

## Pinned source

PR #572 head `60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e`, current head rechecked 2026-10-24:

- [Configurable repo/mode/backend/query and timing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L21-L66) independently change the requested workload.
- [Shared default baseline path](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L112-L119) is `benchmarks/baselines/microbench.json`, not a workload-qualified namespace.
- [Result construction and comparison call](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L153-L173) records repoRoot/mode/requested backend/environment and timing settings, but no query, immutable corpus/index identity, effective retrieval/model identity, or result-cache work mode.
- [The measured call](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L191-L204) really uses the configurable query.
- [compareBaseline](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L376-L400) admits any parsed object with a truthy `components`, then compares each matching component. It does not even inspect the repoRoot/mode/backend/environment that both reports already contain.
- [Summary output](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/60dbba13fc856253c69b560867c71184f907e65e/tools/bench/micro/tinybench.js#L414-L428) prints those ordinary `delta` percentages without an incompatibility warning.

## Small deterministic counterexample

Two otherwise well-formed reports:

| Field | Saved baseline | Current run |
|---|---|---|
| repoRoot | repository A | repository B |
| backend | memory | sqlite-fts |
| component | search-sparse | search-sparse |
| meanMs | 100 | 50 |

The source unconditionally computes `((50 - 100) / 100) * 100 = -50%`. There is no workload-equivalence decision. Even keeping repo/backend identical but changing `--query` cannot be detected afterward because the query is absent from the report.

This is a source-derived counterexample, **not an executed benchmark or an observed speedup**.

## Repair / staging

1. Give the report an explicit schema and benchmark-workload identity: exact query or frozen query schedule/digest, mode, input corpus/index generation/content identity, relevant retrieval policy, requested/effective provider, dimensions/model/input-formatting identity and stub-versus-real mode, and the actual cache/work mode. Record code/runtime/hardware provenance separately.
2. Admit a baseline only when the comparison's controlled axes match. Return a structured `incomparable` disposition with specific differences instead of numeric performance deltas.
3. Support intentional comparisons such as backend A versus B through an explicit experiment declaration: hold corpus/query/results/work mode constant, label the varied axis, and verify both arms actually exercised their requested implementation. Do not impose source-revision equality when the purpose is measuring a code change.
4. Preserve old reports as historical data; do not silently bless a report lacking identity or overwrite a user's chosen baseline merely to make comparison succeed.
5. Coordinate the work-mode receipt with #1726. Fixing query-result-cache replay alone does not make unrelated reports comparable, and adding identity alone does not make cache hits measure retrieval.

## Acceptance

- Pure comparator tests: identical qualified workload; changed query/schedule, corpus/index, mode, effective backend, model/stub state and cache work; missing/legacy identity; explicitly declared intentional axis change; absent/invalid/zero-sample metrics.
- Every mismatched or unknown controlled axis must be visible and suppress ordinary speedup/regression percentages.
- A source-revision change with otherwise matched workload must remain comparable under the declared experiment.
- A small real runner smoke check on the supported runtime must prove the receipt reflects the actual requested query and effective execution, not only authored labels.
- Performance claims still require enough completed operations and sustained duration to exceed startup/timer noise, repeated/interleaved paired runs and raw count/duration/variation reporting. Comparison eligibility must not substitute for statistical evidence or result parity.

## Deduplication and scope

Reviewed the cached all-state backlog through #1723 and refreshed the latest 100 issues immediately before publication. #1655 owns A/B-sweep eligibility, #1687 throughput-file measurement admission, and #1441 bakeoff resume dataset identity; none owns this tinybench saved-report comparator. #1724/#1725 cover other microbenchmark engine/work-count defects. No production edits, user-machine access, project bootstrap or benchmark execution were performed for this report.

## Finding
The render-sort microbenchmark compares different rendered documents: its “current” arm sets `stats.sorted = true` on the same deliberately reverse-ordered pack used by the baseline, without sorting it first. The renderer correctly trusts the flag and skips sorting. Consequently a faster result is not qualified as an equivalent-output optimization.

Source-only audit of current PR #572 at `74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe`, rechecked 24 October 2026. No project code/test/benchmark was executed; no runtime speed or production-rendering defect is asserted.

## Pinned evidence and minimal witness
- [Fixture construction](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/graph/render-sort.js#L14-L36) emits descending distances and chunk IDs.
- [Comparison arms](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/graph/render-sort.js#L39-L58) change only the flag; they do not prepare a canonical current pack or compare outputs.
- [Renderer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/retrieval/output/graph-context-pack.js#L31-L47) copies arrays before sorting, so the baseline does **not** incidentally sort the shared fixture for the next arm.
- [Canonical node comparator](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/graph/ordering.js#L87-L90) orders distance ascending.

For `size=3`, the source-derived node order is:
- baseline: `[1] chunk:chunk-1`, `[2] chunk:chunk-2`, `[3] chunk:chunk-3`;
- current: `[3] chunk:chunk-3`, `[2] chunk:chunk-2`, `[1] chunk:chunk-1`.

This is a deterministic source trace, not an executed output. The existing [skip-resort test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tests/graph/context-pack-skip-resort.test.js) intentionally proves flag trust using unsorted data; that is a valid renderer contract, but not equivalence validation for the performance comparison. The timed helper discards returned results and the CLI emits `ok: true` regardless of parity.

## Repair / acceptance
1. Prepare an actually canonical current fixture with the shared node/edge/path comparators. Assert byte-identical rendered output outside the timed loop before accepting or printing comparative results. Include witness paths, ties, multiple edge kinds and deliberately shuffled input.
2. Decide the comparison explicitly: for **redundant re-sort removal**, feed the same already sorted pack to both arms; for **upstream preparation amortization**, report preparation separately and include it in the stated end-to-end/amortized result. Do not compare sorting reverse input against a falsely tagged reverse input.
3. Emit workload shape, output digest/count, preparation policy and measured completed operations. Fail or mark incomparable if output differs.
4. Include realistic presorted and shuffled shapes and larger sizes; use warmup/repeated sufficiently long samples, not only the default five renders of 2,000 nodes. Report preparation and rendering costs separately rather than inferring an application speedup.

All-state backlog reviewed; existing graph contract consolidation and skip-sort behavior are not this benchmark-equivalence defect. No production edit is requested merely to stop trusting the valid sorted contract.

<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Finding
The graph-store “lazy-load” comparison currently requests the **same expensive artifact families and complete graph assembly in both arms**, then runs the second arm on the first arm's already warmed store. It can report a baseline/current timing delta without exercising the intended lazy omission.

Current PR #572 `74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe`, rechecked 24 October 2026. Source-only: no benchmark, repository test or graph load was executed. This is benchmark design/qualification, not a claim that production graph selection emits incorrect results.

## Exact source trace
[store-lazy-load.js, lines 18–59](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tools/bench/graph/store-lazy-load.js#L18-L59) creates one store, then:
- baseline passes `['callGraph', 'usageGraph', 'importGraph']`;
- current passes `['callGraph']`;
- both use the same `includeCsr` policy and different graph-index cache keys;
- every iteration within each arm reuses that arm's cache key.

Under [loadGraphIndex's actual admission predicates](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/graph/store.js#L540-L563), the two selections resolve identically:

| Admission | Baseline | Current |
| --- | --- | --- |
| graph_relations | yes | yes |
| graph_relations_csr | same availability/policy | same availability/policy |
| symbol_edges | no | no |
| call_sites pair index | same availability | same availability |

The selected graph list is not used to slice graph_relations before [buildGraphIndex](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/graph/store.js#L622-L632), which prepares [all three relation families](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/graph/store.js#L227-L257). This is consistent with the store's existing artifact-level lazy boundary; changing the array alone does not construct a smaller relation artifact.

Meanwhile [loadOnce](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/src/graph/store.js#L447-L457) memoizes each artifact representation in that store. On a fresh compare process, baseline's first iteration owns actual artifact reads, its later iterations are index-cache hits, current's first iteration builds another index from the already resolved same artifact promises, and its later iterations are also index-cache hits. The benchmark returns only aggregate timing summaries, omitting the store's available artifact-use/build/cache telemetry.

Increasing iterations chiefly increases cache-hit observations; it does not repeat cold lazy admission. `mode=current` in a fresh process also has a different artifact-cache history from the current arm in `mode=compare`.

## Existing behavior to preserve
The [lazy-edge-load contract test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/74f59e3c91cf363c16661a45ec40b95d7c7068fe/tests/graph/lazy-edge-load.test.js) does exercise a real boundary: selecting `symbolEdges` alone loads only `symbol_edges`. Current source also drains all started artifact reads on failure and avoids unused string adjacency for admitted CSR. This issue does not reopen those repairs.

## Acceptance / implementation direction
1. Define a real comparison for the same downstream task: e.g. eager load-all versus selecting only a required artifact family, using fixtures with substantial omitted families. Do not just relabel two equivalent selections. If the desired optimization is intra-graph-family projection, measure it only after that boundary actually exists.
2. Separate cold admission/build from warm index hits. Isolate application caches with fresh workers/processes (creating a new store alone does not necessarily clear module-level caches), or an explicit owned test reset; retain identical OS-cache policy and balanced arm order.
3. Assert expected artifact reads/bytes, index-build counts, cache misses/hits and semantic result parity before qualifying a delta. Emit those facts with each arm. Mark the lazy comparison unavailable when the fixture contains no meaningful omitted work.
4. Vary total relation nodes/edges, call-site occurrences and symbol-edge bytes independently. Include both small contract cases and substantial skewed omitted-family cases. Run sustained/repeated timing samples and report cold distributions separately from warm distributions; retain manifest/integrity admission costs rather than bypassing them.
5. Preserve production graph-selection semantics and exact evidence. No requirement to load fewer correctness-required artifacts or weaken admission.

Dedup: closed #243 owns the broader language benchmark-mode program, not this graph-store microbenchmark; #621 owns explicit empty graph selection, not these two nonempty equivalent loader plans; #706's duplicate-adjacency repair is present. Current comments and all-state backlog were checked.

issue.title: [P2] Worker-pool lifecycle loses cleanup handle when destroy rejects
issue.body:
### Resolved — Windows consumer qualification

Failed worker teardown retains its exact pool and original cleanup capability until confirmed closure. Controlled rejection/retry, concurrent initialization/restart, timeout, sibling isolation and actual worker/process controls preserve exactly-once retirement.

Validated on source [`27c2a65af`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/commit/27c2a65afe7c47e2682733992ce34ca360022819), published in PR #572. The batch passes273 distinct affected/gate cases and all eight publish checks, including40 gate cases, with zero latest failures, timeouts, skips or native crashes. [Source-bound receipt and original failure history](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/156e61eb19511da3c3ba5af96eef9836c89af1c0/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.md).

<details>
<summary>Passing coverage</summary>

`indexing/workers/worker-pool-lifecycle-destroy-during-restart`, `indexing/workers/worker-pool-lifecycle-destroy`, `indexing/workers/worker-pool-destroy-timeout`, `indexing/workers/worker-pool-group-cleanup`, `indexing/workers/worker-pool-initialization-cleanup`, `indexing/workers/worker-pool-stuck-drain-cleanup`, `indexing/workers/cleanup-rejection-owner-retry`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Original report and acceptance criteria</summary>

---

## Finding
`shutdownPool` clears the lifecycle's `pool` reference **before** `destroyPiscinaPool` completes ([lifecycle.js lines 98-131](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/index/build/workers/pool/lifecycle.js#L98-L131)). If `pool.destroy()` rejects for a non-timeout reason, `destroyPiscinaPool` rethrows without hard-stop fallback ([piscina-cleanup.js lines 87-119](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d/src/shared/piscina-cleanup.js#L87-L119)); the lifecycle has already lost the sole pool handle. A retry sees `!pool` and cannot reattempt cleanup, while a later restart could create another pool with the old threads still owned externally.

## Direct reproduction
With an injected mock pool whose `destroy()` rejects `Error('destroy failed')`, initialize a `createWorkerPoolLifecycle` and call `forceDestroy()`. It rejects as expected, but `getPool()` is `null` after one destroy attempt; the mock remains available only to the test harness, not to the lifecycle. No real worker pool or active index was touched.

## Expected
Retain the current pool until teardown succeeds or make a failed pool explicitly available for retry/hard termination, with fault-injection coverage for non-timeout destroy rejection. This is distinct from the known general worker teardown umbrella issues. Pure mock probe only; full runner not invoked under unsupported local Node 26.8.1/unverified bootstrap.

</details>

comments.body:
# [P2] Runtime/group teardown wrappers hide falsey worker failures and prevent retry of retained pool ownership

Classification: source-proven composition defect; prefer follow-up/reopen #1033 and cross-link #1035 rather than a new duplicate. Pin `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. Static review only; no execution or new platform qualification claimed.

## Credit and remaining defect
The leaf lifecycle and process-pool repairs are real: unsuccessful teardown retains the original handle/reservation, rejects replacement and clears failed cleanup promises to permit explicit retry. The public runtime path defeats that behavior at two enclosing levels.

1. `src/index/build/runtime/workers.js:698–721` wraps the acquired pool aggregate. Its `firstError = null`, `if (!firstError)`, and `if (firstError)` conflate presence with truthiness. Rejection with `null`, `false`, `0`, or `''` disappears if the crash logger closes successfully; if logger close also rejects, the original falsey failure is overwritten. A truthy failure is memoized permanently in `destroyWorkerPoolsPromise`.
2. Split aggregate `src/index/build/workers/pool.js:993–1020` registers both pool cleanup callbacks in the general lifecycle registry and permanently caches `lifecycle.close()`. `src/shared/lifecycle/registry.js:159–174` snapshots and clears resources before invoking close, and permanently retains its close promise. A second explicit aggregate destroy cannot reach the failed child's retryable lifecycle.
3. These are supported public consumers, not a misuse of a private helper. Runtime creation installs this actual aggregate at `runtime/runtime.js:1086–1114,1336–1338`; teardown chooses it instead of individual pools at `src/integrations/core/build-index/runtime.js:76–92`. Cache-writer shutdown treats the aggregate as covering tokenize/quantize children at `src/index/build/cache-writer-drain.js:80–90`, so it neither bypasses nor repairs the cached failed owner. Shutdown mode does not apply the non-shutdown idle check at lines94–95.

## Trigger and consequence
Acquire the real runtime wrapper (both shared and split modes). Cause the original worker destroy/termination attempt to reject before closure is confirmed. For falsey rejection, the wrapper reports success even though the repaired leaf still owns its child; downstream drain sees a fulfilled owner rather than failed cleanup. For ordinary Error/frozen failure, attempt explicit cleanup again after the original owner becomes terminable: runtime/group returns the cached rejection without retrying that child. Capacity/handles remain retained correctly below but cannot be retired through the supported aggregate entrypoint. Do not repair by freeing capacity on rejection.

The strongest invariant is exact owner closure, not merely absence of a thrown exception. The falsey path is separately certain from direct wrapper control flow; practical child-lifetime consequences depend on rejection occurring before actual close rather than a diagnostic throwing after successful close.

## Existing coverage does not exercise this composition
`tests/indexing/workers/cleanup-rejection-owner-retry.test.js` correctly exercises direct leaf falsey/frozen rejection and original-owner retry. `worker-pool-group-cleanup.test.js:9–26` replaces quantize destroy with a function which first awaits original successful destroy and only then throws; caching that already-settled diagnostic proves idempotence, not retry of an unsettled owner. `tests/indexing/runtime/teardown-original-failure-observations.test.js:95–149` uses stub runtime.workerPools; it proves outer category preservation/retry, not the actual runtime wrapper factory. Existing Windows receipts retain their authored scope and are not invalidated by static review.

## Implementation instructions
- Introduce explicit failure-presence booleans/arrays; preserve exact rejected values and first operational cause without truthiness tests. Compose both worker and logger failures, including frozen and primitive values.

issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Completed — 2026-10-29

Stage1 treats absent/invalid lifecycle timestamps explicitly and releases the real external abort listener even for empty modalities; valid epoch-zero and late-abort controls pass.

Qualified on Windows x64 with Node26.13.0, one job, 30-second fixture bounds and zero retries. Direct controls: `indexing/stage1/process-files-zero-modality-elision`. Original positive/negative controls and failed receipts are retained in the [source-bound qualification archive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json). Published implementation: `66e340c0c7f71ef81b61e63f87fb38ce0499a4db`; publication receipt: `dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58`.
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Finding
`processFiles` attaches `forwardAbort` to an external `abortSignal` at function entry (`src/index/build/indexer/steps/process-files.js`, near lines 376–395). The zero-files/zero-chunks modality branch returns around line 439, before the cleanup `finally` around line 3180 where `detachExternalAbort()` is called. Each empty modality therefore leaves a listener on a possibly long-lived parent signal and retains its stage controller/closure.

## Expected
Detach in the early-return branch or wrap listener ownership around the entire function. Add a focused fixture using an instrumented signal and empty entries/chunks to assert listener count returns to baseline.

Source reviewed at `9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d`; no full indexing run was needed for this source-level leak.

The new parent listener remains; repeated calls accumulate listeners on the already-aborted signal and retain the forwarding closure/stage controller. 1. Give the external forwarding listener an outer lexical `try/finally` spanning every operation after acquisition, including pre-abort validation, logger callbacks, initialization awaits and the zero-modality return. Keep internal resource teardown nested so it accesses only initialized owners.
2. Alternatively reject before acquiring this listener, **and** still ensure later initialization failures cannot bypass listener release. A one-line precheck alone repairs the exact witness but leaves the acquisition-to-inner-try gap.
3. Remove only this invocation's exact listener; preserve unrelated parent listeners and original AbortError/cause. Make detach idempotent and never turn an aborted call into successful elision.
4. Reuse the existing forwarding/lifecycle owners; do not add a parallel controller registry or global listener cleanup.

### Acceptance and negative controls
- Through actual public `processFiles`, pre-aborted empty and nonempty inputs reject canonically and listener count returns to baseline, including repeated calls against the same aborted controller.
- Inject a throwing `crashLogger.updatePhase` and a controlled startup rejection before the existing stage try; retain the primary failure and restore listeners.
- Preserve healthy empty elision, late abort after completion, normal nonempty cleanup, mid-stage cancellation propagation and a preinstalled unrelated abort listener.
- Assert exact listener identities/counts, not only elision logs. No forced GC or sleeps needed.

### Measurement plan
Record before/after listener counts for N repeated rejected entries; expected invariant is constant count. If heap characterization is desired later, measure retained closures separately with task-owned instrumentation. No throughput or memory-byte gain is asserted from static review.

### Compatibility and delivery
This changes listener lifetime, not abort timing, stage selection, timestamp semantics or output schemas. Keep the normal fast path and historical Windows receipt credited. Review the outer-scope refactor against every early exit before enabling it; reverting implementation shape must not restore the pre-abort leak. No new runtime dependency or public option is needed.

issue.title: [P2] Canceled worker tokenization is retried on the main thread and can return success
issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Qualified repair — 2026-10-29

**Status: Fixed and qualified on Windows at `47d1f6058ec32eb0eda8ed575e62182de6c10ffd` (PR #572).**

Aborted worker/parser work preserves cancellation and pending native ownership through CPU and token handoff. It cannot silently retry on the main thread and publish success.

Passing controls: `indexing/workers/worker-pool-stuck-drain-real-worker`, `indexing/file-processor/token-worker-abort-and-evidence`, `indexing/file-processor/tokenization-line-stream-boundary`, `indexing/runtime/worker-pool-default-concurrency`, `indexing/runtime/worker-pool-explicit-policy`, `indexing/tokenization/native-leaf-product-reuse`, `indexing/tree-sitter/async-request-cancellation-boundaries`, `indexing/workers/pressure-reconfigure-admission-authority`, `indexing/workers/hard-pressure-no-progress`. Node 26.13.0; one job, 30-second limits, zero retries and native-status redo disabled. The batch records 255 distinct affected/gate passes and the complete pre-push gate. The separate #1350 semantic-drain timeout and #1362 sidecar fault matrix remain open.

[Published receipt](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/0afde906d49a1ca135a27483a46d1eeba000d932/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.md) · [Exact source bindings and raw-log hashes](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/0afde906d49a1ca135a27483a46d1eeba000d932/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json).
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Finding
`processChunks` (`src/index/build/file-processor/process-chunks/token-flow.js`) catches *every* rejection from scheduled worker `runTokenize` and disables the worker before falling back to synchronous `tokenizeChunkText`; it does not distinguish abort/cancellation. The function receives `signal` but performs no abort check before the fallback or before returning. `attachEmbeddings` immediately returns without checking the signal when embeddings are disabled (`src/index/build/file-processor/embeddings.js`). Thus cancellation of a worker tokenization task can trigger full CPU fallback and return chunk results instead of promptly propagating the abort for sparse-only builds. The worker wrapper in `src/index/build/workers/indexer-worker.js` also wraps errors in a plain `Error` via `formatWorkerError`, losing the original abort `name`/`code`, so cancellation needs signal-based detection or preserved error metadata.

## Expected
Re-throw abort errors or check `signal` in the worker catch and before main-thread fallback/return; preserve cancellation identity across the worker boundary. Keep fallback only for genuine worker failures. Add a focused canceled-worker fixture with embeddings disabled and assert an abort rejection and no synchronous retry.

## Audit provenance
Current source HEAD `9a2380368131c3bca35d1a05b46e9e7f90f9467d`; source/caller proof. Did not execute a full native worker build because local Node is below supported floor. Existing issue search found no matching cancellation/fallback issue.

## Current-head repair credit and remaining parser boundary (2026-10-23)

Rechecked PR #572 `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`. The tokenizer path now forwards `{ signal }`, checks unsafe queue recovery/abort before inline fallback and checks before tokenization; preserve that repair rather than reimplementing it.

The Tree-sitter extension already recorded in [the existing comment](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/issues/1102#issuecomment-6329669867) remains open in current source. [buildTreeSitterChunksAsync](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/lang/tree-sitter/chunking.js#L940-L1040) passes `options.abortSignal` to `pool.run`, but its catch only protects a contained-file session before logging and synchronously reparsing. Cache return, queue-full fallback, pool-unavailable fallback and successful worker return lack an explicit matching abort fence. Current JS and TS [managed adapter preparation](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js#L374-L431) still call this async parser entrypoint.

Complete the existing issue with a recording parser/pool fixture that proves no sync parse and no cache publication after the request is aborted. Include already-aborted warm-cache input, abort during a deferred worker, worker fulfillment after abort, a queue-full decision while aborted, and an ordinary recoverable worker failure control. Preserve the original cancellation and any pending native/worker cleanup ownership; do not merely rename a still-running task's rejection. Verify file/build cancellation is actually carried through the language-context options at the real caller, not just supplied by the test directly to the leaf. No new native/runtime execution was performed in this audit.

comments.body:
# [P2] Retain running-thread cancellation ownership until the original Worker exits

**Disposition:** precise follow-up to closed #1102, whose existing comments explicitly require retaining running worker ownership until termination. Credit the repaired signal forwarding, abort propagation, and no-inline-fallback behavior. This is a remaining physical-lifetime boundary, not a claim that cancellation now publishes successful token results. Cross-link #1033/#1035 only for the distinct teardown-retry composition work; #1397 concerns subprocess/cache-lock propagation, not this thread-task lifetime.

**Evidence:** read-only source audit at `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`; no tests, worker execution, builds or benchmarks. The exact locked Piscina 5.3.2 tarball was fetched from its official npm registry URL and verified against package-lock SHA-512 integrity. Only its compiled implementation sources were inspected; no package code was executed. This is stronger than assuming generic cancellation behavior from library documentation.

## Supported caller and failure sequence
1. Real token processing forwards the request signal through `runProc` to `workerPool.tokenizeChunk` (`src/index/build/file-processor/process-chunks/token-flow.js:398–399`); bounded batch dispatch does the same and reserves CPU plus input/output bytes (`488–491`). These are supported production calls, not an unawaited helper misuse.
2. The facade passes that signal into the thread backend (`src/index/build/workers/pool.js:698–701`). It properly rejects cancellation and does not recover inline (`705–715`).
3. In locked Piscina `dist/index.js:422–430`, an abort first rejects the task with `AbortError`. For an already-running task it then calls `_removeWorker` and `_ensureMinimumWorkers`. `_removeWorker:271–274` calls `workerInfo.destroy()` without awaiting original exit. `dist/worker_pool/index.js:73–87` calls `worker.terminate()` without awaiting its promise, cleans task bookkeeping and marks destruction. Piscina's registered destruction callback emits `workerDestroy` (`dist/index.js:160–162`). The ordinary request promise is therefore not an exit receipt.
4. `src/index/build/workers/thread-pool.js:28–29` marks that original owner retiring. Its later exit deliberately does not poison the pool (`85–89`). The wrapper's `run` registers a retained-CPU scheduler wait and attaches an exact settlement only when `this.fatal` exists (`128–142`). Ordinary aborted removal has no fatal error and returns Piscina's undecorated abort rejection.
5. The facade's `awaitBackendFailureSettlement` returns immediately when the error has no own `workerSettlement` descriptor (`pool.js:66–69`). Its `finally` consequently decrements `backendTasks`, releases language throttle and drains request accounting (`732–737`) before original exit is known. The same helper guards analyze/quantize paths (`805`, `886`). Keeping the old Worker in `thread-pool.owners` is useful eventual teardown ownership but does not retain these task reservations.
6. The scheduler only joins registered waits (`scheduler-core/dispatch.js:343–350`) or preserves an error's pending resource observation (`385–400`). This ordinary abort supplies neither, so `retire` releases the task's reserved resources and pumps another job (`365–376`). The process backend already registers its actual ownership settlement with `retainCpu:true`; preserve that model rather than introducing another scheduler.

A deterministic witness is a running token task, an abort, and a controlled interval before the original Worker's `exit`. At that interval the current code can consider the task's CPU/bytes/throttle released despite the original Worker not having retired. Piscina can create its replacement in the same abort handler. We do **not** claim a particular overlap duration, observed OOM, continued artifact writing, or measured throughput loss; those require execution evidence. The exact invariant is that logical request rejection is being treated as physical lifetime completion.

## Repair instructions
- Give each accepted thread dispatch an original-owner settlement capability, including ordinary running-task abort. Bind it to the actual affected original Worker/generation; do not mistake the newly created replacement, pool queue length, a `workerDestroy` event, or a terminate request for exit.
- Register retained compute with the current scheduler lease before a caller can observe cancellation, and preserve the exact pending/released/settlement capability through the facade. Reuse existing failure-settlement and resource-observation contracts. Keep original abort identity plus cleanup evidence independently.
- Distinguish queued/pre-aborted tasks (never acquired a Worker) from running-task termination. Do not wait for unrelated healthy idle Workers to exit, poison a healthy generation solely because a request was canceled, or block forever on all Workers in the pool.
- Do not patch Piscina internals informally. Encapsulate the required event/task association in the existing adapter with explicit dependency-version compatibility, or use a documented backend cancellation design that can prove the affected original owner. A conservative bounded owner set may be acceptable only if its drain and liveness are proven.
- Keep confirmed normal completion fast, preserve non-abort task failure/fatal behavior, and keep aggregate teardown retry separately owned. If completion is publicly rejected before physical drain, retain reservations in the canonical scheduler until exact settlement rather than releasing/reacquiring optimistically.

## Acceptance and qualification
1. Recording adapter test: running task rejects AbortError, emits workerDestroy, but holds original exit. Assert CPU/byte reservation, backend task and throttle ownership remain held; competing resource-consuming work cannot use those permits. Release only on that original exit.
2. Actual supported Node/locked-Piscina integration after bootstrap: distinguish request rejection and Worker exit with captured original handles. Assert no admission gap; do not rely on a sleep-based chance of catching it.
3. Queued and already-aborted requests acquire no physical worker ownership and settle without waiting for unrelated threads. Healthy concurrent siblings continue normally.
4. Batch and single token calls, quantize and coarse-analysis calls preserve cancellation, no inline fallback, no result/cache publication, and exact resource settlement. Cover canceled owner versus replacement-generation identity.
5. Retain existing fatal-thread, original-handle teardown, delayed cleanup and process-backend controls. Test duplicate abort/exit and settlement-observer failure without double release.
6. Measure canceled-task-to-exit latency, reserved CPU/bytes versus live original workers, peak replacement overlap, event-loop overhead and ordinary steady-state throughput. Report measurements and uncertainty; no performance claim follows from source inspection alone.

## Existing qualification boundary
The cited `worker-pool-stuck-drain-real-worker` fixture explicitly drives lifecycle destruction and checks zero pool threads after forced drain. It does not drive `IndexerThreadPool.run` ordinary task AbortSignal cancellation under a scheduler lease. Its successful result does not establish this missing boundary. Existing #1102 signal/fallback repairs remain credited.

Primary dependency references: [Piscina 5.3.2 run/abort implementation](https://github.com/piscinajs/piscina/blob/v5.3.2/src/index.ts), [Worker owner implementation](https://github.com/piscinajs/piscina/blob/v5.3.2/src/worker_pool/index.ts), [official exact package](https://registry.npmjs.org/piscina/-/piscina-5.3.2.tgz).

### Exact adapter and consumer anchors
- [src/index/build/workers/thread-pool.js:16–142](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/workers/thread-pool.js#L16-L142)
- [src/index/build/workers/pool.js:66–77](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/workers/pool.js#L66-L77)
- [src/index/build/workers/pool.js:698–737](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/workers/pool.js#L698-L737)
- [src/index/build/file-processor/process-chunks/token-flow.js:488–491](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/file-processor/process-chunks/token-flow.js#L488-L491)
- [src/shared/concurrency/scheduler-core/dispatch.js:343–400](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/concurrency/scheduler-core/dispatch.js#L343-L400)

### Migration and rollback
Version the adapter conformance expectation against the locked dependency and supported Node runtime. Land task-to-original-owner association before enabling weighted native capacity experiments. Normal completion, queued cancellation and process transport keep their existing behavior. If a proposed association cannot identify the affected owner without indefinite waiting on unrelated workers, decline that adapter design rather than releasing early. Dependency upgrades must rerun the exact running-versus-queued cancellation matrix; no blanket upgrade or private-library patch is prescribed.

issue.title: [P2] Exclude Lua declaration headers from call relations without removing real recursion
issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Completed — 2026-10-29

Lua assignment functions retain complete local/assignment identities and grammar-based signatures; real recursion stays while declaration headers stay out of calls, with unsupported forms explicit.

Qualified on Windows x64 with Node26.13.0, one job, 30-second fixture bounds and zero retries. Direct controls: `lang/contracts/lua-assignment-call-consumer-acceptance`. Original positive/negative controls and failed receipts are retained in the [source-bound qualification archive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json). Published implementation: `66e340c0c7f71ef81b61e63f87fb38ce0499a4db`; publication receipt: `dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58`.
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Reproduction
```lua
function plain(value)
 return value
end
function caller()
 return plain(1)
end
```
Real pinned Lua parsing succeeds. The actual registered relation adapter emits:
- `plain -> plain`, although `plain` makes no call;
- `caller -> caller`, although `caller` is not recursive;
- `caller -> plain`, the legitimate call.
All three survive the default relation-lexicon policy, call-index construction and per-chunk relation projection. A separate genuinely recursive `function recur(value) return recur(value) end` control emits `recur -> recur`, so globally filtering self-edges would remove a real call rather than repair extraction.

## Cause and impact
[buildLuaRelations](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e/src/lang/lua.js#L358-L370) passes the entire declaration slice, including its header, into [the dotted-call regex](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e/src/lang/lua.js#L68-L76). The identifier before the header's parenthesis is indistinguishable from a call to that regex. Nested function declarations can similarly appear as calls by their containing function even without invocation.
[Registered Lua preparation/relations](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e/src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js#L305-L316) uses this helper. [CPU relation processing](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e/src/index/build/file-processor/cpu.js#L354-L384) retains it in the call index, and [buildChunkRelations](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e/src/index/language-registry/registry.js#L180-L200) emits it in the chunk's relation payload. This proves false call evidence in the legacy chunk consumer, not a claim that every later graph algorithm necessarily retains a self-edge.

## Repair and acceptance
Collect actual call-expression roles from the already available syntax, or restrict a bounded lexical collector to executable body spans while excluding declaration headers and nested callable bodies from the wrong owner. Preserve real recursive calls, local functions, method-call normalization, anonymous functions and ordinary dotted calls. Do not solve it by deleting `caller === callee` or by suppressing all locally declared names.

Add exact-edge assertions for call-free, single-call, recursive and nested functions, declaration-only inner functions versus actually invoked ones, method declarations and quoted/commented call-like text. Test the registered adapter through lexicon and chunk projection, not only positive `some(call exists)` checks. Review producer-version invalidation.

All-state Lua/function, self-call/false-call and collector-name searches found no equivalent owner. #1468 is declaration identity/scope classification, not scanning declaration syntax as executable calls.

## Verification and limits
Live PR #572 head `f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e` rechecked before filing. Exact fetched source blobs match Git blob hashes. Fifteen bounded parse-clean defect/control fixtures run on the current Node **26.12.1** pin, Linux x64, with lockfile-exact tree-sitter 0.25.0, Bash 0.25.1, scoped Lua 0.4.1 and Perl 1.1.1. The runtime and Perl scanner include the current repository patches, reverse-dry-run verified; Perl scanner rebuilt from the patched source. Native grammar loading uses the unchanged production loader/specs. Adapter/helper bodies are unchanged source excerpts with parser dependency wiring to real native ASTs, not fabricated trees. The registered adapter spec/factory, real chunk limits, default lexicon filtering with checked-in language wordlists, call-index construction and chunk-relation projection execute where applicable. These are focused semantic/consumer proofs, not normal bootstrap, full index, native-lifecycle, Windows/platform or full-suite qualification. No shell or Perl source fixture was executed, and no repository implementation was changed.

Reviewed the current issue and full comments against `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. Evidence below is exact-source/static dependency inspection, not a fresh parser/test/build/benchmark execution. Prior executed receipts remain credited only to their recorded commit, route and assertions.



### Concrete remaining boundary

[buildLuaRelations](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/lang/lua.js#L392-L422) selects syntax call facts when present. Its lexical path at lines404–405 removes everything through the first newline of each function chunk:

```lua
function recur(n) return recur(n - 1)
end
```

The existing fallback declaration scanner at lines299–383 recognizes the first-line declaration and standalone closing `end`, so this is not a hypothetical unchunkable input. But the relation scanner receives only `end` and loses the genuine `recur -> recur` edge. Replacing the recursive call with `work(n)` similarly loses an ordinary body edge. The declaration header must be excluded, not the entire first physical line. A subsequent-line call is unaffected.

The current [Lua consumer fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tests/lang/contracts/lua-assignment-call-consumer-acceptance.test.js) contains same-line recursion but invokes `prepareRegisteredLanguage`, whose default [native options](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tests/helpers/native-declaration-acceptance.js#L10-L14) require enabled/strict native parsing. It therefore does not protect the intended lexical fallback explicitly requested in #1477's prior comment.

### Implementation guidance

Have the existing fallback declaration/header owner retain the actual header-end/body-start coordinate. Consume that range rather than skipping a line, while preserving strings/comments and nested declaration ownership. Do not remove all selfedges as a shortcut: real recursion must survive. Avoid creating a second approximate signature parser if the existing lexical boundary owner can supply the coordinate. Unsupported ambiguous boundaries should be explicit partial evidence, not confidently empty calls. Bump the relevant call/source producer replay identity through its existing owner.

### Focused acceptance

Run native and explicitly disabled/unavailable-native routes separately. Independently assert edges for same-header-line ordinary call and recursion with following-line `end`; subsequent-line equivalents; no-call header negative; quoted/commented call-looking text; nested callable ownership and assignment-style declarations. Include real registered relations/payload and warm incremental replay. Preserve bounds and original source offsets. No broad benchmark is needed to prove this semantic defect.

### Non-duplication

All-state Lua/fallback search reviewed #1476/#1477/#1484/#740/#682. #1477 directly owns header exclusion and retained real recursion, including fallback in its comments. #1476 owns assignment declaration attribution, which is independently repaired.

### Compatibility and bounded validation
Retain the existing repaired route as a positive control and change the appropriate existing projection/import identity before replay can reuse changed semantics. Roll back route selection independently from cache validity; never relabel defective old output as current. For later authorized measurement, compare source bytes examined, scan/projection CPU, allocations and retained output on the same independently expected evidence. A lexical-boundary or source-envelope repair is not evidence of a throughput gain.
