issue.title: [P2] Preserve Starlark argument lexical roles when collecting build imports
issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Completed — 2026-10-29

Actual config/template/build consumers preserve complete literal identities, Unicode and lexical argument roles, rejecting dynamic/comment/recipe impostors through real resolution.

Qualified on Windows x64 with Node26.13.0, one job, 30-second fixture bounds and zero retries. Direct controls: `lang/contracts/logical-build-template-import-acceptance`. Original positive/negative controls and failed receipts are retained in the [source-bound qualification archive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json). Published implementation: `66e340c0c7f71ef81b61e63f87fb38ce0499a4db`; publication receipt: `dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58`.
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Reproduced defect
The scanner skips comments while locating balanced Starlark calls, but then extracts argument values from the original unmasked argument text. Ordinary comments inside valid calls suppress the real dependency or replace it with commented-out text.

```starlark
load(
    # where the helpers live
    ":helpers.bzl",
    "build_helper",
)
```
Observed imports: `[]`, versus `[":helpers.bzl"]` without the comment.

```starlark
bazel_dep(
    # name = "wrong"
    name = "right",
    version = "1.0.0",
)
```
Observed imports: `["@wrong"]`, not `["@right"]`.

```starlark
local_path_override(
    module_name = "dep",
    # path = "wrong"
    path = "../right",
)
```
Observed imports: `["wrong"]`, not `["../right"]`. The load and MODULE.bazel cases are independent file fixtures; no mixed-context build execution is implied.

## Root cause and consumer
[readFirstQuotedArgument](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/language-registry/import-collectors/starlark.js#L40-L69) skips whitespace only, so a leading argument comment makes the first character # instead of a quote. The [bazel_dep and local_path_override branches](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/language-registry/import-collectors/starlark.js#L235-L254) regex-match name/path inside raw call.args and choose the first occurrence even in a comment.

The existing balanced scanner already knows comment/string state, but only uses it to find the closing delimiter, not to provide token-aware argument extraction. The same first-argument helper also handles use_extension.

Executing the [registered Starlark adapter](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/language-registry/adapters/heuristic.js#L854-L862) and [registry normalizer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/language-registry/registry.js#L86-L119) preserves the exact incorrect outcomes. In particular @wrong receives a normal starlark-label collector hint with confidence 0.9; no downstream sanitization removes the comment-derived dependency. The adapter's file relations contain the same imports.

## Repair and acceptance
Read positional/keyword arguments with the same lexical state used to locate the call. Skip comments outside strings without deleting comment markers inside string values; match only the requested argument binding, not strings or commented examples. Keep existing budgets, label hints, argument order and real post-comment imports.

Test comments before the first positional argument, between a keyword and its value, before/after name/path bindings, inline comments, multiline strings, escaped quotes and # characters inside genuine labels, and unchanged no-comment controls across load/use_extension/bazel_dep/local_path_override. Assert collector entries, hints, registry imports and file relations. Review semantic cache invalidation. No Bazel evaluation is needed.

## Dedup and evidence
All-state Starlark/comment/import/exact-collector searches found no matching owner. Closed #258 covers build-system resolver staging; #1194 covers configured snapshots; neither fixes this current argument lexer. #931/#932 concern other language comment scanners, not this Starlark post-scan handoff. [The Starlark language specification](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md#lexical-elements) defines comments as non-code.

Exact Node 26.12.1/Linux; tiny inert fixtures; real exported collector/helpers plus literal unchanged registered factory/normalizer bodies. Python ast.parse accepts each selected Starlark-subset fixture without evaluation; this is a syntax cross-check, not actual Bazel qualification. Re-fetch at live PR #572 head `13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8` confirms cited collector, adapter, registry normalizer and file consumer blobs unchanged from executed `f4519baf244be4f4e16d061a11bfa5890f32496e`. No build/fixture/project scripts, full index/bootstrap/suite or implementation changes.

## Current-source follow-up — 2026-10-30

Reviewed the current issue and full comments against `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. Evidence below is exact-source/static dependency inspection, not a fresh parser/test/build/benchmark execution. Prior executed receipts remain credited only to their recorded commit, route and assertions.



### Concrete remaining boundary

The [outer Starlark scanner](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/language-registry/import-collectors/starlark.js#L55-L119) handles escapes in ordinary quoted strings (75–97), but its triple-single/triple-double branches (61–73) terminate on any three quote characters without checking whether the first is escaped. The same scanner controls balanced call-body scanning (122–129) and top-level call collection (132 onward).

This valid Starlark source contains no actual first load:

```starlark
text = """prefix \"""
load(":phantom.bzl", "symbol")
"""
load(":real.bzl", "symbol")
```

The first quote in `\"""` is escaped, leaving two literal quotes, so the string remains open. The production scanner instead exits its triple-string state there, admits the string-contained `load`, then treats the actual closing triple delimiter as a new opening string and can suppress the real following load. This yields both a phantom dependency and a missing real dependency. It is not merely a display preview error; collector entries reach registered import resolution/replay.

The [Starlark specification](https://github.com/bazelbuild/starlark/blob/master/spec.md#string-literals) defines string escapes and triple-quoted literals. Current logical-build-template-import acceptance covers ordinary triples and escaped ordinary quotes, not an escaped quote at a triple terminator boundary. #1503's chunker uses a different escape-aware lexical state; its body/source repair is credited and should not be reopened for this import defect.

### Implementation guidance

Unify quote/escape transition semantics for the outer scan and balanced argument reader, ideally sharing a bounded lexical primitive with the existing static-argument owner rather than copying another scanner. Track escape parity in triple strings and respect raw literal quote behavior where admitted. Keep exact label/value/source spans, literal-vs-dynamic distinction, current source/token/match limits and explicit incomplete coverage. Do not execute Starlark or resolve labels speculatively. Invalidate affected import producer replay identity.

### Focused acceptance

Triple-single and triple-double variants; odd/even backslash runs before delimiter; fake `load`/`use_extension`/`bazel_dep` text inside strings followed by a real admitted call; comment/ordinary-string negatives; LF/CRLF and Unicode offsets; escaped delimiters inside balanced arguments. Assert exact independent import set and literal values through the registered collector and existing merge/cache route, with cold/warm parity and a small source-budget boundary. Assert no phantom dependency edge, not just producer self-equality.

### Non-duplication

All-state triple/escape search returns #1493/#1503/#682; Starlark import search also reviewed titles/body scope of #1484/#1194/#1704/#258. #1493 directly owns argument lexical roles and multiline/escaped-string controls; #1704 is label resolution identity, not string-boundary admission. Full #1493 body/comments read.

### Compatibility and bounded validation
Retain the existing repaired route as a positive control and change the appropriate existing projection/import identity before replay can reuse changed semantics. Roll back route selection independently from cache validity; never relabel defective old output as current. For later authorized measurement, compare source bytes examined, scan/projection CPU, allocations and retained output on the same independently expected evidence. A lexical-boundary or source-envelope repair is not evidence of a throughput gain.

issue.body: ### Completed — 2026-10-29 SQL/XML consumers preserve dialect-aware segmented identities, source envelopes, root metadata and leading content. SQL quoted include literals resolve exactly; directive-like string content never creates imports. Qualified on Windows x64 with Node26.13.0, one job, 30-second fixture bounds and zero retries. Direct controls: `lang/contracts/sql-xml-source-import-acceptance`. Original positive/negative controls and failed receipts are retained in the [source-bound qualification archive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json). Published implementation: `66e340c0c7f71ef81b61e63f87fb38ce0499a4db`; publication receipt: `dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58`. --- ## Reproduction Default config chunking with the unchanged lexical XML path: alphabeta Returns only: - a: `alpha` - b: `beta` The root start tag and **marker="PREAMBLE"** are absent from every chunk. For `beforealphabetweenbetaafter`, the leading text **before** also disappears. Both structures parse successfully. The no-child control `before` retains the entire source; adding a child creates the loss. ## Cause and downstream effect [parseXmlStructure](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/shared/xml-structure.js#L249-L263) exposes only depth-one child sections. [createXmlChunker](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/chunking/formats/xml.js#L28-L39) starts at the first child and never represents root/prefix text. The actual [token-flow consumer](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8/src/index/build/file-processor/process-chunks/token-flow.js#L559-L564) derives tokenText from text.slice(c.start,c.end), so missing bytes are unavailable to this chunk-text route. This affects real root metadata such as namespaces, project attributes and schema declarations, not just whitespace/formatting. ## Acceptance Preserve the complete original source, including XML declaration/DOCTYPE text, root attributes/namespaces and mixed text before the first child, while retaining honest lexical child/name/opening ranges. Keep declarations/entities inert, without external resolution. Test empty/self-closing roots, one/multiple children, comments/CDATA, Unicode and mixed content with full-coverage assertions. Verify marker retrieval in focused indexing coverage. ## Non-duplication All-state XML/root/chunk searches found no owner. #975/#979/#983/#1003/#1053 cover other format-specific prefix paths; the latest preamble repairs do not touch XML. #1189 is future schema/reference enrichment, not loss of admitted searchable text. ## Verification limits Pinned to live PR #572 head 13ccf301ac26b2f73a641dca59e0ddae404f12f8; affected source was re-fetched after the head advanced. Bounded authored syntax fixtures on **Node 26.12.1/Linux**. No production implementation, full index/suite or Windows acceptance. No document instructions, external entities, schemas or referenced files were executed/resolved. The actual structure parsers and chunker bodies run in the supported default non-native config path; optional native config chunking and end-to-end retrieval were not executed.

issue.title: [P2] Reject empty offsets sidecars for nonempty JSONL artifacts
issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Completed — 2026-10-29

Exported artifact row loading detects same-size restored-mtime edits, fresh-call changes and count/truncation mismatches with cancellation/close and empty-pair controls.

Qualified on Windows x64 with Node26.13.0, one job, 30-second fixture bounds and zero retries. Direct controls: `shared/artifact-io/offsets-loader-proof-lifetime`. Original positive/negative controls and failed receipts are retained in the [source-bound qualification archive](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json). Published implementation: `66e340c0c7f71ef81b61e63f87fb38ce0499a4db`; publication receipt: `dab0468e3d5882d534c02656e019e5a99bf5ed58`.
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Concrete validation gap

At PR #572 head `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`, [validateOffsetsAgainstSources](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/artifact-io/offsets.js#L549-L600) computes the offset count, then performs every source/boundary check inside `for (first = 0; first < count; ...)`. If the sidecar is zero bytes, count is zero and the function returns true even when the JSONL file contains records or arbitrary nonempty data. Alignment alone accepts zero bytes.

The corresponding [row reader](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/artifact-io/offsets.js#L332-L349) treats every requested index as out of range when offsetCount is zero. The pair can therefore pass this validator yet look empty to random access. A real writer emits one offset for every row ([writeJsonlItems](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/src/shared/json-stream/jsonl-write.js#L32-L52)), so zero offsets with nonempty data is not a valid writer-produced empty artifact.

The focused [windowed validation test](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/shared/artifact-io/offsets-validation-windowed.test.js) covers both files empty, misalignment, seams, corruption, short reads and cancellation, but not the asymmetric-empty pair. Other schema/count/checksum gates may independently reject a specific artifact; this report does not claim every end-to-end loader bypasses those gates. It is a precise shared validator contract defect.

## Required behavior
- Define the paired-empty invariant: zero offsets is valid only for a zero-byte JSONL payload under this format; a nonempty offset sidecar with an empty payload remains invalid. Reject with the established offsets error type before allocating/reading row buffers.
- Keep completeness distinct from boundary validation. If a higher-level manifest declares row count, require its count to reconcile with sidecar cardinality in its existing owner. Do not claim this two-line empty check proves all rows were indexed, nor introduce an unconditional second whole-file scan merely to address it.
- Preserve the bounded 64-KiB scratch/window algorithm, trailing-newline rules, typed corruption errors, and opened-descriptor lifetime.

## Acceptance
Use four tiny pairs: empty/empty succeeds, nonempty JSONL/empty offsets fails, empty JSONL/nonempty offsets fails, and one valid row/one zero offset succeeds. Include a sidecar truncated to zero after a valid write and ensure the exported low-level validator and verified row-reader validation agree. The generic streaming loader must not reuse earlier path-only success (the separate path-only proof-lifetime issue owns that behavior). Assert independent sequential record count cannot be reported as zero from the invalid pair, preserve cancellation/close assertions, and keep existing positive windowed tests.

Source-only audit with no executed fixture, production indexing, or implementation. All-state offsets-empty/validation searches reviewed; existing windowed validation and short-read work remains credited.

comments.body:
## Source-confirmed interaction between completed repairs
Audit pin: `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`, branch `codex/pr557-audit-repairs-20261012`. This is a static producer/consumer trace, not an executed test.

The repairs for #1571/#1572 correctly removed process-global path proof and reject a manifest-count mismatch on ordinary primary reads. #1741 correctly distinguishes canonical artifact paths from physical `.bak` paths. The row-stream consumer does not use that distinction when selecting its count authority, so recovery bypasses the newer cardinality gate.

## Exact evidence
1. [`resolveRequiredSources`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-source-resolution.js#L217-L235) returns `canonicalPaths: paths` and `paths: resolvedPaths`; `resolvedPaths` can name `.bak` files chosen by [`resolveReadableArtifactPathState`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-source-resolution.js#L64-L84).
2. [`streamArrayArtifactRowsFromSources`, lines 67–70](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-row-stream.js#L58-L70) builds `expectedCounts` from **`sources.paths`**, converts each physical filename to a relative path, and looks up exact `piece.path === relative`. For manifest `rows.jsonl` recovered from `rows.jsonl.bak`, this cannot find the manifest entry and produces null.
3. [`streamJsonlRowsFromSources`, lines 123–128](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-array-payload.js#L123-L128) forwards that null to offset validation.
4. [`validateOffsetsAgainstSources`, lines 587–598](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/offsets.js#L587-L598) checks cardinality only if `expectedCount != null`. Its remaining bounded checks verify offset alignment/monotonicity/newline boundaries, not that every JSONL row has an offset.
5. The existing [production-loader fixture, lines 66–68](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tests/shared/artifact-io/offsets-loader-proof-lifetime.test.js#L66-L68) already demonstrates why the manifest count is necessary: a one-entry `[0]` table for two rows is otherwise boundary-valid. It covers the primary filename, not recovery spelling.

## Bounded counterexample
Extend the existing fixture's exact valid `sample` manifest: canonical `rows.jsonl`, count 2, canonical metadata selecting `rows.offsets.bin`. Put its two valid newline-terminated JSONL rows only in `rows.jsonl.bak` and keep the offset sidecar as a single uint64 zero.

Call exported `loadJsonArrayArtifactRows(root, 'sample', { manifest, strict: true })`. Source control flow predicts:
- recovery selects the backup data file;
- count lookup searches `rows.jsonl.bak`, finds no manifest piece, and passes null;
- the one offset starts at zero, is in range, and the payload ends in newline, so boundary validation succeeds;
- sequential streaming still yields both rows, falsely admitting the declared random-access table.

This is **not** a claim that sequential decoding loses those rows. The incorrect admitted offsets table cannot address the second record and should have failed the same cardinality contract as the primary representation. Independent full-manifest checksum validation may reject some separately configured calls; it does not repair this exported loader's missing count binding, and the existing fixture deliberately exercises that loader with a valid supported manifest.

## Repair instructions
- Select count/provenance by each source's canonical manifest path, using `sources.canonicalPaths` rather than recovering authority from a physical path. Better, carry an admitted per-source descriptor containing canonical identity, physical read target, sidecars and expected count so new consumers cannot accidentally reconstruct authority from `.bak`/compression suffixes.
- Preserve exact path identity and existing canonical shard-gap/containment checks. Do not strip `.bak` heuristically from arbitrary user filenames, and do not weaken missing-source checks.
- Preserve invocation-local validation, bounded scratch windows, abort propagation and descriptor settlement. No extra full-data scan is needed for this repair.
- Keep legitimate legacy cases without declared counts distinct; do not silently turn a failed exact mapping of a declared canonical source into optional count evidence.

## Acceptance
Run the existing offset-proof-lifetime owner with primary data, backup-only data, backup-only sidecar, and both backed up. For each, healthy two-row/two-offset pairs succeed; nonempty one-offset truncation fails with the established offsets error before yielding rows. Include multiple parts with different counts to catch index misalignment, valid canonical filenames that themselves contain `.bak`, and cancellation/close accounting. Retain empty-pair and same-size/restored-mtime controls.

## Relationship
Cross-link #1741 (canonical versus physical paths) and #1571/#1572 (offset validation proof/cardinality), crediting their existing fixes. This is the remaining consumer binding at their intersection, not a repeat of the old global Set or zero-byte-sidecar defect.

Deduplication checked at audit time: all-state `offsets backup` search returned #1741 and two unrelated research/test-reduction issues; no separate current owner for the physical-path expected-count bypass was found.

## Dedicated file-metadata consumer: the same accepted count contract

The same count-authority obligation is also omitted by the dedicated file-metadata stream on **primary** paths. [src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-file-meta.js:89–98](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-file-meta.js#L89-L98) calls `streamJsonlRowsFromSources` with paths/offsets and a rowMapper but no expectedCounts. The shared function therefore passes undefined at `core-array-payload.js:127`; offsets592 only checks count when non-null. A manifested two-row file_meta shard with valid `{id,file}` rows and a one-entry `[0]` offsets sidecar passes the file row mapper and boundary validation. This does not depend on backup recovery and does not claim sequential row loss. It is a missing sibling caller of the same canonical per-piece count contract, not another offset algorithm bug.

#1572 explicitly requires declared manifest cardinality reconciliation in its higher-level owner while distinguishing that from the repaired empty-sidecar guard. Extend the implementation and acceptance to exported `loadFileMetaRows` as well as generic `loadJsonArrayArtifactRows`; healthy/truncated primary and backup pairs must agree. Do not force offsets validation into materializing readers that neither use nor certify the sidecar unless their contract explicitly requires it.
## Disposition and bounded implementation validation
The explicit original requirement in #1572 is: “If a higher-level manifest declares row count, require its count to reconcile with sidecar cardinality in its existing owner.” Its accepted follow-up reiterates that requirement. The generic recovery and dedicated file_meta routes above still omit that authority. Reopen this issue for those two concrete consumer gaps, while preserving credit for the delivered zero-sidecar, lifetime and ordinary generic-primary repairs. #1571 and #1741 remain related repaired owners, not additional reopen requests.

Do not introduce another full payload scan: pass already-admitted canonical piece counts to the existing offsets validator. Instrument piece lookups/opens/read bytes to prove the fix adds no payload pass. If a private path index is later introduced, compare O(P+S) plan construction with current repeated scans for 1/10/1,000 shards and retain plan-memory measurements; this is a hypothesis, not a measured gain. Preserve supported absent-count legacy cases, but an unsuccessful lookup for a declared canonical piece is not permission to discard its count. Keep adapters during migration; rollback cannot disable required cardinality validation.

issue.title: [P2] Stop producer execution when its last confirmed queue lease expires
issue.body:
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:start -->
### Qualified closeout — 2026-10-29

**Completed.** The per-claim controller independently expires confirmed authority while renewal/replay I/O is pending, aborts the exact producer once, retains cleanup ownership and rejects late revival. Focused controls cover transient recovery, no-write receipts, stuck I/O, clock rollback, replacement claims, malformed authority and shutdown diagnostics. Lease-loss failure accounting is repaired; no stale finalization is admitted.

Published candidate: `9f6399e9dc60f8d1c427fc145629b480eff62ccf`; implementation source `ed21c8a01`. The [durable correctness/repair receipt](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9f6399e9dc60f8d1c427fc145629b480eff62ccf/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.md) and its [source/report mappings](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/9f6399e9dc60f8d1c427fc145629b480eff62ccf/docs/archived/p2-p3-closeout-2026-10-29.json) retain original failures, focused passing observations and unchanged-source earlier controls. All eight publication checks pass, including 40/40 gate tests. Cases use 30-second bounds and zero retries. No broad final-tree or unrelated native/performance qualification is implied.
<!-- poc-issue-closeout:end -->

---

## Current-head finding

Source audit of PR #572 at `ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523`; this is a source-derived counterexample, not a claim that a runtime reproduction was executed.

The service correctly fences explicit owner/version mismatches and skips completion after a known lease loss. However, a worker can continue expensive producer work indefinitely when it can no longer confirm its lease, without ever receiving one of those explicit mismatch responses.

### Evidence and counterexample

- [queue-worker.js, lines 158–215](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/service/indexer-service/queue-worker.js#L158-L215) initializes `lastSuccessAt` from the local clock, then puts replay-state loading and heartbeat I/O in a single renewal promise. While `inFlight` is true every subsequent interval returns.
- Only `LEASE_FENCE_ERRORS` sets `claimControl.leaseLost` and aborts the job. Generic I/O/lock failures calculate the failure count and `maxRenewalGapMs`, but these values only govern logging. There is no independent confirmed-authority deadline.
- [queue.js, lines 1601–1641](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/service/queue.js#L1601-L1641) can requeue the expired running claim. A worker that is still failing or stuck in replay/renewal I/O may never receive the mismatch that cancels its old execution.
- A successful heartbeat can also be the minimum-interval no-write return at [queue.js, lines 1536–1545](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tools/service/queue.js#L1536-L1545). A receipt time alone is therefore not the persisted lease expiry.
- [worker-renewal.test.js](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/ed0b0c5420e16be9b4a0b4b19b0c06de53461523/tests/services/queue/worker-renewal.test.js) runs the renewal-loss case for 350 ms with a 1200 ms lease, checks that finalization still occurs, and does not inspect cancellation. It does not establish behavior after confirmed authority expires.

Example: claim A starts a long embedding/index job; renewal reads repeatedly fail or one renewal remains pending; the last persisted lease expires; a different worker requeues/claims B. A continues consuming resources until its work finishes or a subsequent explicit mismatch eventually arrives. Existing publication/build locks may still protect artifacts. This issue does **not** claim exactly-once delivery or prove index corruption.

## Required design

1. Put a per-claim renewal controller behind one owner, keyed by the exact claim owner/version plus execution identity. Track the actual expiry from the claim and confirmed renewal record, not merely `Date.now()` when a promise fulfills.
2. Separate renewal scheduling from a confirmed-authority deadline guard. A stuck renewal must not disable the deadline. Define the safety margin and clock assumptions explicitly; transient failures within the remaining lease may remain recoverable.
3. On deadline exhaustion, atomically mark this execution authority-lost, stop admitting producer work, and abort through the existing job signal. Preserve ownership of outstanding child/native/I/O cleanup until it actually settles. A timeout must not fabricate a successful drain.
4. Late renewal completion must not revive an abandoned execution or overwrite a replacement claim's state. Keep owner/version fencing and the existing completion-skip path. Do not complete/requeue a claim on behalf of the new owner.
5. Make the policy internally consistent: normalized renew intervals and permitted confirmation gap must fit inside the actual lease, including short custom leases and oversized interval overrides in `lease-policy.js`.
6. Expose last confirmed expiry, time since confirmation, renewal-in-flight age, cancellation reason, and cleanup-pending state in existing structured diagnostics. Avoid repetitive error floods after the deadline.

## Small independent proof plan

Use an injected clock/timer and gated fake heartbeat/producer, not a multi-minute soak.

- Transient rejection before the deadline, then a valid receipt: work stays alive and the deadline advances only to the returned expiry.
- Repeated generic rejection through expiry: the exact old signal aborts once and no new producer work starts.
- A never-settling replay read or heartbeat: the independent deadline still fires; ownership remains pending until the fake I/O is released.
- A minimum-interval no-write receipt cannot extend authority beyond its persisted expiry.
- A late successful renewal after abandonment cannot reactivate the old execution.
- Two claims for the same job ID: cancelling/retiring A cannot cancel or finalize B; existing owner/version checks still reject A.
- Verify queue retry/completion metrics distinguish lease loss from successful job completion, and bound timer/listener/renewal ownership after settlement.

## Dedupe / repair credit

This is the remaining expiry-without-response edge of closed #151 and #154, under #362's explicitly at-least-once contract. Current explicit mismatch cancellation and completion fencing are present; #606's post-claim resource-setup repair and #671's sibling settlement are also present. Do not replace those owners with a parallel lifecycle framework.

## Current source re-audit: normal closeout still has an expiry gap

At PR #572 `52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd`, commit `bb5a68187` substantially repairs the original active-producer defect: independent confirmed-expiry timing, exact owner/version receipts, short-lease interval normalization, cancellation and late-renewal fencing are present. Keep that implementation credit. The following narrower closeout path remains before treating the issue's authority/metrics acceptance as complete.

### Source-derived sequence (not an executed runtime test)

1. A valid claim begins, a renewal replay read or heartbeat is pending, and the producer returns before the last confirmed expiry.
2. [The worker enters `jobLifecycle.close()`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/indexer-service/queue-worker.js#L341-L365). [Lifecycle close runs close hooks before joining tracked pending promises](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/src/shared/lifecycle/registry.js#L159-L174). The [renewal close hook sets `stopped` and cancels both timers](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/indexer-service/claim-renewal.js#L81-L83).
3. The pending renewal now remains owned and awaited, correctly, but its drain can cross the confirmed expiry after the independent deadline timer was removed. On fulfillment, [`confirm` returns immediately for `stopped`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/indexer-service/claim-renewal.js#L58-L59); no authority-loss flag is set.
4. On ordinary closeout, [the worker checks only the retained `leaseLost` value and then calls `finalizeJobRun`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/indexer-service/queue-worker.js#L366-L382). It never calls `checkLeaseAuthority` here. The retained-cleanup **recovery** path already makes that call, which does not cover this successful ordinary drain. `syncWorkerShutdownState` can also add an await after timers have stopped.
5. [`completeJob`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/queue.js#L1341-L1364) uses [`assertLeaseOwnership`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tools/service/queue.js#L468-L493), which verifies running state, owner and version, not expiry. With the same still-running record and no reclaim yet, success can be persisted and counted after its confirmed authority expired without ever recording lease loss.

This does **not** establish that a replacement owner's record can be overwritten: the owner/version/status fences remain effective. It also does not claim producer work continued after its return. The residual is inconsistent expiry/completion classification across ordinary versus recovery closeout; the documented repair says late completion is fenced.

### Bounded completion work

Carry the confirmed-authority check through ordinary closeout before terminal/retry finalization, including any telemetry or queue-lock awaits. Define and enforce whether terminal mutation itself requires an unexpired claim inside the locked queue transition; a single pre-await check is not an atomic expiry fence. Preserve successful resource settlement and the original work outcome separately from authorization to commit queue completion. Do not replace existing owners or discard unresolved renewal I/O.

Extend the authored [confirmed-expiry fixture](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/52ba353029adb163676675078347647856d059cd/tests/services/queue/confirmed-lease-expiry.test.js) with the missing ordering: start a renewal, let producer succeed while authority remains valid, begin close (timer removed), advance the fake clock past expiry while renewal or shutdown telemetry is held, release it, and assert the defined lease-lost completion/metrics result. Existing expiry-before-producer-return tests do not cover this sequence. Include normal fast closeout, no-write late receipts and a replacement claim to retain existing fencing. No heavy suite, native job or benchmark was run for this source review.

comments.body:
## Remaining accepted contract: confirmed lease expiry can still be crossed during ordinary success closeout

**Disposition:** partial repair of existing #1586; P2, high confidence from static control flow. Credit the independent confirmed-expiry timer, cancellation of active producers, monotonic/wall-time rollback defense, and owner/version fencing. The remaining issue is the narrower ordinary success-finalization ordering already described in the issue's full discussion, not a duplicate request to implement the timer.

Pinned source: `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`.

### Source-derived counterexample
1. The producer returns success shortly before its last confirmed lease expiry. In [`queue-worker.js:325–361`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/service/indexer-service/queue-worker.js#L325-L361), ordinary completion enters `finally`, closes the job lifecycle, and awaits shutdown telemetry.
2. [`claim-renewal.js:44–83`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/service/indexer-service/claim-renewal.js#L44-L83) maintains independent expiry, but its lifecycle close hook sets `stopped` and clears the expiry timer. A later renewal confirmation is ignored when stopped. [`registry.js:159–174`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/lifecycle/registry.js#L159-L174) runs close hooks before joining tracked pending work.
3. Hold a pending renewal/cleanup or shutdown-telemetry operation until after that confirmed expiry. The timer is already canceled, so no `leaseLost` observation is introduced while draining.
4. [`queue-worker.js:367–384`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/service/indexer-service/queue-worker.js#L367-L384) checks only stored retirement/lease-loss state and then finalizes; it does not revalidate authority after drains. The recovery branch does perform a check at line242.
5. [`queue.js:468–490`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/service/queue.js#L468-L490) validates running status, owner and version, not expiry. [`completeJob:1355–1361`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/service/queue.js#L1355-L1361) therefore permits a still-running, same-owner/version record to become successful after its confirmed authority expired.

This does **not** claim an owner/version replacement can be overwritten, or that producer execution necessarily continues after return. The defect is an expired-authority success publication. No reproduction, build, benchmark or test was executed by this audit.

### Why the existing fixture does not close this ordering
[`confirmed-lease-expiry.test.js:88–116`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tests/services/queue/confirmed-lease-expiry.test.js#L88-L116) waits for abort inside the producer, then returns success and checks that finalization is forbidden. This correctly proves expiry *before producer return*. It does not exercise success first, timer retirement second, expiry during closeout third. Preserve all existing transient-renewal, stuck-renewal, rollback and owner/version controls.

### Implementation instructions and tradeoff
- Define the authoritative completion boundary explicitly. Under the existing contract, retain lease-authority checks until success is committed, not merely until producer return.
- Recheck the existing monotonic/wall expiry owner after all awaited drains and immediately before successful finalization. Do not refresh the deadline from an unconfirmed renewal or restart an allowance on teardown.
- Add an expiry check inside the canonical locked queue completion transition, alongside owner/version checks, to close the check-to-write window. Use the existing lease policy and canonical clock inputs; avoid a separate divergent expiry implementation. Decide and document failure outcome for expired authority without stealing a replacement owner's record.
- Keep original cleanup ownership until settlement even when authority is lost. An expired lease is not permission to abandon children, stop joining pending work, or release reservations early. Preserve the original typed lease-loss outcome and exact owner/version fences.
- If policy instead permits success from work completed before expiry, record an authoritative fenced completion event before retiring the lease and make that alternate contract explicit; an unfenced local return timestamp alone cannot establish publication authority.

### Acceptance / negative controls
- Actual queue-worker: success before expiry, gated lifecycle pending work crosses expiry, then release: no successful finalization.
- Repeat with gated shutdown telemetry and with renewal returning the same expiry or returning after retirement. No late extension may retroactively authorize publication.
- Actual locked `completeJob`: same owner/version but expired lease rejects; valid future lease succeeds; replaced owner/version remains protected; race expiry between precheck and lock rejects.
- Fake monotonic and wall clocks cover backward wall-clock adjustment, exact expiry equality and no accidental renewed allowance. Retain normal fast success, active producer expiry, abort, pending-renewal cleanup and transient renewal failure controls.

### Measurement plan
Use deterministic phase gates and clock advancement; record producer return, timer retirement, confirmed expiry, drain settlement and locked transition. Measure cancellation/settlement latency separately if runtime characterization is later authorized. No measured throughput or latency improvement is claimed.

### Compatibility and delivery
Retain at-least-once queue semantics, current owner/version errors and successful fast completion. Add the authority fence through the canonical lease policy rather than changing every lifecycle close hook. Coordinate worker precheck and locked mutation so old callers cannot bypass the new contract. Rollback may disable an optional diagnostic, not permit an expired claim to publish success again.

issue.title: [P2] Preserve artifact-cleanup observation failures instead of reporting inaccessible targets as absent
issue.body:
## Verified scope and existing repair credit
Source audit of `doublemover/PairOfCleats` branch `codex/pr557-audit-repairs-20261012`, pinned at `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. No tests or production workloads were run for this audit.

The fix for #1081 correctly retains failures **after removal is admitted**: `removeArtifactNow` rejects an unsuccessful removal, cleanup outcomes distinguish completed from failed actions, and the publication path can retain the original failure. Do not regress or re-report those repaired paths. A pre-admission gap remains in the same owner.

## Source evidence
- [`cleanupPathExists`, lines 13–20](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts-write/family-dispatch.js#L13-L20) catches **every** `fs.access` exception and returns `false`.
- [`removeArtifact`, lines 129–140](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts-write/family-dispatch.js#L129-L140) interprets that false as proven absence and immediately returns `{ ok: true, staged: false, targetPath }`. No action is recorded in `cleanupActions`, no failure reaches `outcomes`, and the removal helper is never called.
- [`summaryFor`, lines 38–57](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts-write/family-dispatch.js#L38-L57) consequently has no evidence from which to report the failed observation; an otherwise empty cleanup can be `not-required`.

## Deterministic counterexample
Use a genuine legacy sparse-artifact cleanup target selected by `prepareArtifactCleanup`, and make only its initial `fs.access` reject with `EACCES` or `EIO`. Leave unrelated observations and the configured removal boundary unchanged. The current implementation returns the same successful unstaged result as `ENOENT`, although it never established that the artifact was absent or removed. This follows directly from the shown branches; it is not a claim of an executed fault-injection fixture or of a universally reproducible platform permission error.

The error is not harmless logging: vector-only/format cleanup can retain stale artifacts while the receipt says no cleanup was needed. It also loses the original operational error before resource/failure ownership can examine it.

## Implementation instructions
1. Give cleanup observation a narrow three-way contract: observed present, known absence, and failed/unavailable. Only the deliberately supported absence errno(s) may return false. Do not globally change unrelated path-existence helpers.
2. Retain/propagate the original observation error through the existing storage-failure utilities. Decide explicitly whether staging an unobserved target is safe; otherwise reject preparation with structured path/phase context. Never claim `{ ok: true }` or omit the failed target from the receipt solely because observation failed.
3. Make immediate and staged cleanup follow the same policy. Preserve existing immutable-generation exclusions, actual-removal failure accounting, and independent error ownership.
4. Extend the existing `cleanup-removal-failure-receipts` owner rather than adding a competing cleanup implementation. If the serialized receipt cannot represent preparation failures, extend its contract explicitly and update corresponding schema/documentation.

## Acceptance
- Present target: normal removal and completed accounting remain correct.
- `ENOENT`: legitimate absence remains a no-op.
- `EACCES`, `EIO`, and an ownership-bearing observation failure: no false absent/success result; original error/path/phase remain inspectable; publication cannot call this a completed or not-required cleanup.
- Exercise both immediate and staged policy paths through `prepareArtifactCleanup`, not only the private helper.
- Preserve the existing failed-removal, immutable-artifact, repeated-commit, and logging-secondary-failure controls; do not increase fixture deadlines or run a full index.

## Compatibility, measurement and deduplication
#1081's actual-removal error accounting is repaired. Its original and accepted follow-up requirements concern admitted removals, so this is a new adjacent preflight-observation issue, not a request to reopen the completed removal-result repair. Fresh all-state cleanup/access and cleanup-observation searches found no exact alternative owner; #1574 owns repository cleanup exclusion, not this writer-family preflight.

Keep the public valid-present/known-absent behavior unchanged. Add structured preparation failure within the existing cleanup owner; do not replace contained-operation authority with an access check, since preflight cannot make a subsequent operation atomic. Count observations and actions in tiny fixtures to ensure no redundant filesystem probe was introduced. Any timing comparison must preserve identical selected targets/errors and report raw measurements; no speedup is claimed. Roll back optional helper extraction independently, never restore catch-all false absence.

issue.title: [P3] Sum logical payload rows for sharded symbol statistics instead of reporting the largest shard
issue.body:
## Verified scope
Static source audit at `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b` on `codex/pr557-audit-repairs-20261012`. No tests, build or indexing workload was executed for this report.

#1100's chunk-meta repair is present and should remain credited. However, the generic statistics path still repeats the old largest-shard mistake for other real sharded producers.

## Concrete producer-to-consumer evidence
- [`symbols.js` lines 280–288](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts/writers/symbols.js#L280-L288) registers **each** JSONL payload shard with `name: 'symbols'` and its local `count: result.counts[i]`.
- [`buildFamilyStats` lines 92–106](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/index/stats.js#L92-L106) selects these exact payload entries but reports `Math.max(...countCandidates)` rather than their sum.
- [`stats.js` lines 252–259](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/index/stats.js#L252-L259) uses that helper for symbols, symbol occurrences, symbol edges, graph relations, call sites and file metadata, as well as phrase/chargram families. The symbols path alone establishes the defect; other families require producer-specific cardinality checks rather than a blind global sum.
- [`stats-artifacts.js` lines 22–32](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/tools/index/stats-artifacts.js#L22-L32) already contains the repaired logical-payload sum/unknown/safe-integer policy used by chunk metadata and token postings.

## Counterexample and impact
For a valid symbols manifest containing payload shards of 2 and 3 records, the current CLI reports `modes.code.symbols.rows: 3` instead of 5. Adding metadata/offset pieces does not fix it, because `buildFamilyStats` selects the exact `symbols` name. One part remains correct, making small-fixture success insufficient.

The issue is incorrect reporting/diagnostics, not lost indexed symbols and not a demonstrated search-ranking error. A related unknown-value flaw exists in this path: `normalizeCount(null)` yields zero, whereas the repaired chunk path retains unknown/invalid counts as null.

## Implementation instructions
1. Inventory count semantics for each family consumed by `buildFamilyStats` and `buildEmbeddingStats`: distinguish disjoint shard-local counts, whole-family metadata totals, and alternative encodings. Document that distinction beside one shared aggregation owner.
2. Reuse/refactor `stats-artifacts.js` to sum admitted disjoint logical payload rows, avoid double-counting metadata/offset/alternate representations, and preserve null for missing/invalid/overflow counts. Do not simply replace every maximum with a sum—some representation metadata totals are duplicated.
3. Route symbols and other proven sharded row families through that owner. Keep per-family bytes and total physical-byte accounting separate.
4. Preserve the current chunk-meta required-payload, vector-only policy and selected-generation fixes; this repair must not revert them.

## Acceptance
- Exercise the actual symbols writer with a small shard cap that creates uneven 2+3 (or equivalent) payload parts, then run the actual `index stats --json` consumer and assert the exact total.
- Cover a single shard, empty supported family, metadata/offset auxiliaries, compression, and alternative encodings without duplication.
- Missing, null, negative, fractional and unsafe counts remain explicitly unknown/invalid rather than fabricated zeros or rounded totals.
- Add producer-backed controls for each additional migrated family, and preserve mixed-mode/root accounting.

## Deduplication
All-state repository search for `stats shards` returned #1100 and unrelated performance/reduction issues; #1100 specifically describes `chunk-meta`, whose current source is fixed. This is a residual sibling-family aggregation defect revealed while auditing that closeout. Cross-link #1100 rather than claiming its original chunk-meta counterexample persists.
## Compatibility and performance validation
Keep logical row totals distinct from total physical bytes and preserve the already-fixed required-payload checks. A shared family policy must encode disjoint local counts versus duplicated whole-family totals and alternative encodings; it must not infer meaning from a filename prefix alone. This changes incorrect diagnostics, not stored index rows or search semantics. Preserve unknown values rather than silently converting them to zero. Compare manifest traversal counts/allocations for one and many shards; no throughput gain is required or claimed. Migrate each producer-backed family separately and keep unmigrated adapters until its count semantics are established. Fresh all-state stats/symbols search also found #1101, whose totalBytes omission is a different statistic.

issue.title: [P2] Reject non-array JSON payloads instead of completing strict artifact streams as empty
issue.body:
## Scope and confidence
Source-confirmed at `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b` on `codex/pr557-audit-repairs-20261012`. No project test, build, benchmark or reproduction executed. This is a malformed-artifact semantic admission defect, not evidence that current normal writers emit malformed JSON or that every consumer is affected.

## Evidence and counterexample
- [`loadJsonArrayArtifactRows`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core.js#L55-L98) defaults `strict: true`, resolves a declared source and passes strictness to the format dispatcher.
- [`core-row-stream.js:27–32`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-row-stream.js#L27-L32) parses JSON, then executes `Array.isArray(payload) ? payload : []`. An object, null, string, number or boolean becomes successful zero-row EOF, regardless of strictness.
- The materialized sibling explicitly rejects the same shape with `ERR_ARTIFACT_INVALID` in [`core-array-payload.js:22–29`](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/core-array-payload.js#L22-L29). Columnar streaming similarly throws on invalid shape at core-row-stream.js35–43. This is a genuine divergent duplicated format-admission rule, not an intentional difference in stream materialization.
- `readJsonFile` only parses JSON syntax and applies read/size/containment policy (`json/read-json.js24–39`); it does not require an array. Strict source resolution enforces declaration/presence/containment and ambiguity, not array payload shape (`core-source-resolution.js95–161`). JSON is an explicitly supported manifest format, not an unsupported custom encoding.

Counterexample for implementation testing: construct a correctly versioned manifest declaring one JSON array artifact, with a contained primary `.json` whose bytes are `{}` (and internally consistent bytes/hash metadata if the surrounding test validates checksums). The materialized API rejects. Iterating the streaming API with strict=true reaches normal EOF and returns zero rows. Use `[]` as the legitimate empty control. This does not require bypassing path containment or checksum validation: integrity of bytes does not establish semantic array shape.

## Supported consumer consequence
The exported streaming context-pack seed path calls this loader and correctly rethrows caught strict errors (`src/context-pack/seed-resolution.js201–237`), but the loader produces no error. It returns `rowsIndexed:0, readState:'ready'` at239–243. Thus a declared malformed JSON map can still appear as a healthy empty seed inventory. Current normal chunk-UID-map writers emit JSONL; this consequence is specific to the supported JSON representation and exported streaming API, not a claim that ordinary CLI context-pack requests all take this path.

The API-contract tooling also explicitly falls back to this strict generic loader for non-JSONL symbols/call-sites (`src/integrations/tooling/api-contracts.js624–632`). Keep artifact-format validation in the shared loader rather than making every consumer rediscover the same rule.

## Implementation
1. Extract/reuse one small array-payload admission primitive for materialized and streaming JSON paths. Require Array.isArray; throw the same stable `ERR_ARTIFACT_INVALID`, artifact identity and source context on invalid shape. Do not convert failure to an empty array, optional absence or a warning-only result.
2. Preserve valid empty arrays, format selection, containment, backup policy, resource cleanup and original read errors. Do not change strict=false semantics accidentally: the existing materialized API rejects invalid array shape even in permissive mode; document and test intentional parity.
3. Avoid eagerly copying/collecting the array a second time; the shared primitive validates shape and returns the already decoded array. Keep family-specific row validation separate rather than hoisting incompatible schemas.
4. Review JSON/columnar/binary/JSONL admission as a format matrix, but do not expand this bug into an unproven claim about all required-key policies. No producer semantic version bump is needed solely to correct failure admission; if implementation changes stored row meaning, follow the shared analysis-version contract.

## Acceptance
- Table-driven exported-loader tests: `{}`, null, scalar string/number/boolean reject with exact code; valid `[]` and nonempty arrays preserve rows/order. Compare materialized and streaming APIs.
- Exercise raw and supported compressed JSON variants and missing-primary/backup routing. Keep invalid JSON syntax, oversized bytes and containment failures unchanged.
- Invoke `buildChunkUidMapSeedIndex` or exported streaming assembler using declared JSON `{}` and assert failure, not ready/unknown-UID. Valid empty-map miss remains usable. Retain #1566's JSONL missing/corrupt/later-shard controls.
- Verify early return/throw and read failure settle the existing descriptor owner. No new broad buffering or weaker byte caps.

## Dedup and repair credit
All-state exact `loadJsonArrayArtifactRows` search returned only #1566; `non-array` and JSON/stream/array searches found no separate owner of this shape mismatch. Read #1566 body and full comment. Its repaired catch/rethrow behavior and qualified JSONL controls remain credited. This is the lower-level format-specific hole that prevents that catch from observing malformed JSON; this new shared-loader issue cross-links #1566 rather than reopening its completed catch/rethrow repair. Do not reopen its already-correct blanket-catch implementation claim.

## Cold JSON consumer extension and limiting guard

[src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/chunk-meta.js:62–68](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/loaders/chunk-meta.js#L62-L68) has a second silent non-array JSON branch in `loadChunkMetaColdRows`: it yields only when Array.isArray and otherwise completes normally. Route this branch through the same array-admission primitive. However, do **not** claim every modern hot/cold index silently succeeds: representation-plan `hotColdSplit` sets `requireColdRows` at190-204, and transform235-236 rejects each hot row lacking its cold row. The silent-success consequence is limited to a supported plan-less/optional cold representation or an empty hot inventory; it remains semantic rejection drift at the reader boundary. Preserve the modern missing-required-cold guard and add both guarded and optional/legacy controls. Open #1253 (full body read) owns identity-only cold projection and expressly preserves malformed-cold/schema checks; cross-link rather than claiming projection should skip those checks.
## Migration and work validation
Reuse one shape-only guard, not a second materialization pass or full-row schema. Confirm unchanged array object/row ordering and allocation counts for valid large arrays; rejecting a non-array is constant-time admission after the existing bounded parse. Keep source/error contexts and documented permissive behavior aligned across wrappers. Roll back optional module movement independently of malformed-payload rejection. Fresh all-state stream/non-array and exact-loader searches established no closer shared-array-shape owner. Cold identity projection remains #1253; this change must not weaken its discarded-field integrity requirements.

issue.title: [P2] Admit columnar row cardinality before iterating or allocating decoded rows
issue.body:
## Verified defect and scope
Static source trace at `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`; no tests/builds/probes run. The shared JSON-columnar decoder trusts declared length without admitting its integer/range/column-extent semantics. Strict exported readers can fabricate rows, hide nonempty arrays as empty, or schedule work far beyond the encoded payload size. This is the JSON `columnar` format, not the binary-columnar framing repaired by #1740.

## Exact evidence and independent counterexamples
`src/shared/artifact-io/columnar-rows.js:1-21` accepts any object arrays container and selects any finite payload.length at7-9. It does not reject negative/fractional/unsafe lengths or reconcile column lengths. At29, absent elements become null. `iterateColumnarRows:61-70` yields while i<length. `inflateColumnarRows:43-52` instead executes new Array(length), so API semantics diverge on invalid lengths.

`loadJsonArrayArtifactRows` defaults strict=true (`loaders/core.js:55-98`); its columnar branch (`core-row-stream.js:35-42`) delegates directly without a shape/cardinality guard. Manifest source resolution verifies declared paths/format/presence, not decoded cardinality. The payload can be below maxBytes with consistent manifest checksums: byte integrity does not make its length safe.

Tiny witness: `{format:'columnar',columns:['id'],arrays:{id:[7]},length:3}` produces `{id:7},{id:null},{id:null}` rather than rejecting. Set length:-1 and the streaming branch completes empty despite one stored element; length:1.5 causes two streamed rows but materialization raises RangeError. A tiny payload with finite length:1e100 permits effectively unbounded synthetic iteration; do not actually run that loop in a fixture. The accepted length lacks a bound derived from real admitted row extents.

These are not arbitrary stricter semantics invented by the audit: `src/contracts/schemas/artifacts/core.js:79-89` and `symbols-call-sites.js:12-22` define nonnegative integer length. The real chunk-meta columnar producer (`index/build/artifacts/writers/chunk-meta/iterator.js:251-277`) pads every discovered column to the same exact row count, emits columns, and records that count. The schema alone does not reconcile vector extents; the shared decode admission should.

Dedicated file_meta readers validate every emitted row (`core-file-meta.js:62-70`), which will reject fabricated null IDs after the valid prefix. That consumer mitigates some consequences but does not repair shared admission-before-yield, negative-length empty success, or generic stream callers. `loadChunkMetaRows` uses materialization for this format and may throw RangeError earlier; do not describe every consumer as unbounded.

## Implementation
Add a single pure columnar-envelope admission owner consumed by both iterate/inflate, before allocation or first yield. Require a safe nonnegative integer length; an explicit invalid length must not silently fall back to another column. Validate unique string column names, own array-backed columns and consistent extents according to the declared format. Determine/document compatibility for omitted length/columns only where actually supported; legacy inference must derive a bounded exact length from admitted arrays. Distinguish null cells (valid padding emitted by producer) from missing column elements (malformed extent). Table-coded cells retain existing semantics; do not rewrite dictionary values or introduce unrelated semantic normalization.

Use stable typed artifact errors with family/source context at loader boundaries, not accidental RangeError or successful empty output. Reconcile manifest row count where its semantics are row-local. Keep max encoded bytes separate from decoded cardinality/work bounds. No new format or producer version is needed merely to reject malformed payload; any changed accepted encoding requires explicit compatibility/versioning.

## Acceptance
Actual exported materialized/streaming generic loaders and dedicated chunk/file loaders must agree on negative, fractional, unsafe, missing/invalid length, unequal column lengths, absent declared columns, duplicate column names, empty columns with positive length, and explicit legitimate zero-row envelopes. Use tiny shapes and assert failure before first emitted row/allocation; a huge declared length test only requests the first result and expects immediate rejection, never drains the malformed iterator.

Generate valid fixtures with the actual columnar producer, including late-added nullable columns and table-coded values, and prove row/column order and value parity unchanged. Exercise strict, documented permissive/legacy behavior, raw/compressed/backup sources, checksum-valid malformed payload, and all supported consumer routes. Preserve containment, read limits and exact cleanup observations. Report fixture execution only when implementation runs under supported bootstrap; none was run here.

## Dedup and relation
Live all-state searches `columnar length`, exact `columnar-rows` and `iterateColumnarRows` found no matching decoder-cardinality owner. Full #1253 body was read: it owns identity projection and requires existing corruption checks, not declared-length admission. #1740 owns streamed binary aggregate-byte limits; #1358 binary batched writes; #1366 representation planning. Array-shape rejection is adjacent shared-admission work, but this is a distinct columnar extent contract and requires the separate counterexamples and acceptance matrix above.


## Compatibility, complexity and rollout
An O(number of columns) envelope/extent check should precede allocation/iteration; avoid scanning every cell twice merely to establish column lengths. Retain downstream family cell/schema validation, including table-coded semantics. Measure envelope visits, emitted rows and allocations against the existing producer on small and wide valid payloads. No measured performance improvement or observed memory exhaustion is claimed. Document any supported legacy omitted-column/length inference before tightening it, and migrate that compatibility adapter explicitly; never treat a present invalid length as omitted. Roll back optional optimization independently of safe-integer and admission-before-yield fixes.

The schema proves integer/nonnegative policy, not every proposed equal-extent or uniqueness rule; those details need explicit compatibility decisions, grounded in the actual producer's equal-length padding. Fresh all-state columnar/length search found binary framing/performance and representation-planning owners but no JSON-columnar cardinality owner.

Pinned review anchors: [src/shared/artifact-io/columnar-rows.js:1–70](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/artifact-io/columnar-rows.js#L1-L70); [src/contracts/schemas/artifacts/core.js:79–89](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/contracts/schemas/artifacts/core.js#L79-L89); [src/index/build/artifacts/writers/chunk-meta/iterator.js:251–277](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts/writers/chunk-meta/iterator.js#L251-L277).

issue.title: [P2] Drain original manifest checksum readers before cancellation releases publication ownership
issue.body:
# [P2] Drain original manifest checksum readers before cancellation releases publication ownership

Pin `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. Source/dependency-derived supported-caller defect; no tests, hashing workloads, builds or project execution. Exact locked `p-queue@10.0.0` official registry artifact was verified against package-lock SHA512; only implementation/readme source inspected, with integrity provenance retained. Not a claim this was introduced by the version upgrade.

## Delivered repairs retained
The manifest writer rejects escaped paths, snapshots its request, verifies sealed size, reuses valid sealed checksums and hashes through the original contained descriptor. `withFileLock` already retains resource prerequisites present on its worker outcome. `runWithSettledConcurrency` already exists and is used by stage-output and artifact-publication. Those are correct owners; the manifest's remaining queue composition does not consume the settled-work helper.

## Exact composition failure
1. `src/index/build/artifacts/checksums.js:110–121` snapshots inputs and runs `writePiecesManifestLocked` under the canonical index-state publication lock (or borrowed initial-publication capability).
2. The action uses `runWithConcurrency(..., {signal: effectiveAbortSignal})` at31–90. A piece without a sealed checksum, or index_state.json, calls `checksumFileObservation`64. `src/shared/hash.js:34–72` owns the actual contained descriptor, awaits original read51 and original close via `withContainedFile`.
3. `src/shared/concurrency/run-with-queue.js:442–444` makes a private PQueue. It passes the same abort signal to `queue.add`309–315 and tracks only that public task promise326–345. Its own pending drain also races the signal348–410.
4. Locked p-queue implementation `index.js:500–510` races abort against the running callback. Its finally531–540 removes logical task state and schedules `#next`;265–270 decrements pending. `onIdle`776–781 observes that logical pending count, not the original callback. The dependency's own pending-zero documentation786 explicitly distinguishes aborted tasks from still-running functions. This is intended dependency behavior, not a library bug.
5. Abort while the original checksum read or close is outstanding can therefore reject the manifest action with a plain cancellation before that checksum callback finishes. `src/shared/index-state-publication.js:61–78` passes the action outcome through `withFileLock`; `src/shared/locks/file-lock.js:275–295` observes only that outcome and supplies it to releaseFileLockOrThrow. The early cancellation does not carry the later reader's original ownership prerequisite.
6. If the original close subsequently rejects, `contained-file-resource.js:229–233` correctly generates a pending-owner failure and retains the original session in its global ledger101–115. The detached checksum callback receives that failure, but the already-rejected queue race cannot return it through the publication action. Original low-level handle retention is credited; **the enclosing lock/caller loses the prerequisite and recovery evidence**, rather than a claim the low-level ledger immediately discards the descriptor.

A deterministic witness is an admitted manifest piece whose checksum descriptor read/close is held, followed by request abort. The manifest call can reject and its lock can retire before that original read/close settles. Releasing the original read into a failed close then proves the pending session cannot reach the earlier public failure. No malicious caller or concurrent arbitrary source mutation is needed.

## Impact boundaries
- No claim that an aborted manifest is published, that checksum bytes are wrong, or that artifact corruption has been observed. The awaited queue rejects before manifest write91.
- This is the publication-owner retirement/original-failure evidence boundary. A subsequent cooperating action may acquire the same publication lock while the original reader remains outstanding; do not inflate that into a demonstrated overlapping writer corruption scenario.
- Process-files has a separate original process-file drain registry, and stage-output already uses settled concurrency. Do not label every runWithQueue caller broken.
- Merely adding `queue.onIdle()` is insufficient for this exact dependency's aborted running callback behavior. `Promise.allSettled` over the same raced task promises is also insufficient.

## Repair shape
Use the existing `runWithSettledConcurrency` (or equivalent original-callback owner) for this manifest checksum interval, explicitly setting `collectResults: true` so the sorted normalized piece list is preserved (that helper defaults to false). Pass cancellation to the actual checksum operation, stop admitting additional pieces after cancellation/failure, drain every started callback and preserve all original failure observations before returning the action outcome. Do not forward a cancellation race into the queue as a substitute for draining the original operation.

Preserve first cancellation/operational cause separately from secondary close failures, including falsey/frozen values, and let the existing lock release owner see pending original resource observations. A retained failed close must keep the lock/session recovery contract; a delayed but successful close may release normally. Keep path containment, sealed receipt verification and checksum reuse unchanged. No global change to runWithQueue's prompt-cancellation contract is necessary; classify ownership-bearing consumers and migrate deliberately.

## Acceptance
- Actual writePiecesManifest → actual concurrency owner → original descriptor: hold read, abort, verify no manifest write and no publication completion/lock retirement before the original callback settles.
- Hold close instead of read; abort; original close rejects with pending capability. Public failure retains exact session and pending observer; same-root cooperating publication stays fenced until explicit original-owner recovery.
- Several started checksum siblings: one failure/cancellation, no new pieces admitted, all started readers drain, every pending close observation retained without replacing the primary.
- Pre-aborted and queued-only controls open no descriptor; normal completion and delayed-successful-close controls release once; reused sealed checksum still avoids unnecessary reads; explicit index_state checksum path remains verified.
- Exercise ordinary withIndexStatePublicationLock and borrowed initial-publication context. Keep stage-output's settled-work controls and process-files' independent original-drain tests as negative controls.
- Measure cancellation-to-reader-settlement and retained descriptors/lock ownership separately. No benchmark claim from this audit.

## Exact publication and ownership anchors
- [src/index/build/artifacts/checksums.js:31–121](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/artifacts/checksums.js#L31-L121)
- [src/shared/hash.js:34–72](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/hash.js#L34-L72)
- [src/shared/concurrency/run-with-queue.js:309–410](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/concurrency/run-with-queue.js#L309-L410)
- [src/shared/index-state-publication.js:61–78](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/index-state-publication.js#L61-L78)
- [src/shared/locks/file-lock.js:275–295](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/locks/file-lock.js#L275-L295)
- [src/shared/contained-file-resource.js:101–115](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/contained-file-resource.js#L101-L115)
- [src/shared/contained-file-resource.js:229–233](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/shared/contained-file-resource.js#L229-L233)

## Compatibility, deduplication and delivery
The generic `runWithQueue` prompt-cancellation contract is deliberate: `run-with-queue-abort-inflight-hang.test.js` expects return while its original callback remains pending. Preserve it. `run-with-queue-error-ownership.test.js` covers a delivered callback failure, not an earlier cancellation race hiding a later failed close. Migrate the manifest owner only, using settled concurrency with `collectResults: true`; retain sorted piece order, sealed-hash reuse, manifest schema and both lock-entry variants.

Live all-state searches for writePiecesManifest, checksum/cancel and manifest ownership found no equivalent focused owner. #245 owns immutable transactional generation publication; its body and completion comment do not establish this queue-adapter cancellation boundary. #671's service batch sibling join is repaired and is a useful structured-lifetime precedent, not the same caller. #918 containment, #1110 checksum validation, #1234 sealed-hash reuse and #1547 served-manifest identity remain distinct. This is a focused new issue linked to #245/#671, not grounds to reopen those completed contracts.

First add deterministic original-read/close phase gates at the public manifest entrypoint, then change only this concurrency interval. Retain cancellation latency as a distinct measurement from original settlement latency. If delayed native/descriptor close cannot be bounded, keep the existing pending-resource recovery capability and publication fence rather than inventing successful drain. Rollback may retain a conservative serial settled implementation; it must not restore early publication-owner retirement. No new queue dependency, hashing algorithm or durable schema is required.

Dependency evidence: [exact p-queue 10.0.0 package](https://registry.npmjs.org/p-queue/-/p-queue-10.0.0.tgz), verified against package-lock SHA512; [documented queue semantics](https://github.com/sindresorhus/p-queue). Source inspection is high-confidence for the ordering; no overlap duration, leak magnitude or artifact corruption was measured.
