issue.title: [P2] Keep escaped triple-string content out of Python import pre-scan
issue.body:
### Concrete remaining boundary

[stripPythonStringsAndComments](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/lang/python/imports.js#L73-L99) skips escaped characters in single/double strings, but the triple-string branches89–99 unconditionally recognize the next triple quote. `collectPythonImportState` invokes that sanitizer before logical statement collection at115–150.

```python
text = """prefix \"""
import phantom
"""
import actual
```

The first apparent triple terminator begins with an escaped quote and remains string content. The scanner instead closes early, exposes `import phantom` as a standalone import statement and consumes the actual closing delimiter as a new triple string, hiding `import actual`. Python's [lexical specification](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#string-and-bytes-literals) explicitly distinguishes escaped quotation from unescaped triple termination.

The current #1736 tests correctly verify accumulated multiline parenthesis depth, blank continuation, LF/CRLF and persisted import identities. They do not exercise this separate sanitizer boundary; retain their repair credit.

### Implementation guidance and acceptance

Use a single bounded string-state owner for import sanitization with correct escape parity and raw/prefixed-string handling; preserve newlines and UTF-16 source coordinates. Reuse parser-owned evidence where already available, without requiring an extra heavyweight parse for the lightweight pre-scan. Never infer executable imports from literal content. Preserve explicit incomplete state on unsupported syntax and retire older import-analysis fingerprints.

Test both quote styles, odd/even backslashes, raw-string quote boundaries, prefixed literals, fake imports inside followed by real imports outside, comments, same-line semicolons, LF/CRLF and Unicode. Assert exact module+usage pairs through actual registered collection/import scan and bundle replay; old sanitized false positives cannot be accepted from cache. Small deterministic fixtures suffice; no broad suite needed for the core defect.

### Non-duplication

All-state Python/import/string search includes #1736 (logical statement continuation) and #656 (registry AST argument handoff), neither title/body source cause is escaped triple termination. Triple/escape search finds no Python-specific owner. The Starlark defect above has the same lexical mistake but a different producer and syntax contract; coordinate shared primitive work without merging language-specific acceptance into an unbounded umbrella.



### Actual producer boundary, receipt and migration
[src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js:635–638](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js#L635-L638) installs this collector; [src/index/build/imports.js:759–786](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/imports.js#L759-L786) uses it in the fresh graph pre-scan. The separately repaired AST relation route does not restore entries already lost here. Preserve the legacy collector’s explicit partial receipt: this issue does not allege a complete-parser claim. Retire the affected import-analysis fingerprint, but do not globally discard unrelated language caches. A rollback may select an earlier qualified scanner while continuing to reject entries produced by the defective identity. Measure source bytes examined, scanner CPU/allocation and cold/warm replay on identical exact import sets; no speedup is asserted.

issue.title: [P2] Preserve Python Unicode module names and aliases in import pre-scan
issue.body:
Source-proven semantic omission, linked to #656 and #1736 without reopening their repaired causes. Pin `24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b`. Static audit only; examples were reasoned from source, not executed.

## Evidence and consumer
- `src/lang/python/imports.js:11–20` accepts module strings only through ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*` or ASCII relative-module regex. `normalizeUsage:23–26` has the same restriction for imported names/aliases. The from-statement regex at175 rejects non-ASCII module names before normalization.
- `src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js:635–638` installs this as Python's collectImportEntries. Actual import graph scan `src/index/build/imports.js:759–786` selects the registered collector for Python; registry122–135 invokes it and normalizes its result. It does not obtain Python AST imports for this source pre-scan. The shared `src/index/shared/import-specifier.js:15–44` preserves Unicode, but cannot restore entries discarded upstream.
- Separate AST relations correctly consume `pythonAst.imports` (`src/lang/python/relations.js:15–24`) and native AST visitor `ast-script.js:506–521` retains Python-parsed names. The repaired #656 argument handoff remains valid. This bug affects the lightweight graph/import producer and no-AST relation fallback, not every Python semantic channel.

Valid examples:

```python
import café
from 包 import 模块
from .包 import 模块 as 别名
```

Current pre-scan yields no import entries for these module names. With an ASCII module, e.g. `from pkg import 模块 as 别名`, it retains pkg but loses both usage names. Python supports non-ASCII identifiers and applies NFKC normalization during parsing; language identity must not be reduced to ASCII or replaced with generic path normalization. [Official Python lexical specification](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#names).

## Implementation instructions
1. Give the Python lexical owner a version-qualified identifier/dotted-module recognizer. Support relative leading dots separately from identifier segments. Retain original spelling/source spans, and represent Python-normalized semantic names separately when needed. Do not simply allow every non-ASCII character: emoji, invalid combining starts and separators remain invalid identifiers.
2. Reuse an already prepared CPython token/AST product where actually available. For the lightweight pre-scan, avoid spawning a second interpreter merely to decide each name; a small explicit language-qualified validator is acceptable if its Unicode-version boundary and unsupported state are honest. Node Unicode properties are not automatically identical to the selected Python release's XID rules.
3. Keep keywords, dotted-name separators, aliases, relative import levels, string/comment exclusion, logical continuations and source coordinates under the Python producer. No evaluation/importing of modules. Do not normalize Unicode filenames globally or merge raw and normalized provenance silently.
4. Preserve existing typed import extraction/omission receipt and source/version invalidation. Bump the appropriate Python import-analysis producer version so old empty scan results cannot be reused. Do not mark a declined syntax family complete-empty.

## Acceptance
Actual collectLanguageImportEntries and normal scanImports consumption, not only helper outputs. Include the examples above, dotted Unicode package segments, ASCII module with Unicode imported member/alias, NFKC-equivalent identifier forms with explicit expected Python semantic spelling, relative levels, combining continuations, invalid characters, quoted/commented lookalikes and unchanged ASCII/continuation cases. Compare prepared AST route versus lexical import route for supported names, but use independently stated expected module/usage sets. Verify local Unicode module resolution where supported and exact persisted/import-cache replay after producer-version change. If a platform cannot create an equivalent filename, separate lexical semantics from filesystem qualification rather than discarding the language evidence.

The existing `tests/lang/python/registry-relations.test.js:7–25` proves #656 with ASCII names and no-AST controls; #1736's continuation matrix likewise does not establish Unicode name acceptance. Preserve those controls.

## Dedup and limits
Live all-state searches for Python/Unicode/import, Python/identifier and normalizeSpecifier found no focused matching owner. Full #656 body and its single comment were read: exact cause was AST passed in wrong argument position, now repaired. Full #1736 source/history identifies delimiter-depth and blank-continuation boundaries, not identifier classes. The escaped triple-string issue identified separately is a separate lexical-state defect; coordinate canonical Python scan work but keep independent regressions and dispositions. 

Performance plan: bounded mixed ASCII/Unicode source corpus, compare lexical scan CPU/allocations and exact import output with warm/cold incremental replay. No dependency installation, runtime execution, benchmark, measured missing-edge count or throughput claim was made here.

### Exact source anchors
[src/lang/python/imports.js:11–26](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/lang/python/imports.js#L11-L26); [src/lang/python/imports.js:115–190](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/lang/python/imports.js#L115-L190); [src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js:635–638](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/language-registry/registry-data.js#L635-L638); [src/index/language-registry/registry.js:122–135](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/language-registry/registry.js#L122-L135); [src/index/build/imports.js:759–786](https://github.com/doublemover/PairOfCleats/blob/24230d7960127ab7e4a01f2c040bf3d859f6b46b/src/index/build/imports.js#L759-L786).

Final all-state dedup and current #656/#1736 bodies/comments were reviewed on 2026-10-30. Neither repaired cause covers this syntax boundary. Keep the Unicode identifier, inline-suite admission and escaped-string regressions independently attributable even if implementation shares one Python lexical owner. Preserve the existing partial extraction receipt; no claim of complete Python binding is added. Rollback must not reactivate stale import-analysis identities.
